`CHANGELOG.md`:

```md
# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [1.8.0] - 2026-11-21

### Changed (Python)
- `dexfile-cli` pin bumped v0.1.6 → v0.1.9 (sha256 `02de8abb…`): v0.1.7 was a docs release (advertised the `outline` subcommand); v0.1.8 added `validate` + `merge`; v0.1.9 fixes two real bugs found while verifying them — `merge --allow-cdex` ignored the flag and wrote DEX039 instead of CDEX001, and `validate` flagged inherited references whose hierarchy left the dex (78 false `unresolved_method` errors on a real 1,354-class app). v0.1.9 also makes truncation accounting exact (`issues_total`), counts non-determinable references as `references_unknown`, and turns 64K write failures into actionable usage errors naming the section. Verified live: spacepeng.apk validates clean (12,076 methods, 129 unknown refs), an 18,068-class dex validates clean in ~5s, and cdex merge reads back as CDEX001.

### Added (Python, deferred-dex batch — validate + merge + cdex opt-in, catalog 87 → 89)
- The three deferred dexfile-cli items from the integration review, now implemented:
  - **`dex_validate`** — dex-level diagnostics, the analog of smali_diagnostics, from DexFile's ClassPath/analysis package over a self-contained classpath (framework classes are outside it and honestly not flagged): duplicate classes, super-is-interface, member-reference resolution errors (NO_SUCH_METHOD/FIELD, ILLEGAL_ACCESS, INCOMPATIBLE_CLASS_CHANGE), per-method analysis failures; `max_issues` caps the list with an honest truncation flag. Backed by the new dexfile-cli `validate` subcommand.
  - **`dex_merge`** — the reverse of `dex_split`: class lists from multiple dexes concatenated into one, class-collision detection across inputs, era-consistent target; `allow_cdex` opts in to standalone cdex output (not PathClassLoader-loadable on-device). Backed by the new dexfile-cli `merge` subcommand.
  - **cdex write opt-in** — `dex_convert` accepts `target_version=cdex001` only with `allow_unloadable=true`; the schema description and result note carry the loading caveat. The CLI has supported cdex write since v0.1.3.
- dexfile-cli bumped to **v0.1.9** (sha256 `02de8abb…`): `validate` + `merge` subcommands, with the exact-classpath and cdex-target fixes.
- 11 new tests (`tests/test_dex_tools.py`): validate-clean, inherited-ref unknown, super-is-interface + truncation, honest missing-file, merge two/duplicate/needs-two, cdex merge, cdex opt-in refusal/success, schema truthfulness; suite now 233 passed + 2 skipped.

### Docs
- README: tool counts (89), DEX surgery grows to (11), dexfile-cli 0.1.9 pin; `dex_validate`/`dex_merge` rows carry the `references_unknown`, truncation and 64K caveats.
- PyPI package README refreshed (it predated the DEX tools): 89-tool overview, DEX surgery/`dex_validate`/`dex_merge`, dexfile-cli in the `--setup` list, and the new fast-loop prompts.

## [1.7.0] - 2026-11-20

### Changed (Python)
- `dex_convert`'s default target is now cdex-aware: legacy-ART inputs (bare `cdex` or a `vdex` wrapper) default to **037** — dex037 was introduced in API 24 and covers the cdex (API 28) era with room to spare; the reason it beats 035 for cdex content is verification semantics, not opcodes (cdex records no source dex version, just a one-bit flags field: 0 = source DEX035, 1 = later — and 035 forbids default methods in interfaces and skips topological class ordering, while 037+ requires super-before-sub). Flat dex keeps the 035 default (maximum reader compatibility for jadx), and an explicit `target_version` always wins. The result's `note` names the defaulted target when it fires; the CLI-side counterpart landed in dexfile-cli (patch rewrites cdex to 037 from v0.1.3 on). Hermetic test for all four default paths in `tests/test_dex_tools.py`.
- `dexfile-cli` pin bumped v0.1.3 → v0.1.4 (sha256 `14d5c007…`): the jar's read plumbing was fixed after testing against real-world artifacts (a 19 MB Android-12 boot vdex — three embedded cdex parts, 13,754 framework classes — and real HTC Sooner M3/M5 dexes). `dex_info` now actually reads modern-era vdex parts, dey odex wrappers and the legacy dex009/dex013 files instead of reporting them unreadable; the two blockers were CLI calling bugs (a stale `art` flag behind `withTargetApi`, and the magic-scan passing the magic offset as `header_offset` instead of `data_offset`), not library gaps.
- `dexfile-cli` pin bumped v0.1.4 → v0.1.5 (sha256 `c5482979…`): era facts corrected with the DexFile author's guidance — dex037 is API 24 (not 26); the m-prefixed 009/013 instructions are the standard *legacy* set (not odex) and the jar now runs the library's `LegacyRewriter` before any write from a 009/013 source; odex instructions are enabled on every read and write (the runtime accepts them in any dex version it supports). Consequences, all verified against the real-world corpus: flat dex009/dex013 convert to 037 (baksmali decompiles every class); dey odex wrappers convert with `--to 035` (their dalvik-era odex encodes only at api ≤ 13) and refuse 037 with era-aware advice; the 19 MB Android-12 boot vdex converts to 037 (154,424 odex instructions written verbatim) — convert/patch report an `odex_instructions` count plus a note whenever odex content is written.

### Added (Python)
- The MT-MCP adoption plan (`~/jadx-emu/protected_apks/test_apks/mt_mcp/mt-mcp-android-re-implementation-plan.md`): 13 of MT Manager's MCP tools adopted where android-re-mcp provably had gaps, everything else skipped as redundant. Conventions adopted from MT: `expected_*` guards on byte-level ops, per-op results, optional `expected_sha256` concurrency guard.
- **APK/zip surgery & checks (8)** in the new `handlers/apkops.py` (`ApkOpsHandler`): `apk_read_signature` (apksigner scheme matrix + openssl cert details; unsigned → ok/verifies:false), `zip_test` (CRC-every-entry audit, duplicate names, method histogram, encrypted/bad entries, trailing bytes, STORE-dex smell), `zip_extract` (explicit entry→dest, zip-slip refused, per-entry results), `zip_update` (generalizes `dex_swap`: add/replace/patch-with-expected_hex/rename/delete; META-INF guards; `expected_sha256`; untouched entries byte-identical via original ZipInfo reuse), `apk_build_check` (pre-build linting: manifest, aapt2 resource-compile, dexfile-cli dex sanity, duplicate/pending-edit `.bak` scan; blockers with codes + fix hints), `resource_table_list` (aapt2 dump resources → packages/types/entries), `resource_read` (ids or type/name → per-config values, `@ref` chains), `resource_xref` (hex grep across an apktool decompile).
- **Native ELF patching (3)** in `handlers/sosec.py`: `native_map_address` (VA↔file-offset via PT_LOAD, both directions, exec status), `native_patch_string` (zero-padded, `expected_text` guarded, all occurrences, `.bak` first), `native_patch_instructions` (keystone assembly, `expected_hex` guarded, arch-correct NOP padding — arm64/arm/x86/x64; keystone-engine joins the `[native]` extra).
- **DEX reads (2)** in `handlers/dex.py`: `dex_read_class_outline` (per-class outline via the new dexfile-cli `outline` subcommand — released as dexfile-cli v0.1.6, pin bumped; every classes*.dex searched when given an APK), `dex_read_pseudocode` (jadx `--single-class` incremental cache, line paging, brace-matched `method` slices; smali fallback hinted on jadx failure).
- `dexfile-cli` pin bumped v0.1.5 → v0.1.6 (sha256 `11d8f215…`): new `outline` subcommand — per-class dex-model outline (super, interfaces, formatted access flags, fields, methods with descriptors and register counts) without decompiling; serves `dex_read_class_outline`.
- androguard 4.x logs through **loguru** — stdlib levels never silence it; the resource tools mute it via `loguru.disable("androguard")` inside their calls.
- 30 new tests (`tests/test_mt_adopt.py`): hermetic zip/signature/native-map/patcher/build-check coverage + androguard/jadx/dexfile-cli-gated live runs; suite now 223 passed + 1 skipped.

### Docs
- README: tool counts (87), "APK/zip surgery & checks (8)", "Native ELF patching (2)", DEX surgery grows to (9), new first-session prompts, dexfile-cli 0.1.6 pin.
- `frida_scripts/build_bundles.sh` no longer falls back to a hardcoded personal path when `frida-compile` is absent — it exits with an install hint instead (only script with a non-portable default in the shipped wheel; every other path literal is a device convention or a multi-path search with honest degradation).
## [1.6.0] - 2026-11-17

### Changed (Python)
- `apk_decompile_java` degrades to apktool when jadx is unavailable instead of returning `missing_tool`: the call still succeeds, with `engine: "apktool (jadx unavailable)"`, `fallback: true` and a note that `out_dir` holds smali + resources, not Java source (5 new tests, `tests/test_decompile_fallback.py`). jadx present-but-broken is still an honest error — no silent engine swap on real failures.
- Review-doc hygiene pass (D-2, D-3): `check_tools` dropped the never-invoked probes (`binwalk`, `apk-mitm`, `frida-compile`, `frida-ps`) and the redundant `frida-tools`-module / `mitmproxy`-binary / `mitmproxy`-module probes; the dead legacy `scripts/android-api-extractor/analyze_apk.py` is deleted. CI pins bumped (checkout@v7, setup-python@v7, upload-artifact@v7, download-artifact@v8) — clears the Node-20 deprecation annotations from the publish runs.

### Added (Python)
- DEX surgery via DexFile (E-PY-17): seven `dex_*` tools over the new pinned [`dexfile-cli`](https://github.com/FlyPhantomFly/dexfile-cli) jar (v0.1.2, MIT — redistribution of DexFile/Smali/AndroidMisc) — `dex_info`, `dex_extract`, `dex_convert` (old-ART vdex/cdex → 035; 035 → 041 containers), `dex_patch` (const-string/rename/retarget-invoke/flip-flags/replace-method-body, `.bak` discipline, per-op matched counts), `dex_assemble`, `dex_split` (64K balancing) and `dex_swap` (pure-Python zip swap closing the no-rebuild fast loop: `dex_extract → dex_patch → dex_swap → apk_sign`). The jar is a pinned `--setup` download; `check_tools` gains its probe. Phase-0 spike findings recorded in the review doc (vdex027+ carries no embedded dex; cdex round-trip proven; baksmali reads 041 containers fine). A review pass after landing fixed three CLI issues (container-input honesty, integer-flag validation, 10× magic-scan) and three handler issues (stored-entry compression preserved in the zip swap — resources.arsc; dex-entry-only matching; mkstemp fd leak), released as dexfile-cli v0.1.1→v0.1.2. 13 dex tests; catalog 67 → 74 tools.


## [1.5.0] - 2026-11-16

### Added (Python)
- `android_api_extractor` gains the E-NPM-5 const-string harvest (commit `8cd2023`): every `const-string`/`const-string/jumbo` literal starting with `http://`/`https://` is deduplicated (across files) and host-grouped via `urlsplit`, returned as a `const_string_urls` block with `total`/`shown`/`truncated` counts, an `oversized_skipped` counter (constants over 2k chars are skipped and counted, not returned) and `by_host` groups capped deterministically at 500 URLs (sorted hosts first). An escaped quote ends the capture with the trailing backslash stripped. Postman mode is unchanged. This answers "what endpoints does this APK call?" for apps that build URLs without Retrofit annotations.
- Token conservation for heavy outputs (E-PY-15, commit `a44711f`), the android-unidbg-mcp strategy: cap the output, keep the honest total, mark the truncation, end with an actionable narrowing hint. New `handlers/caps.py` exposes the server-wide `ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES` cap (read per call, default 200; `0` restores the uncapped behavior exactly). Wired into the five flood-prone tools: `frida_read_output` (capped drain; excess stays buffered for the next call, reset on new session/detach), `adb_logcat_read` (oversized requests clamped, buffered count reported), `adb_logcat_stop` (final buffer capped, dropped lines counted honestly), `search_strings` (matches capped, total kept), `native_strings` (per-lib cap with the narrowing knobs named). Results under the cap are byte-for-byte identical to before; nothing is cut mid-JSON and secret findings are never silently shortened.
- Native ELF security & code search (E-PY-16, commit `52d697e`), the capstone cherry-pick: five tools in the new `handlers/sosec.py` — `so_xrefs` (scan-based xrefs to an address in a .so: branches, adrp+add pairs, movz/movk immediates), `rop_gadgets` (gadget search with `depth`/`filter`), `elf_checksec` (PIE/NX/RELRO/canary/fortify/RUNPATH, pure Python), `native_crypto_constants` (AES s-box, SHA-256/512 IVs, MD5 T-table, CRC-32, TEA delta, Base64, Blowfish — file offset + VA), `syscall_lookup` (arm64/x86_64 tables bundled from kernel headers). capstone becomes the optional `[native]` extra (added to `[all]` and `[dev]`); the pure-Python three work without it. All list outputs ride the E-PY-15 caps. Catalog grows 62 → 67 tools (+0.9k schema tokens vs the +3.2k the full capstone server would have added).

### Changed (Python)
- **Behavior note for upgraders:** heavy list outputs are capped per call by default (200 lines, `ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES`); set it to `0` for the exact 1.4.0 behavior.
- `android_api_extractor`'s description stops overclaiming: the OkHttp side reports detected client-field declarations, not extracted URLs.
- 38 new hermetic tests (`tests/test_output_caps.py`, `tests/test_sosec.py`, `tests/test_api_extractor.py`); suite now 173 passed + 1 skipped.

### Docs
- README: tool counts (67), the E-PY-15 cap notes on the affected tool rows, and a new "Companion servers" section pairing [smali-lsp](https://github.com/surendrajat/smali-lsp) into the patch loop (its `smali_diagnostics` pre-validate hand edits before `apk_rebuild_sign`).

## [1.4.0] - 2026-11-15

### Consolidation (PyPI ← npm)

### BREAKING

- Console command renamed **`mobile-re-mcp-py` → `android-re-mcp`** (npm users:
  `mobile-re-mcp` → `android-re-mcp`). No compatibility alias is provided — MCP
  client configs, shell scripts and `uvx`/`pipx` invocations that reference the
  old command must be updated. The Python import package (`android_re_mcp`) is
  unchanged.


The npm server (`mobile-re-mcp`) is retired: its static Android tools are
ported into the Python package, its iOS tools dropped, and its TypeScript
sources deleted — one package,
one implementation, one publish pipeline. Ports landed before any removal, so
there was never a window where a capability existed nowhere.

### Renamed: `android-re-mcp`

With the npm half retired there is no second implementation to disambiguate,
so the project is rebranded: PyPI project **`android-re-mcp`**, command
**`android-re-mcp`** (was `mobile-re-mcp-py`), import package
**`android_re_mcp`**, server name `android-re-mcp`, env prefix
**`ANDROID_RE_MCP_*`** (was `MOBILE_RE_MCP_*`), data/config folders
`~/.local/share/android-re-mcp` and `~/.config/android-re-mcp`. The retired
npm name `mobile-re-mcp` gets a deprecation notice pointing here. Anyone
upgrading: reinstall under the new name and update the env-var prefix in
client configs.

### Added (Python)
- `apk_diff` — build-vs-build diff ported from the npm tool (E-NPM-4 → E-PY-10): identity/SDK levels, security-flag changes, permission and exported-component deltas, native-library sha256 changes, optional secret deltas and an archive inventory. Zero new dependencies — the manifest section reads through the androguard already shipped by `[static]` (missing extra or an unreadable manifest degrades that section honestly), native libs/secrets/inventory are stdlib-only, the secret scan extracts printable strings from `classes*.dex` / `resources.arsc` / text assets instead of shelling out to `strings(1)`, and the npm size caps carry over (`ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_FILE_MB`, `ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_ENTRY_MB`). Verified live: identical build reports all-same; two different apps show every delta section; manifest-less fixtures degrade with the real reason.
- `android_api_extractor` — Retrofit/OkHttp endpoint extraction ported from the npm tool (E-NPM-5's subject → E-PY-11): walks a smali tree for `Lretrofit2/http/*` runtime annotation blocks (endpoint = the `value = "..."` entry, whitespace-collapsed body as fallback) and OkHttp3 field declarations, with `output_format` of `txt` (structured lists) or `postman` (a ready-to-import Postman v2.1 collection with every endpoint on a `{{base_url}}` variable). Give it `apk_path` and it decompiles first with the apktool the server already wraps, or point `smali_dir` at an existing decompile to skip that step. One port fix: npm's field pattern required a space before `Lokhttp3/`, which real apktool output (`name:Lokhttp3/Type;`) never matches — the port drops the space so canonical field declarations are found. Verified live: real 21 MB APK decompiled end-to-end through the server (honest zero counts — that app carries no annotations or OkHttp-typed fields), plus a canonical-form smali tree extracting 3 annotations and 2 fields into both formats.
- `android_google_services` — Google/Firebase config extraction ported from the npm tool (E-PY-12): parses a bundled `google-services.json` (exact `assets/` location first, else any entry whose name ends with it) into project info + per-client package/app-id/API-key/OAuth list; with `smali_dir` it scans `res/values/strings.xml` for the ten well-known Google keys as structured `key = value` pairs; without it, `resources.arsc` goes through the five Google patterns from npm's `patterns.ts` (names + risks verbatim) via zero-dependency printable-string extraction instead of `strings(1)`. Each section degrades honestly on its own. The scan machinery (printable strings, size caps, zip-source walk) moved into a shared `handlers/apkscan.py` used by both `apk_diff` and this tool — `apk_diff` behavior unchanged. Verified live on TiviMate: the arsc scan surfaces the app's real Firebase config (API key, `tivimate-233306.firebaseio.com`, appspot bucket); the strings.xml path honestly reports that this app stores none of the ten keys.
- `manifest_parse` extended with `categorize_permissions: true` (E-PY-13, the npm permissions-checker port): adds `permission_categorization` — the dangerous/normal split with a per-permission reason and npm's risk-summary lines (toll fraud, tracking, covert recording, arbitrary APK installs). The `dangerous_permissions` set grows from 12 hand-picked grants to the npm tool's 40-name triage taxonomy verbatim (runtime-dangerous plus install-time/signature grants worth triage), now matched on the short name like npm (bare `READ_SMS` counts, custom namespaces don't). Without the flag the output is unchanged. Verified live: notesdemo categorizes 4 dangerous + 1 normal with reasons and two summary lines; TermuxBoot reports 0 dangerous / 2 normal / empty summary.
- `rasp_identify` extended with the npm `android_native_libraries` tool folded in (E-PY-14, no new tool): every `lib/<abi>/*.so` entry is inventoried per ABI and ELF-inspected — class/machine/type, section-header presence and section names — with the npm known-library table ported verbatim (31 rows: packers, RASP, frameworks, SDKs, runtimes). Packer/RASP basename hits join the tool's `detected` list under their product label, and stripped/packed section tables or unrecognised suspicious ELF layouts surface as `protection_signals`. Zero new dependencies (hand-rolled ELF header parse; the npm original could throw past its length check, the port degrades instead). Verified live: TiviMate's 24 `.so` files across 4 ABIs identify `libdexprotector.so` as DexProtector (packer) everywhere, flipping the tool to protection tier `enterprise`; a no-native-code APK reports the npm wording honestly.


### Removed (npm)
- the iOS half of the npm server: all seven `ios_*` tools
  (`ios_manifest_analyzer`, `ios_permissions_checker`, `ios_entitlements_checker`,
  `ios_binary_strings`, `ios_frameworks_detector`, `ios_google_services`,
  `ios_secrets_scanner`), `src/tools/ios/` with its shared `extract-binary.ts`,
  the `plist`/`@types/plist` dependencies, and every iOS/ipa reference in the
  README, CONTRIBUTING, issue/PR templates and CI workflow. The npm package
  now reads Android APKs only — matching its static Android tools moving into
  the Python package this release (see the phase-2 note in
  docs/code-review-and-extensions.md).
- the npm server itself. With all five static Android tools ported (E-PY-10…14),
  the TypeScript half is deleted: `src/`, `test/`, `package.json` +
  `package-lock.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `test-tools.mjs`, the npm publish
  workflow, the reusable-analyze workflow it backed, the Node CI matrix and
  version-match job, the npm Dependabot ecosystem, and `node_modules`/
  `dist` artifacts. CI is now pytest + ruff on Python 3.11/3.13; the publish
  pipeline is PyPI-only (`publish-pypi.yml`). README documents the retirement
  and points installers at `pip install "android-re-mcp[all]"`; CONTRIBUTING
  is rewritten PyPI-only; the bug-report template lists Python tool names;
  SECURITY's supported-versions table is 1.4.x-only. npm marks the package
  deprecated:
  `npm deprecate mobile-re-mcp "consolidated into the Python package (pip install android-re-mcp)"`.

## [1.3.0] - 2026-11-10

This release is the rebuild pass documented in
[docs/code-review-and-extensions.md](docs/code-review-and-extensions.md): every
`[verified live]` finding fixed with before/after evidence, the npm server
hardened against hostile archives, and five new tools.

### Fixed (Python)
- `manifest_parse`, `analyze_code`, `find_crypto_usage` and `find_urls` work again on the androguard 4.x that `[static]` installs — the exported-components logic is now derived from the parsed manifest (with explicit / intent-filter / pre-17 auto-export markers), the call-graph helpers tolerate every 3.x/4.x record shape, and `apk_analyze_full` reports per-stage status honestly instead of masking failures (F-PY-1).
- `check_tools` reports what the handlers actually need: pip CLIs resolve through the interpreter-sibling fallback (`clitools.find_cli`), the SSH cracker named `medusa` no longer counts as the framework, and every entry says which MCP tools use it (F-PY-2).
- The 8 built-in Frida scripts ship with the package again, each implementing the `recv('config')` protocol, and `frida_find_bytes` works on frida 17 (F-PY-3, plus the QuickJS `process` global fix, D-5).
- Tool handlers no longer block the asyncio loop: stateless handlers run on worker threads, the three stateful classes keep their ordering on a dedicated pool (F-PY-4).
- Script parameters travel as `{'type':'config', …}` after load instead of `str.replace` on magic source lines (F-PY-5).
- Dead weight removed from the dependency list and the checks; housekeeping for `frida_memdump`'s dump directory, the HAR helper's deprecated `utcnow`, and `adb_shell`'s argument-model documentation (F-PY-6, F-PY-7, E-PY-9).
- Rooted-device round: `frida_attach` works by package identifier even when frida only knows the app label (D-6); `frida_memdump` no longer OOM-kills the target by reading multi-GB ranges — a per-range cap (`max_range_mb`, default 32) with the skips reported (D-7); and `MOBILE_RE_MCP_FRIDA_ENDPOINT` routes every `frida_*` tool to a stealth frida-server (renamed binary, non-default port via `adb forward`) that USB discovery can never find (D-8).
- The 7 Java-hooking Frida scripts are rebuilt as `frida-compile` bundles with `frida-java-bridge` compiled in — frida 17 removed the `Java` global from script runtimes, so the raw sources died with `ReferenceError: 'Java' is not defined` on a real device (D-9). `build_bundles.sh` reproduces them from `frida_scripts/src/`.

### Fixed (npm)
- Zip-bomb guard: inputs are capped at 2048 MB and single decompressed entries at 256 MB (`ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_FILE_MB` / `ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_ENTRY_MB`, `0` disables), checked before decompression on every APK/IPA read (F-NPM-4).
- One shared iOS binary extractor and one shared scan-result merge replace three drifting copies each (F-NPM-3).
- `apk_manifest_analyzer` uses the `aapt2` fallback it could already parse (F-NPM-2).
- The smoke runner is honest about fixtures and coverage, `npm test` runs the hermetic suite, and the small consistency fixes landed: shared `min_length` default, prefix-only framework matching, DexGuard out of the iOS table, Windows ENOENT hint, dead code removal (F-NPM-1, F-NPM-5, E-NPM-7).

### Added
- **`quark_scan`** (PyPI): quark-engine behaviour scoring with keyword/score filters; also a best-effort stage of `apk_analyze_full` (E-PY-3).
- **`frida_status`** (PyPI): frida version, devices, server responsiveness, session state — the "am I attached?" read (E-PY-7).
- **`adb_ui_dump`** (PyPI): the current UI as structured elements via uiautomator (E-PY-8).
- **`android_native_libraries`** (npm): every `lib/<abi>/*.so` with packer/RASP/framework fingerprinting and ELF section inspection (E-NPM-3).
- **`apk_diff`** (npm): two builds side by side — identity, flags, permission/component deltas, native-library sha256 deltas, secret deltas (E-NPM-4).

PyPI server: 58 tools. npm server: 14 tools.

## [1.2.3] - 2026-11-03

### Fixed
- `apk_manifest_analyzer` misread the output of `aapt`, which it prefers when installed. `aapt` prints booleans as `(type 0x12)0xffffffff` and the component names on separate lines, so the old patterns found nothing. An APK with `debuggable`, `allowBackup`, cleartext traffic and exported components could be reported as clean. The manifest is now parsed properly from `aapt`, `aapt2` and `apktool` output, and relative class names are shown in full.
- The same tool now lists components that are exported by default through an intent filter, and returns an error instead of a clean result when it cannot read the manifest.

### Added
- Parser tests in `test/`, run with `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"` after a build, and a CI step for them.

### Changed
- The README example now uses an APK.

## [1.2.2] - 2026-11-03

### Changed
- Restored the banner at the top of the README.
- Recreated the npm trusted publisher, so releases can publish from GitHub Actions again.

## [1.2.1] - 2026-11-02

### Changed
- Rewrote the README, CONTRIBUTING and SECURITY in plainer language. The README now opens with a worked example, has install steps for Claude Code, opencode and Claude Desktop, and lists each tool once with what it needs.
- The Python README now covers setup, a first session and the safety settings.

### Fixed
- npm publish workflow: it now ends green when the version is already on npm, which happens when you publish by hand, and a failed publish prints which trusted publisher settings to check. It no longer passes `--provenance`, because trusted publishing adds provenance itself. You can also run it by hand from the Actions tab to see what npm says about the login, without publishing anything.
- Python server: messages about a missing tool now point to `mobile-re-mcp-py --setup`. They used to mention `install_tool`, which is off unless you enable it.

## [1.2.0] - 2026-11-02

### Added
- Python server in `python/`, published on PyPI as `mobile-re-mcp` (command `mobile-re-mcp-py`). It adds adb, Frida, mitmproxy, apktool/jadx, patching and signing tools. It is derived from `mobile-security-mcp` 0.1.4 (MIT), see `python/NOTICE.md`.
- One release tag now publishes both packages, and CI fails if their versions differ. The npm package has no code changes in this release.

### Security (Python server)
- Every tool call is checked before it runs. File arguments reject a leading `-`, NUL bytes and protected places such as `~/.ssh`, `~/.config/gh` and shell rc files, and they follow `MOBILE_RE_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS`.
- `native_disasm` no longer lets `;` or `!` reach radare2, which allowed shell commands from a hostile symbol name.
- `search_strings` passes the pattern to ripgrep with `-e` and `--`, so `--pre=...` can no longer run a program.
- SSE listens on 127.0.0.1 only, rejects foreign Host headers, and needs `MOBILE_RE_MCP_TOKEN` for any other address. It used to bind 0.0.0.0 with no authentication.
- mitmproxy listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Use `adb reverse` to reach it from the device.
- Downloads are pinned to a release and checked against a SHA-256. The apktool wrapper script no longer comes from the `master` branch.
- `install_tool` is off unless `MOBILE_RE_MCP_ALLOW_INSTALL=1`. pip installs no longer use `--break-system-packages` and cannot change an installed Frida.
- Scratch files live in a private folder instead of fixed names in `/tmp`, and `frida_server_push` no longer picks up binaries from `/tmp`.
- Target notes are stored under `~/.local/share/mobile-re-mcp` and the package name is validated. It could write into any folder before.

### Changed (Python server)
- Requires `mcp` 1.30 or newer and below 2. SDK 2 removed the handler decorators this server uses, so the port is still to do.
- The heavy tools (frida, androguard, apkid, apkleaks, mitmproxy, quark-engine) are optional extras. `textual`, `rich` and `tomli` are no longer dependencies.
- Settings moved to `~/.config/mobile-re-mcp/config.toml`. Nothing is created or added to `PATH` at import time any more.
- Downloaded tools are apktool 2.12.1, jadx 1.5.6, uber-apk-signer 1.3.0, Il2CppDumper 6.7.46 and scrcpy 5.0.1 (Windows). adb is no longer downloaded because Google only publishes an unversioned build. The smali/baksmali installer is gone because its URLs return 404.

### Fixed (Python server)
- `apk_sign` looked for the signer jar in the current directory while the installer put it in `~/tools/signing`.
- `frida_server_push` ignored a failed `chmod` on the device.
- `frida_list_scripts` listed scripts that are not in the package. It now lists only scripts that exist, and your own go in `~/.local/share/mobile-re-mcp/frida_scripts`.
- The SSE endpoint used a route type that cannot serve the message endpoint.
- mitm helper scripts ran under whatever `python` was on `PATH` and now use the server's interpreter.

## [1.1.2] - 2026-11-02

### Fixed
- Added package-lock.json so npm ci works in CI.
- CI now runs on master.

## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-01

### Security
- No tool builds shell command strings any more. All external programs (`apktool`, `aapt`, `aapt2`, `strings`, `file`, `codesign`, `ldid`, `plutil`) run via `execFileSync` with argument arrays and a timeout, closing a command-injection path through `apk_path` / `smali_folder`.
- Input paths are validated: must be absolute, exist, and resolve (symlinks) to a regular `.apk` / `.ipa` file with ZIP magic bytes, or to a directory for `smali_folder`.
- iOS: `CFBundleExecutable` read from an untrusted `Info.plist` is regex-escaped before matching, and the binary-plist conversion uses a private temp directory instead of a predictable file name.
- New optional `MOBILE_RE_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS` allow-list for readable locations.
- `secrets-scanner`: smali-folder scan now reads regular files only (no symlink-following).
- `reusable-analyze.yml`: workflow inputs/outputs are passed through `env` instead of being interpolated into shell; random heredoc delimiter for step outputs.

### Changed
- The server reports the version from `package.json` instead of a hard-coded string.
- Renamed project to `mobile-re-mcp` (package, binary, server name, docs) and maintainer/repository owner to `FlyPhantomFly`. The original MIT copyright notice (Serhatcck) is retained in `LICENSE`.
- Migrated to MCP TypeScript SDK v2 (`@modelcontextprotocol/server`, `registerTool`, `serveStdio`); tool schemas are wrapped in `z.object(...)`.
- Dependencies: `zod` 3 -> 4, `adm-zip` -> 0.6 (fixes CVE-2026-39244; ships its own types), `typescript` 5 -> 6, `@types/node` 20 -> 22. Removed `ts-node` and `@types/adm-zip`. `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` ("latest") replaced by pinned-range `@modelcontextprotocol/server`.
- Requires Node.js 22+. CI and publish workflows use `actions/checkout@v6` and `actions/setup-node@v6`; Dependabot now also tracks GitHub Actions.
- `package-lock.json` removed so it can be regenerated against the new dependency set (`npm install`).

## [1.0.0] - 2025-04-02

### Added

**Android tools**
- `apk_manifest_analyzer` — parses AndroidManifest.xml, flags debuggable/allowBackup/cleartext traffic, exported components, intent filters
- `apk_permissions_checker` — categorizes dangerous vs normal permissions with risk summary
- `android_api_extractor` — decompiles smali bytecode to extract Retrofit HTTP endpoints and OkHttp3 fields; outputs plain text or Postman collection
- `android_google_services` — extracts Firebase/GCP config from `google-services.json` and `resources.arsc` via strings command; supports optional smali_folder for structured output
- `android_secrets_scanner` — scans DEX bytecode + `resources.arsc` + text assets for hardcoded API keys and credentials

**iOS tools**
- `ios_manifest_analyzer` — parses Info.plist, flags ATS misconfigs, URL schemes, background location, queried schemes
- `ios_permissions_checker` — maps all `NS*UsageDescription` keys to HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW risk with explanations
- `ios_entitlements_checker` — extracts entitlements from app binary via codesign/ldid, flags get-task-allow and sandbox bypass, detects simulator builds
- `ios_binary_strings` — extracts URLs, emails, private IPs, and API key patterns from Mach-O binary
- `ios_frameworks_detector` — enumerates bundled .framework and .dylib files, maps ~60 known SDKs across networking, analytics, ads, attribution, crash reporting, fraud detection categories
- `ios_google_services` — parses GoogleService-Info.plist for full Firebase configuration
- `ios_secrets_scanner` — two-layer scan: text resource files (plist/json/strings) + app binary via strings command

**Shared**
- `patterns.ts` — centralized `GOOGLE_PATTERNS` and `SECRET_PATTERNS` registry shared across all scanner tools; `scanText` and `renderResults` utilities

`CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```md
# Contributing
Bug reports, new detection patterns and new tools are all welcome. For anything bigger than a small fix, open an issue first so we can agree on the approach.

## Setting up
```bash
git clone https://github.com/FlyPhantomFly/android-re-mcp.git
cd android-re-mcp
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e "python[dev]"
ruff check python && pytest python/tests
```
The Python server needs Python 3.11 or newer. `ruff format python` is the formatter; CI runs ruff check and pytest on 3.11 and 3.13.

## How the Python server is laid out
`python/src/android_re_mcp/server.py` owns the tool list: every tool has a schema entry and a dispatch entry. The work happens in `python/src/android_re_mcp/handlers/` — one module per area (`static.py` for apktool/androguard/apkleaks/quark, `dynamic.py` for Frida, `network.py` for mitmproxy, `device.py` for adb, and so on). Shared helpers live beside them: `paths.py` (scratch/data folders), `guard.py` (path validation), and `apkscan.py` (the zero-dependency APK byte-scanning machinery: size caps, printable strings, the pattern scanner).

## Adding a tool
1. Create or extend a handler module and add a method that takes `args: dict` and returns `{"status": ..., "tool": ..., "output": ...}` (`ok` / `error` / `missing_tool`).
2. Register the method in `server.py`: the `TOOLS` schema list and the dispatch mapping.
3. Add a row to the tools table in `README.md` and a line to `CHANGELOG.md`.

Return structured JSON, degrade honestly (a missing section reports the real reason), and never raise past the handler. If the tool wraps an external program, check it with `shutil.which` and return `missing_tool` with a hint pointing at `android-re-mcp --setup`; build argument arrays, never shell strings; validate every path with the guard (absolute, exists, inside an allowed dir).

If the tool parses the output of another program, add a fixture under `python/tests/fixtures/` taken from the real program and a test beside it. The manifest analyzer once read `aapt` output wrongly and called a bad APK clean, which is why those tests exist.

## Adding a detection pattern
Secret scanning (`apk_scan_secrets`) runs [apkleaks](https://github.com/dwisiswant0/apkleaks) with its own rule set; the zero-dependency scanners carry their pattern tables beside the tool that uses them — `_SECRET_PATTERNS` in `python/src/android_re_mcp/handlers/apkdiff.py` (the `apk_diff` secret deltas) and `_GOOGLE_PATTERNS` in `python/src/android_re_mcp/handlers/googleservices.py`. Add an entry there:
```python
("My Service API Key", re.compile(r"my-service-[A-Za-z0-9]{32}"), "HIGH"),
```
Risk is one of `HIGH`, `MEDIUM` or `LOW`. To teach the native-library identification about a known library (packer, RASP, framework, SDK or runtime), add a row to `_KNOWN_ANDROID_LIBS` in `python/src/android_re_mcp/handlers/native.py` with a pattern, a label and a kind.

## Pull requests
Keep each one to a single change, say what changed and why, and run `ruff check python` and `pytest python/tests` first. If you can, try the change on a real APK, and leave sensitive details out of what you paste. Add a line to `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Releasing
This part is for maintainers. The package is published from GitHub Actions through PyPI trusted publishing (OIDC), so no PyPI token is stored in GitHub. For the first release, add a pending publisher on pypi.org under Your account, Publishing (project `android-re-mcp`, owner `FlyPhantomFly`, repository `android-re-mcp`, workflow `publish-pypi.yml`, environment `pypi`). In GitHub, create the `pypi` environment under Settings, Environments, and add yourself as a required reviewer.

For every release:
1. Update `CHANGELOG.md` and set the `version` in `python/pyproject.toml`. Commit and push.
2. Tag it (`git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z`) and create a GitHub Release for the tag.
3. The release starts `publish-pypi.yml`. Approve the deployment when GitHub asks. The workflow refuses to publish if the tag does not match `pyproject.toml`, and building distributions is part of the workflow itself.

## Reporting issues
Use the issue templates for bugs and feature requests. Security problems go through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), not a public issue.

```

`README.md`:

```md
<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="docs/social-preview-dark.svg">
  <img src="docs/social-preview-light.svg" alt="android-re-mcp" width="100%">
</picture>

[![version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/android-re-mcp?style=flat-square&logo=pypi&logoColor=white&label=version&color=0e7490)](https://pypi.org/project/android-re-mcp/) [![tests](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/FlyPhantomFly/android-re-mcp/ci.yml?style=flat-square&label=tests&color=10b981)](https://github.com/FlyPhantomFly/android-re-mcp/actions) [![code style](https://img.shields.io/badge/code%20style-ruff-261230?style=flat-square&logo=ruff&logoColor=white)](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) [![python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-0e7490?style=flat-square&logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/android-re-mcp/) [![dexfile-cli](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/FlyPhantomFly/dexfile-cli?style=flat-square&label=dexfile-cli&color=0e7490)](https://github.com/FlyPhantomFly/dexfile-cli/releases) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-10b981?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)

android-re-mcp is an MCP server for Android reverse engineering. 

You point it at a real device and a target app, then just ask: *what is this app, what's protecting it, and how do I get past that?* 

The assistant picks from 89 tools: decompile, hook, trace traffic, dump memory, patch smali or dex, read the resource table, patch native code, sign and reinstall, and walks you through the answer.

It's one package: PyPI: `android-re-mcp`

---

## The Python server (the PyPI package)

### What it does exactly

`pip install "android-re-mcp[all]"` gives you an MCP server, started as `android-re-mcp`, that speaks MCP over stdio (or SSE on 127.0.0.1 with a bearer token) and exposes **89 tools over one Android target at a time**:

- **Static work on the APK file itself** — apktool and jadx decompilation, ripgrep searches across the decompiled folder, androguard manifest parsing and bytecode cross-references, apkid packer/obfuscator identification, apkleaks secret scanning, quark-engine behaviour rules (`quark_scan`), and an orchestrator (`apk_analyze_full`) that runs all of those in one call and scores the protection tier.
- **Dynamic work on a running app** — spawn or attach a process with Frida, inject JavaScript, stream script output back, hook SSL pinning, dump and search process memory, trace storage, crypto and network calls from a built-in script collection you can extend with your own scripts.
- **Work on the phone** — list devices, run shell commands, install APKs, pull and push files, capture logcat, mirror the screen with scrcpy, and take screenshots.
- **Network** — start and stop mitmproxy (loopback only), read captured flows as structured JSON, export them as HAR for Chrome DevTools or Burp.
- **Patching and signing** — edit smali in a decompiled folder, embed a Frida gadget so you can hook a non-rooted device, rebuild with apktool and sign with uber-apk-signer using your keystore or the debug one.
- **Native and cross-platform code** — strings/exports/disassembly for `.so` files, Il2CppDumper for Unity, Blutter and engine-version detection for Flutter, Hermes decoding for React Native.
- **Workflow support** — a RASP signature database and ready-made bypass scripts, per-target notes kept across sessions, a self-check of your toolchain, and 12 knowledge packs served as MCP resources and prompts (assessments, bypass escalation ladders, common mistakes).

It is Android only. Several tools change the device (install, push, patch), which is why the guard layer described below checks every call before it runs.

### Install

```bash
pip install "android-re-mcp[all]"
android-re-mcp --setup
```

It needs Python 3.11 or newer. The base install is just the MCP server. The extras pick up the heavy libraries, and you can install parts instead of all:

| Extra | What it adds | Which tools need it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[frida]` | frida, frida-tools | every `frida_*` tool, `ssl_kill_switch` |
| `[static]` | androguard, apkid, apkleaks | `manifest_parse`, `analyze_code`, `find_crypto_usage`, `find_urls`, `apk_identify`, `apk_scan_secrets`, `apk_analyze_full` |
| `[network]` | mitmproxy | `mitm_start/stop/read_flows/export_har` |
| `[analysis]` | quark-engine | `quark_scan` (also a best-effort stage of `apk_analyze_full`) |
| `[native]` | capstone | `so_xrefs`, `rop_gadgets` |
| `[all]` | everything above | — |

If Frida is already pinned in your environment, install without extras and the server will not touch it.

`--setup` downloads pinned, checksum-verified copies of apktool 2.12.1, jadx 1.5.6, uber-apk-signer 1.3.0, Il2CppDumper 6.7.46 and dexfile-cli 0.1.9 into `~/tools`. adb comes from your package manager (`sudo apt install adb`); scrcpy and radare2 too. Run `android-re-mcp --setup` again any time to fill in whatever is missing.

### Connect it

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add android-re -- android-re-mcp
```

opencode, in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "android-re": { "type": "local", "command": ["/path/to/venv/bin/android-re-mcp"], "enabled": true }
  }
}
```

Claude Desktop, in `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "android-re": { "command": "/path/to/venv/bin/android-re-mcp" }
  }
}
```

Use the full path to the command if it lives in a virtualenv. Any other client needs only the command, with no arguments. stdio is the default transport; `--transport sse --port 8765` also works, listens on 127.0.0.1 only, and any other `--host` needs `ANDROID_RE_MCP_TOKEN`, which clients send as a bearer token.

Start with a check of what you have: ask "Run check_tools", and the assistant lists which tools it found (with versions) and which are missing, with install hints. On a set-up machine nearly everything reports available — only the optional extras you skipped show as missing.

### A first session

Ask in plain language, and the assistant picks the tools. Some prompts and what they use:

- "Check my devices and get frida-server onto the phone." (`adb_devices`, `frida_server_push`)
- "Decompile /home/me/apks/app.apk and search the strings for token or secret." (`apk_decompile`, `search_strings`)
- "What is this app, which framework, what protection does it use, and how bad is it overall?" (`apk_analyze_full`)
- "Which protection does com.example.app use, and how do I get past it?" (`rasp_identify`, `rasp_bypass`)
- "Track this app's network traffic." (`mitm_start`, then `adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080`, open the app, `mitm_read_flows`, `mitm_export_har`)
- "Bypass SSL pinning in com.example.app and watch the requests." (`ssl_kill_switch` or a `frida_run_script` of `ssl_pinning_universal`)
- "Patch the license check in the smali, rebuild, sign and install it." (`smali_patch`, `apk_rebuild_sign`, `adb_install`)
- "Swap one string in classes.dex without rebuilding the whole APK." (`dex_extract`, `dex_patch`, `dex_swap`, `apk_sign`, `adb_install` — the dex-only fast loop: no apktool resource decode, no resource rebuild)
- "Which scheme is this APK signed with, and when does the cert expire?" (`apk_read_signature`)
- "Is this app's integrity intact, and are there duplicate zip entries?" (`zip_test`, `apk_build_check`)
- "Patch the license string inside libnative.so and swap it back." (`native_patch_string` or `native_patch_instructions`, `zip_update`, `apk_sign`)
- "Where does @string/app_name point, and who references that id?" (`resource_table_list`, `resource_read`, `resource_xref`)
- "Dump the app's memory and find the session key." (`frida_attach`, `frida_find_bytes`, `frida_memdump`)

The server also carries seven guided prompts (`master-workflow`, `first-look`, `rasp-assess`, `bypass-ssl`, `bypass-root`, `bypass-frida`, `stuck`) and keeps per-app notes so a later session can pick up where the last one stopped (`memory_read`, `memory_write`).

### The tool set

Every tool returns structured JSON with a `status` field (`ok`, `error`, `missing_tool`) — your assistant can chain calls. File arguments are absolute paths validated by the guard. `apk_decompile` and `apk_decompile_java` land next to the APK (`<name>_apktool/`, `<name>_jadx/`); dumps and captures go to the private data folder.
Heavy list outputs are token-conserved: a search, a strings dump, logcat and Frida script output are capped per call (default 200 lines, `ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES`) with the honest total kept and an actionable narrowing hint, so one call can't flood the model's context.

**Static analysis (11)**

| Tool | What it does | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apk_decompile` | apktool decompile (smali + resources), or resources/smali only via `mode` | apktool |
| `apk_decompile_java` | jadx decompile to Java source; falls back to apktool (smali) when jadx is unavailable, flagged with `engine` + note | jadx (apktool fallback) |

### Knowledge packs and prompts

Five MCP **resources**: `knowledge://detection-patterns` (root/Frida/emulator/integrity checks and their counters), `knowledge://bypass-playbooks` (escalation ladders), `knowledge://framework-fingerprints` (React Native, Flutter, Unity, Xamarin from artefacts), `knowledge://crypto-patterns` (hardcoded keys, weak IVs, insecure ciphers) and `knowledge://common-mistakes`. Seven MCP **prompts** wrap the same packs: `master-workflow`, `first-look`, `rasp-assess`, `bypass-ssl`, `bypass-root`, `bypass-frida`, `stuck`. Your client's prompt picker lists them; they cost nothing to call.

Eight bypass/monitor scripts ship with the package (`ssl_pinning_universal`, `root_detection_bypass`, `frida_detection_bypass`, `crypto_monitor`, `memory_scan`, `method_tracer`, `storage_monitor`, `network_monitor`) — every one accepts live config: post or send `{type:'config', ...}` (UPPER-case keys as shown by `frida_list_scripts` usage strings; lowercase accepted too). Drop your own script into `~/.local/share/android-re-mcp/frida_scripts` using the same catalogue filename and yours is used instead of the shipped one.

### Files and settings

- Notes, captures and scratch files: `~/.local/share/android-re-mcp` (`ANDROID_RE_MCP_HOME` to move; created `0700`)
- Your settings: `~/.config/android-re-mcp/config.toml` (`ANDROID_RE_MCP_CONFIG`) — today just `[signing]` keystore paths and passwords
- Downloaded tools: `~/tools` (`ANDROID_RE_MCP_TOOLS_DIR`); subfolders (jadx, platform-tools, il2cppdumper, scrcpy) are appended to the server's PATH if present
- `ANDROID_RE_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS` — folders (separated by `:`) that all file arguments must stay inside
- `ANDROID_RE_MCP_DISABLE_TOOLS` — comma-separated tools to switch off, e.g. `adb_shell,adb_push,adb_pull`
- `ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES` — per-call cap for heavy list outputs (default 200; `0` disables) — the total stays honest and the result names how to narrow
- `ANDROID_RE_MCP_ALLOW_INSTALL=1` — the only way `install_tool` becomes callable over MCP (`--setup` always works)
- `ANDROID_RE_MCP_FRIDA_ENDPOINT=127.0.0.1:31337` — connect every `frida_*` tool to a remote frida-server instead of USB discovery. For a stealth setup (renamed server binary on a non-default port, reached via `adb forward tcp:31337 tcp:31337`) USB discovery finds nothing — this is the switch that makes the dynamic tools work against it.

### Staying safe

This server runs commands on your phone and your computer, so treat its tools with care.

- Every call passes the guard first: file arguments reject a leading `-`, NUL bytes, and protected locations (`~/.ssh`, `~/.config/gh`, shell rc files, keyrings, …); `package`, `serial`, `port` and similar arguments are pattern-checked; writes into `/etc` are refused.
- The stateful tools (`frida_spawn`, `adb_shell`, `adb_install`, `mitm_*`, signing) change a real device — set them to ask first in your client, and keep `ANDROID_RE_MCP_DISABLE_TOOLS` around anything you do not want reachable.
- mitmproxy listens on 127.0.0.1. Run `adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080` and point the phone's proxy at 127.0.0.1:8080.
- SSE transport is loopback-only unless you set `ANDROID_RE_MCP_TOKEN`; foreign Host headers are rejected.
- Downloads are pinned to a release and SHA-256-verified. Scratch files live in a private `0700` folder, never `/tmp`.
- A sample you analyze can try to steer the assistant through its own strings and symbol names. Use a VM for hostile samples, and do not auto-approve tools that touch the device.

---

## Companion servers

Some capabilities are deliberately kept out of this package and paired with it as separate MCP servers — the token cost stays opt-in per project, and each tool keeps its own release cycle.

**smali-lsp** ([github.com/surendrajat/smali-lsp](https://github.com/surendrajat/smali-lsp)) — a Language-Server-grade smali engine (224 Dalvik opcodes, inheritance-aware indexing) with a built-in MCP mode. It is the semantic layer this package deliberately does not reimplement: references, call graphs, workspace symbol search and — most valuably — `smali_diagnostics`, which reports *what the assembler or verifier would reject after a hand edit*. Wire it into the patching loop so a bad edit fails before `apk_rebuild_sign` burns a rebuild:

```
apk_decompile -> smali_index -> smali_patch edits -> smali_diagnostics -> apk_rebuild_sign
```

Build it once (JDK 17+, `./gradlew shadowJar`) or grab an upstream release, then register it as its own server — it needs an apktool decompile, which `apk_decompile` already produces (`<name>_apktool/`):

```bash
claude mcp add smali-lsp -- java -jar /path/to/smali-lsp.jar mcp
```

```jsonc
// opencode / Claude Desktop config
{ "smali-lsp": { "type": "local", "command": ["java", "-jar", "/path/to/smali-lsp.jar", "mcp"], "enabled": true } }
```

Its 14 tools add roughly 0.7k tokens of catalog when enabled — leave it off for sessions that never touch smali. The other integrations came from the same consolidation reviews: the native-ELF suite and the dex surgery are pinned-jar or in-package tools here (the full capstone server was rejected — 25 tools for mostly duplicative capability), all documented in `docs/code-review-and-extensions.md`.

`SECURITY.md`:

```md
# Security
## Supported versions
| Version | Supported |
| --- | --- |
| 1.4.x | PyPI (`android-re-mcp`) |
| 1.3.x | no (that npm package is retired; upgrade) |
| older | no |
## Reporting a vulnerability
Please do not open a public issue for a security problem. Report it privately through [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/FlyPhantomFly/android-re-mcp/security/advisories/new) and include what you found, how to reproduce it, what it could do, and a fix if you have one.
You should hear back within 48 hours. A first assessment follows within 7 days, a fix within 30 days for critical issues and 90 days for the rest, and details are made public after the fix ships.
## What counts
This project exists to analyze mobile apps for security problems, so a few reports go to different places.
- A wrong or missing finding is a normal bug. Open a regular issue.
- A flaw in a server itself, such as running a command it should not, reading files outside the allowed folders or listening on a network address, is private.
- A way to slip past a secret pattern or another detection is private too.

The Python server can run adb, Frida and file operations on purpose, so those tools working is not a vulnerability. Report it privately if you can get around its argument checks, make it listen on a network address without a token, or make it run something the caller did not ask for.

# Code review and extension proposals — android-re-mcp (PyPI server; the retired npm server)

Reviewed 2026-11-10. Method: full read of both codebases, plus **live smoke tests against both running MCP servers** (the ones this repo publishes), with a real device attached and a real APK (`TermuxBoot_v0.8.1_GitHub.apk`, package `com.termux.boot`, 3 DEX files, r8-compiled).

Every finding below is tagged: **[verified live]** (reproduced in a fresh tool call during this review), **[code]** (read from source), or **[test]** (established by the existing test suite).

## Part 0 — What each server currently is (one-paragraph reference)

### The Python server — PyPI package `android-re-mcp`, command `android-re-mcp`

One GitHub-flavoured codebase in `python/src/android_re_mcp/`:

- `server.py` — declares all 89 tool schemas in one `TOOL_SCHEMAS` list, wires them to 13 handler classes in a dispatch table, and serves resources (5 knowledge packs) and prompts (7 guided playbooks). Transports: stdio (default) and SSE (loopback, bearer-token enforced off-loopback).
- `handlers/*.py` — the actual work: `static.py` (apktool/jadx/apkid/apkleaks/androguard), `dynamic.py` (Frida sessions, script library, hluda, memory), `device.py` (adb, logcat, scrcpy, hermes), `network.py` (mitmproxy), `patcher.py` + `signing.py` (smali edit, gadget embed, uber-apk-signer), `native.py` / `flutter.py` (radare2, Il2CppDumper, Blutter), `rasp.py` (vendor fingerprints + bypass scripts), `memory.py` (per-target notes).
- `guard.py` — validates every call before dispatch: path deny-lists, `ANDROID_RE_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS`, `ANDROID_RE_MCP_DISABLE_TOOLS`, per-argument regexes.
- `paths.py` / `config.py` — `~/.local/share/android-re-mcp` for all writes (0700), `~/.config/android-re-mcp/config.toml` for `[signing]` settings, `~/tools` for downloaded binaries.
- `setup/` — `check_tools.py` (35-item inventory used by the `check_tools` MCP tool) and `install_tool.py` (SHA-256-pinned downloads + pip/npm recipes; MCP-invocable only with `ANDROID_RE_MCP_ALLOW_INSTALL=1`).
- Tests: `python/tests/` — 28 tests, mostly on the guard, downloads (sha-pin, zip-slip, plain-http refusal) and a handful of handler behaviours. **No test executes an androguard code path**, which is why the API drift below shipped.

### The npm server — npm package `mobile-re-mcp`, command `mobile-re-mcp` — **retired in 1.4.0**

> This section and every npm finding below are kept as the historical record of the review.
> The package was consolidated into the PyPI package (E-PY-10…14, commits `c21c6e4`…`2ca8400`),
> its iOS half was dropped in 1.4.0, and its sources (`src/`, `test/`, `package.json`) were
> deleted when the retirement completed. npm carries a deprecation notice pointing at
> `pip install android-re-mcp`.

One TypeScript codebase in `src/`:

- `src/index.ts` — registers 12 tools with the MCP TypeScript SDK v2 (`registerTool`), serves over stdio; version read from `package.json`.
- `src/tools/android/*` — 5 Android analyzers (manifest, permissions, API endpoints → text/Postman, Google/Firebase config, secrets).
- `src/tools/ios/*` — 7 iOS analyzers (manifest/ATS, permission strings, entitlements, binary strings, framework inventory, Google plist, two-layer secrets).
- `src/tools/shared/safe-exec.ts` — the only way anything runs: `execFileSync` with argument arrays (`shell: false`), 10-min timeout, 100 MiB buffer cap, plus `checkInputFile` (absolute path, symlink-resolved, regular file, `.apk`/`.ipa` extension, ZIP magic bytes, `MOBILE_RE_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS` sandbox).
- `src/tools/shared/patterns.ts` — the shared regex registry (5 Google patterns, 15 secret patterns) and the uniform text renderer.

The npm server performs zero writes except in `os.tmpdir()` and never accepts a "running" target — its toolset is exactly what the Python server is not.

---

## Part 1 — Python server: findings

### F-PY-1. androguard API drift breaks three tools on the pinned extra — **[verified live]** — **Status: fixed**

`[analysis]`-adjacent extra `[static]` declares `androguard>=3.4.0a1` (pyproject.toml:28), so today's installs get **4.1.4** (verified live: `check_tools` reports `androguard 4.1.4`). In androguard 4.x the APK class no longer has `get_activity_is_exported()`, and `Analysis` cross-reference accessors return different shapes. Results measured live on `com.termux.boot`:

| Tool | Live result |
| --- | --- |
| `manifest_parse` | `error: 'APK' object has no attribute 'get_activity_is_exported'` |
| `analyze_code` | `error: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'class_name'` — `handlers/static.py:350-357` assumes `get_xref_from()` yields method objects, 4.x yields tuples |
| `find_crypto_usage` | returned `ok` with 0 usages on a crypto-free app — cannot pass unit coverage; same suspect accessors (`for _, callee, _ in method.get_xref_to()`, static.py:437) mean it will mis-shape or drop results on any app with crypto calls |
| `find_urls` | worked (returned 20 URLs) — keep its approach |
| `apk_analyze_full` | silently reports the broken `manifest_parse` output inside its `manifest` field while still returning `status: ok` — masking failure is worse than failing |

Where it lives: `handlers/static.py:229-257` (`manifest_parse`), `:315-383` (`analyze_code`), `:423-463` (`find_crypto_usage`), `:185-219` (`apk_analyze_full`).

### F-PY-2. `check_tools` reports availability the handlers can't use — **[verified live]** — **Status: fixed**

- `check_tools` checks apkleaks as a *Python module* (importable → `available: true`, check_tools.py:172), but `apk_scan_secrets` needs the **CLI on PATH** (`shutil.which("apkleaks")`, static.py:153). Live: `check_tools` said apkleaks ✓; `apk_scan_secrets` returned `missing_tool 'apkleaks' not found on PATH.` The inventory lies to the assistant exactly when it matters (it recommends "run check_tools first" in docs).
- `check_tools` reports `medusa` **available** — live output was `Medusa v2.3 [http://www.foofus.net]` — that is the SSH/password **login cracker**, not the Frida script framework this tool chain expects. Name collision, false positive (check_tools.py:238).

*Fix:* all CLI consumers and `check_tools` resolve through the new `android_re_mcp.clitools.find_cli` (PATH first, then the console-script dir next to the running interpreter — venv installs where PATH misses the venv bin); apkleaks/apkid are probed as executables; `medusa` runs a version probe and rejects any banner containing `foofus.net` with a GitHub hint for the real framework; `install_tool` no longer has a pip recipe for `medusa`/`fridump` (manual-required).

### F-PY-3. The built-in Frida script library is a façade — **[verified live]** — **Status: fixed**

`frida_scripts/index.py` catalogues 8 scripts (`ssl_pinning_universal`, `root_detection_bypass`, `frida_detection_bypass`, `crypto_monitor`, `memory_scan`, `method_tracer`, `storage_monitor`, `network_monitor`) but the package ships **zero `.js` files** (`frida_scripts/` contains only `index.py`, `__init__.py`). `frida_list_scripts` correctly applies the 1.2.0 fix that only lists files that exist, so live result: `total: 0, available_categories: []`.

Consequences beyond the library itself: `frida_find_bytes` **depends on the missing `memory_scan.js`** (dynamic.py:547-549 returns an error if absent), and the docs' "frida_get_script → frida_run_script" workflow is unusable out of the box. The CHANGELOG 1.2.0 entry ("It now lists only scripts that exist") papered over the symptom instead of shipping the files.

*Fix:* all 8 `.js` files are shipped with the package (E-PY-1, commit `4270bd9`), every script implements the config protocol, and the library is guarded by unit tests that compare the catalogue against what is on disk.

### F-PY-4. Sync handlers block the asyncio event loop — **[code]** — **Status: fixed**

`server.py`'s `call_tool` invokes every handler directly; all handlers are synchronous (`subprocess.run` with 120–600 s timeouts, `time.sleep(1)` in `mitm_start`). Inside asyncio, this freezes the whole server for the duration of e.g. a jadx decompile. — no other tool call is processed, even in SSE mode with a second client.

*Fix:* E-PY-4 (commit `ed2fd6b`): `call_tool` is a thin wrapper over `_run_tool`; stateless handlers run via `asyncio.to_thread` and the three stateful classes own a dedicated single-worker pool (`_SERIALIZE`), proven by `tests/test_concurrency.py`.

### F-PY-5. Config values for Frida scripts are injected by textual `var X = "";` replacement — **[code]** — **Status: fixed**

`frida_run_script` (dynamic.py:265-270) and `frida_find_bytes` (dynamic.py:553-563) patch values into JS via `str.replace`. Any apostrophe or quote in a user-provided search string breaks (or re-flows) the injected script, and the pattern depends on the script author remembering an exact `var SEARCH_STRING = "";` line. A message-passing config protocol (below) removes both hazards.

*Fix:* E-PY-6 (commit `a4e15e1`): parameters travel as `{'type':'config', …}` posted after load; the textual replacement is gone from `frida_run_script` and demoted to a documented fallback inside `frida_find_bytes`.

### F-PY-6. Dead weight in dependencies and checks — **[code]** — **Status: fixed**

- `quark-engine` is an optional extra **and** a check_tools entry, but no handler references it (grep: zero uses). Install cost ~200 MB for nothing. *(resolved by E-PY-3 `quark_scan`)*
- `capstone` and `keystone-engine` are checked in check_tools.py:211-212 but used by nothing. → **removed from the check list** (still installable via `install_tool` on demand)
- `fridump` is checked in check_tools.py:183 and installed by `--setup`, but `frida_memdump` deliberately does not use fridump (dynamic.py:450 comment: "does NOT require fridump"). → **removed from the check list and the install recipes**
- `_check_binary("medusa")` — see F-PY-2. → **disambiguated by running the binary and rejecting the foofus.net banner**

### F-PY-7. Assorted smaller items — **[code]** — **Status: fixed**

- `manifest_parse`'s `exported_services` filter is logically unrelated to services: `[s for s in apk.get_services() if apk.get_declared_permissions_dict()]` returns services whenever the APK declares **any** permission (static.py:246-248). → **fixed** by the XML-driven manifest rewrite (E-PY-2, commit `bec0bfc`).
- `mitm_export_har`'s helper script uses `datetime.utcnow()` (deprecated in 3.12+). → **fixed** (E-PY-9, commit `cc3e59e`).
- `frida_memdump` defaults its dump folder into `~/tools/dumps` — the tools-download dir doubles as output dir; `data_dir()/dumps` would be the right home. → **fixed** (E-PY-9).
- `adb_shell` runs `shlex.split(command)` then hands argv to `adb`, which rejoins them — device-side operators (`|`, `&&`) still work, but space-containing single arguments cannot be expressed; worth one line in docs. → **documented in the tool description** (E-PY-9).
- `install_all_missing_tools()` installs `medusa` from `core_tools` — coupled with F-PY-2, it would pip-install the cracker rather than the framework. → **fixed in-commit** during F-PY-2: `medusa` left the pip recipe path entirely (`_MANUAL_TOOLS` with instructions).

### F-PY-8. Things verified to work well — **[verified live]**

- `adb_devices`, `memory_read` (template + traversal-safe path), `apk_identify` (apkid 3.2.0 JSON), `find_urls` (20 URLs on TermuxBoot), `check_tools` inventory otherwise accurate.
- npm-side cross-check matched: `apk_manifest_analyzer` + `apk_permissions_checker` + `android_secrets_scanner` all returned consistent, clean output on the same APK.
- Pin hygiene in `install_tool.py` is solid: HTTPS-only fetch, SHA-256 verification, zip-slip rejection (all unit-tested, [test] tag from tests/test_handlers.py).

## Part 2 — npm server: findings (code-read; all paths under `src/`)

### F-NPM-1. Stale and non-hermetic smoke script — **Status: fixed**

`test-tools.mjs` is advertised by `package.json` (`npm run test:tools`) but: headers say "1/8 … 8/8" while 12 tools exist; it never calls `android_google_services`, `android_secrets_scanner`, `ios_google_services`, `ios_secrets_scanner`; and it requires `example.apk`/`example.ipa` in the repo root, which `.gitignore` excludes — it cannot run on a fresh clone. The real tests (`node --test "test/*.test.mjs"` in CI) cover only the manifest parser — 1 of 12 tools.

*Fix:* commit `90545cb`. The smoke runner now discovers the tool list from the server itself (14 today), calls every tool with a fixture recipe, skips the rest with a stated reason, and — without the fixture files — prints the full inventory plus the `npm test` pointer instead of failing. `npm test` (build + `node --test`) is now a first-class script, and the hermetic suite covers 14 tools with 25 test cases.

### F-NPM-2. Manifest analyzer ignores the `aapt2` fallback it already supports — **[code]** — **Status: fixed**

`apk_permissions_checker` tries `aapt` → `aapt2` → `apktool`; `apk_manifest_analyzer` tries `aapt` → apktool only, even though `parseManifest()` handles the aapt2 tree format and the repo ships the `test/fixtures/aapt2-xmltree.txt` proving it. On aapt2-only machines the manifest tool always pays the apktool cost.

*Fix:* `apk_manifest_analyzer` now walks the same `aapt` → `aapt2` → `apktool` chain (`aapt2 dump xmltree --file AndroidManifest.xml <apk>`), keeping the `Source:` label so the report still names which tool produced it. Verified live with a broken-`aapt` shim first on PATH: report comes out `Source: aapt2` with the full component analysis; with both healthy, `Source: aapt` (unchanged). The existing fixture tests already cover aapt2 tree parsing on both formats.

### F-NPM-3. Triple-duplicated iOS binary-extraction logic — **[code]** — **Status: fixed**

`extractBinary` is copy-pasted three times with **drifting resource-exclusion lists** (entitlements-checker.ts vs binary-strings.ts vs secrets-scanner.ts — one ignores `lproj`/`storyboard`, another `json`/`dylib`), so the same IPA can yield different binaries to different tools. `merge()` is likewise duplicated in both secret scanners, and unchanged-file dedup uses `includes()` (O(n²)). One shared helper fixes all three.

*Fix:* `src/tools/ios/extract-binary.ts` is the single implementation — `resolveBinaryEntry` (Info.plist `CFBundleExecutable`, else the one extension-less root file of the `.app`, against the **union** of the three drifted exclusion lists), `writeBinary` (used by binary-strings + entitlements-checker; the pointless `chmodSync(0o755)` disappears with it) and `readBinary` (secrets-scanner). `merge()` became `mergeScanResults` in `shared/patterns.ts`, used by both secret scanners, with Set-based dedup instead of `includes()`. Tests: `test/ios-extract.test.mjs` (6 cases: named binary, fallback, union-list exclusions, null case, write/read round-trip, merge dedup).

### F-NPM-4. No decompression-size limits (zip-bomb surface) — **[code]** — **Status: fixed**

`entry.getData()` (adm-zip) fully decompresses before any size check — for DEX, plists, assets, framework binaries. maxBuffer only caps `strings` output. A crafted, small, highly-compressed IPA can OOM the process. There is also no cap on the input APK/IPA file size itself.

*Fix:* `src/tools/shared/zip.ts` is the single zip gateway: `openZip` (checks the input against `MOBILE_RE_MCP_MAX_FILE_MB`, default 2048, then opens with a normalized error — also fixing the one unprotected `new AdmZip` in frameworks-detector), `readEntry` (checks `header.compressedSize`/`header.size` against `MOBILE_RE_MCP_MAX_ENTRY_MB`, default 256, *before* decompressing), `requireEntryData` for single-entry callers, and a `[skipped: …]` placeholder for scan loops. `0` disables a cap. Every APK/IPA consumer is wired through it. Verified live: a 2 KB APK whose `assets/big.json` decompresses to 2 MB is reported as `[skipped: entry 'assets/big.json' declares 2.0 MB uncompressed, above the 1 MB cap …]` with the rest of the scan intact; a 2 MB input with `MOBILE_RE_MCP_MAX_FILE_MB=1` fails with `input file is 2.0 MB, above the 1 MB cap`. Tests: `test/zip-limits.test.mjs` (6 cases).

### F-NPM-5. Other smaller items — **Status: partially fixed** (each bullet below)

- `ios_frameworks_detector` has an unprotected `new AdmZip(...)` (frameworks-detector.ts:132) — the only zip access not wrapped in try/catch, so a valid-magic/corrupt IPA throws past the repo's error normalization. Also `DexGuard` (an Android obfuscator) sits in the iOS `KNOWN_FRAMEWORKS` table, and matching uses loose `startsWith || includes`, so names like "Segment", "Branch" or "Realm" inside unrelated frameworks can mislabel. **[code]** → *both fixed:* the unprotected open is wrapped by the zip gateway (F-NPM-4, commit `daa3e4b`); DexGuard is removed and the matcher is prefix-or-exact only (commit `90545cb`).
- `min_length` default is 6 for `ios_binary_strings` but 8 for both secret scanners — same operation family, different defaults. **[code]** → *fixed* (commit `90545cb`: 8 everywhere).
- `ios_google_services` skips binary plists during pattern rescan (`bplist` → continue) while `ios_secrets_scanner` decodes those same plists through `plutil` — inconsistent findings between two tools over the same files. **[code]** → *deferred (reason:* behavioral change needing binary-plist fixtures to prove; the tools' reports are independently labeled, so no finding is *hidden* — follow-up candidate*).*
- `android_api_extractor` claims OkHttp endpoint extraction but collects only `Lokhttp3/` *field declarations*; no URLs come from it — only Retrofit annotations produce endpoints (api-extractor.ts:80-93). **[code]** → *deferred to E-NPM-5 (reason:* not in the approved extension order for this round; the const-string harvest proposal stands — README wording already narrows the claim*).*
- Dead code: `p.startsWith("{") ? p : p` (api-extractor.ts:168-169); pointless `chmodSync(0o755)` on the extracted iOS binary (entitlements-checker.ts:127); string-sentinel control flow `Record|null|"simulator"` (entitlements-checker). → *dead ternary and chmod fixed* (commits `90545cb` / `0925a77`); *sentinel wontfix (reason:* internal three-state used by exactly one caller — reshaping it is churn without a behavior change*).*
- Android `DANGEROUS_PERMISSIONS` includes `ACCESS_WIFI_STATE` / `CHANGE_WIFI_STATE`, which are install-time "normal" permissions, plus signature-type `INSTALL_PACKAGES` — defensible as a triage list, but mislabeled against Google's taxonomy. **[code]** → *fixed in-commit* (`cc3e59e`: the set keeps triage semantics under a renamed "Sensitive Permissions" header with the taxonomy note in the source).
- `/[0-9a-zA-Z]{40}/g` in `ios_binary_strings` labels every 40-char alnum run a key — noisy on real apps. **[code]** → *deferred (reason:* tightening risks *missing* real 40-char keys; noise is labeled LOW risk and capped — safer to leave*).*
- Windows `apktool.bat` support is prose-only; `execFileSync("apktool", …)` fails with ENOENT and offers no hint at runtime. **[code]** → *fixed* (commit `90545cb`: `run()` converts bare ENOENT into "not found on PATH" with the Windows .exe-vs-.bat note).

### F-NPM-6. Verified working end-to-end — **[verified live]**

Manifest analyzer, permissions checker and secrets scanner all produced clean, correct output on a real 3-DEX APK through the live MCP server. Output conventions (`=== Header ===`, `⚠`, `✓`, severity tags) are uniform across all 12 tools.
