```py
async def _run_tool(
    name: str,
    arguments: dict,
    dispatch: dict[str, Callable[..., object]],
    serial_pools: dict[int, ThreadPoolExecutor],
) -> CallToolResult:
    """Resolve and execute one tool call without blocking the event loop.

    * guard refusals → isError CallToolResult (never raised)
    * async handlers are awaited directly
    * sync handlers of stateless classes run on the default executor
      (``asyncio.to_thread``) — concurrent calls overlap freely
    * sync handlers of classes flagged ``_SERIALIZE`` (Dynamic/Network/
      Device: they own a Frida session, mitm process or logcat reader) run
      on a per-instance single-worker pool, so a second call queues
      instead of racing the first on shared state — same observable
      ordering as the old synchronous dispatch, minus the block
    """
    try:
        args = guard.validate(name, arguments)
    except guard.GuardError as exc:
        return CallToolResult(
            content=[TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps(
                {"status": "error", "tool": name, "error": f"refused: {exc}"}, indent=2))],
            isError=True,
        )

    handler = dispatch.get(name)
    if handler is None:
        result = {
            "status": "error",
            "tool": name,
            "error": f"Unknown tool: {name}",
        }
    else:
        try:
            if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(handler):
                result = await handler(args)
            else:
                bound_self = getattr(handler, "__self__", None)
                if getattr(bound_self, "_SERIALIZE", False):
                    pool = serial_pools.get(id(bound_self))
                    if pool is None:
                        pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(
                            max_workers=1, thread_name_prefix="mobile-re-serial"
                        )
                        serial_pools[id(bound_self)] = pool
                    result = await asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(
                        pool, handler, args
                    )
                else:
                    result = await asyncio.to_thread(handler, args)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            logger.exception("Tool %s raised an exception", name)
            result = {
                "status": "error",
                "tool": name,
                "error": str(exc),
            }

    return CallToolResult(
        content=[TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps(result, indent=2))]
    )


def create_server() -> Server:
    """Build and return a configured MCP Server instance."""

    server = Server("android-re-mcp", version=__version__)

    # Instantiate stateful handlers
    static = StaticHandler()
    apkdiff = ApkDiffHandler()
    apiextractor = ApiExtractorHandler()
    googleservices = GoogleServicesHandler()
    dynamic = DynamicHandler()
    rasp = RaspHandler()
    device = DeviceHandler()
    network = NetworkHandler()
    signing = SigningHandler()
    memory = MemoryHandler()
    native = NativeHandler()
    flutter = FlutterHandler()
    sosec = SoSecHandler()
    dex = DexHandler()
    apkops = ApkOpsHandler()
    patcher = PatcherHandler()

    # Dispatch table: tool_name → callable(args) → dict
    _dispatch: dict[str, object] = {
        # static
        "apk_decompile": static.apk_decompile,
        "apk_decompile_java": static.apk_decompile_java,
        "apk_identify": static.apk_identify,
        "apk_scan_secrets": static.apk_scan_secrets,
        "apk_analyze_full": static.apk_analyze_full,
        "apk_diff": apkdiff.apk_diff,
        "android_api_extractor": apiextractor.android_api_extractor,
        "android_google_services": googleservices.android_google_services,
        "quark_scan": static.quark_scan,
        "manifest_parse": static.manifest_parse,
        "search_strings": static.search_strings,
        # dynamic (original)
        "frida_spawn": dynamic.frida_spawn,
        "frida_attach": dynamic.frida_attach,
        "frida_inject": dynamic.frida_inject,
        "frida_read_output": dynamic.frida_read_output,
        "frida_detach": dynamic.frida_detach,
        "frida_status": dynamic.frida_status,
        "objection_run": dynamic.objection_run,
        # dynamic — script library
        "frida_list_scripts": dynamic.frida_list_scripts,
        "frida_get_script": dynamic.frida_get_script,
        "frida_run_script": dynamic.frida_run_script,
        # dynamic — hluda / anti-detection
        "frida_spawn_hluda": dynamic.frida_spawn_hluda,
        "frida_server_push": dynamic.frida_server_push,
        # dynamic — memory operations
        "frida_memdump": dynamic.frida_memdump,
        "frida_find_bytes": dynamic.frida_find_bytes,
        # rasp
        "rasp_identify": rasp.rasp_identify,
        "rasp_bypass": rasp.rasp_bypass,
        # device
        "adb_devices": device.adb_devices,
        "adb_shell": device.adb_shell,
        "adb_install": device.adb_install,
        "adb_pull": device.adb_pull,
        "adb_push": device.adb_push,
        "adb_logcat_start": device.adb_logcat_start,
        "adb_logcat_read": device.adb_logcat_read,
        "adb_logcat_stop": device.adb_logcat_stop,
        "hermes_decode": device.hermes_decode,
        "scrcpy_start": device.scrcpy_start,
        "adb_ui_dump": device.adb_ui_dump,
        "scrcpy_screenshot": device.scrcpy_screenshot,
        # network
        "mitm_start": network.mitm_start,
        "mitm_stop": network.mitm_stop,
        "ssl_kill_switch": network.ssl_kill_switch,
        # signing
        "apk_sign": signing.apk_sign,
        "apk_rebuild_sign": signing.apk_rebuild_sign,
        # memory
        "memory_read": memory.memory_read,
        "memory_write": memory.memory_write,
        # static — deep androguard (Gap #7)
        "analyze_code": static.analyze_code,
        "find_crypto_usage": static.find_crypto_usage,
        "find_urls": static.find_urls,
        # native (Gap #1 + #8)
        "native_strings": native.native_strings,
        "native_exports": native.native_exports,
        "native_disasm": native.native_disasm,
        "il2cpp_dump": native.il2cpp_dump,
        # native ELF security & code search (E-PY-16)
        "so_xrefs": sosec.so_xrefs,
        "rop_gadgets": sosec.rop_gadgets,
        "elf_checksec": sosec.elf_checksec,
        "native_crypto_constants": sosec.native_crypto_constants,
        "syscall_lookup": sosec.syscall_lookup,
        "native_map_address": sosec.native_map_address,
        "native_patch_string": sosec.native_patch_string,
        "native_patch_instructions": sosec.native_patch_instructions,
        # dex surgery (E-PY-17)
        "dex_info": dex.dex_info,
        "dex_extract": dex.dex_extract,
        "dex_convert": dex.dex_convert,
        "dex_patch": dex.dex_patch,
        "dex_assemble": dex.dex_assemble,
        "dex_split": dex.dex_split,
        "dex_swap": dex.dex_swap,
        "dex_read_class_outline": dex.dex_read_class_outline,
        "dex_read_pseudocode": dex.dex_read_pseudocode,
        "dex_validate": dex.dex_validate,
        "dex_merge": dex.dex_merge,
        # MT-MCP adoption: apk/zip surgery, signatures, resources, build checks
        "apk_read_signature": apkops.apk_read_signature,
        "zip_test": apkops.zip_test,
        "zip_extract": apkops.zip_extract,
        "zip_update": apkops.zip_update,
        "apk_build_check": apkops.apk_build_check,
        "resource_table_list": apkops.resource_table_list,
        "resource_read": apkops.resource_read,
        "resource_xref": apkops.resource_xref,
        # flutter (Gap #2)
        "flutter_version": flutter.flutter_version,
        "dart_snapshot_info": flutter.dart_snapshot_info,
        "blutter_extract": flutter.blutter_extract,
        # network — traffic reading (Gap #4)
        "mitm_read_flows": network.mitm_read_flows,
        "mitm_export_har": network.mitm_export_har,
        # patcher (Gap #6)
        "smali_patch": patcher.smali_patch,
        "inject_gadget": patcher.inject_gadget,
        # setup
        "check_tools": lambda _args: check_all_tools(),
        "install_tool": lambda args: _install_tool(args.get("tool_name", "")),
    }
    # One single-worker executor per stateful handler instance (F-PY-4):
    # dynamic (Frida session), network (mitm process), device (logcat).
    _serial_pools: dict[int, ThreadPoolExecutor] = {}

    # ── List tools ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @server.list_tools()
    async def list_tools() -> ListToolsResult:
        tools = [
            Tool(
                name=s["name"],
                description=s["description"],
                inputSchema=s["inputSchema"],
            )
            for s in TOOL_SCHEMAS
            if s["name"] not in guard.disabled_tools()
        ]
        return ListToolsResult(tools=tools)

    # ── Call tool ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @server.call_tool()
    async def call_tool(name: str, arguments: dict) -> CallToolResult:
        return await _run_tool(name, arguments, _dispatch, _serial_pools)

    # ── List resources ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @server.list_resources()
    async def list_resources() -> ListResourcesResult:
        resources = [
            Resource(uri=uri, name=filename, description=desc, mimeType="text/markdown")
            for uri, filename, desc in RESOURCE_DEFS
        ]
        return ListResourcesResult(resources=resources)

    # ── Read resource ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @server.read_resource()
    async def read_resource(uri) -> str:
        uri = str(uri)
        match = next(
            ((u, f, d) for u, f, d in RESOURCE_DEFS if u == uri),
            None,
        )
        if match is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown resource URI: {uri}")
        _uri, filename, _desc = match
        path = KNOWLEDGE_DIR / filename
        if not path.exists():
            text = f"# {filename}\n\n_Content not yet available._\n"
        else:
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        return text

    # ── List prompts ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @server.list_prompts()
    async def list_prompts() -> ListPromptsResult:
        prompts = [
            Prompt(name=name, description=desc)
            for name, desc, _file in PROMPT_DEFS
        ]
        return ListPromptsResult(prompts=prompts)

    # ── Get prompt ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @server.get_prompt()
    async def get_prompt(name: str, arguments: dict | None) -> GetPromptResult:
        match = next((p for p in PROMPT_DEFS if p[0] == name), None)
        if match is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown prompt: {name}")
        _name, desc, filename = match
        path = KNOWLEDGE_DIR / filename
        if path.exists():
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        else:
            text = f"# {name}\n\n_Prompt not yet implemented._\n"

        return GetPromptResult(
            description=desc,
            messages=[
                PromptMessage(
                    role="user",
                    content=TextContent(type="text", text=text),
                )
            ],
        )

    # ── SSE helper ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    async def run_stdio() -> None:
        from mcp.server.stdio import stdio_server

        async with stdio_server() as (read_stream, write_stream):
            await server.run(
                read_stream,
                write_stream,
                server.create_initialization_options(),
            )

    async def run_sse(host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 8765) -> None:
        import hmac
        import os

        import uvicorn
        from mcp.server.sse import SseServerTransport
        from starlette.applications import Starlette
        from starlette.responses import PlainTextResponse, Response
        from starlette.routing import Mount, Route

        token = os.environ.get("ANDROID_RE_MCP_TOKEN", "")
        loopback = host in ("127.0.0.1", "::1", "localhost")
        if not loopback and not token:
            raise SystemExit(
                f"Refusing to listen on {host} without ANDROID_RE_MCP_TOKEN. "
                "This server can run adb and Frida commands."
            )

        try:
            from mcp.server.transport_security import TransportSecuritySettings

            hosts = ["127.0.0.1:*", "localhost:*", "[::1]:*"] + ([] if loopback else [f"{host}:*"])
            sse = SseServerTransport(
                "/messages/",
                security_settings=TransportSecuritySettings(
                    enable_dns_rebinding_protection=True,
                    allowed_hosts=hosts,
                    allowed_origins=["http://127.0.0.1:*", "http://localhost:*"],
                ),
            )
        except ImportError:
            sse = SseServerTransport("/messages/")

        async def handle_sse(request):  # noqa: ANN001
            async with sse.connect_sse(
                request.scope, request.receive, request._send  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
            ) as streams:
                await server.run(
                    streams[0], streams[1], server.create_initialization_options()
                )
            return Response()

        class BearerAuth:
            def __init__(self, app) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001
                self.app = app

            async def __call__(self, scope, receive, send) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001
                if token and scope["type"] == "http":
                    sent = dict(scope["headers"]).get(b"authorization", b"").decode()
                    if not hmac.compare_digest(sent, f"Bearer {token}"):
                        await PlainTextResponse("unauthorized", status_code=401)(scope, receive, send)
                        return
                await self.app(scope, receive, send)

        app = BearerAuth(
            Starlette(
                routes=[
                    Route("/sse", endpoint=handle_sse),
                    Mount("/messages/", app=sse.handle_post_message),
                ]
            )
        )
        config = uvicorn.Config(app, host=host, port=port, log_level="warning")
        await uvicorn.Server(config).serve()

    # Attach transport helpers to the server object so __main__ can call them
    server.run_stdio = run_stdio  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    server.run_sse = run_sse  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

    return server
```

`python/src/android_re_mcp/setup/check_tools.py`:

```py
"""
setup/check_tools.py — Verify all required tools are available.

Can be run standalone:
    python -m android_re_mcp.setup.check_tools

Returns structured JSON per tool so the MCP check_tools() tool
and the TUI dashboard both use identical data.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

from android_re_mcp.clitools import find_cli


@dataclass
class ToolStatus:
    name: str
    kind: str                   # "binary" | "python" | "java_jar" | "npm"
    available: bool
    version: Optional[str] = None
    path: Optional[str] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None
    install_hint: str = ""
    used_by: Optional[list[str]] = None   # MCP tool names that invoke this entry

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "name": self.name,
            "kind": self.kind,
            "available": self.available,
            "version": self.version,
            "path": self.path,
            "error": self.error,
            "install_hint": self.install_hint,
            "used_by": self.used_by or [],
        }


# Every MCP tool whose handler needs dexfile-cli.jar. dex_swap is pure Python
# and dex_read_pseudocode uses jadx, so neither belongs here.
_DEXFILE_CLI_TOOLS = [
    "dex_info",
    "dex_extract",
    "dex_convert",
    "dex_patch",
    "dex_assemble",
    "dex_split",
    "dex_read_class_outline",
    "dex_validate",
    "dex_merge",
]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Individual checkers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _check_binary(
    name: str,
    version_flag: str = "--version",
    hint: str = "",
    kind: str = "binary",
    used_by: Optional[list[str]] = None,
) -> ToolStatus:
    """Check a CLI by running it with a version flag.

    Resolution goes through android_re_mcp.clitools.find_cli — the exact
    lookup the handlers use — so a console script living next to the
    interpreter counts just as much as one on PATH.
    """
    from android_re_mcp.clitools import find_cli

    used_by = used_by or []
    path = find_cli(name)
    if path is None:
        return ToolStatus(
            name=name, kind=kind, available=False, used_by=used_by,
            error=f"'{name}' not found on PATH (or next to the interpreter)",
            install_hint=hint,
        )
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            [path, version_flag], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10,
        )
        lines = (result.stdout or result.stderr).strip().splitlines()
        version = lines[0].strip() if lines else "unknown"
        return ToolStatus(name=name, kind=kind, available=True, version=version, path=path, used_by=used_by)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return ToolStatus(name=name, kind=kind, available=True, version="timeout", path=path, used_by=used_by)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        return ToolStatus(name=name, kind=kind, available=True, path=path, error=str(exc), used_by=used_by)


def _check_python_module(
    name: str,
    import_name: Optional[str] = None,
    hint: str = "",
    used_by: Optional[list[str]] = None,
) -> ToolStatus:
    """Check a Python importable module."""
    used_by = used_by or []
    mod_name = import_name or name.replace("-", "_")
    try:
        mod = importlib.import_module(mod_name)
        version = getattr(mod, "__version__", None) or getattr(mod, "VERSION", "installed")
        return ToolStatus(name=name, kind="python", available=True, version=str(version), used_by=used_by)
    except ImportError as exc:
        return ToolStatus(
            name=name, kind="python", available=False, used_by=used_by,
            error=str(exc), install_hint=hint or f"pip install {name}",
        )


def _check_medusa(used_by: Optional[list[str]] = None) -> ToolStatus:
    """Check for the Medusa RE framework, refusing the SSH-cracker namesake.

    Two unrelated tools are called 'medusa': the well-known SSH login
    cracker from foofus.net (the one usually on PATH) and Ch0pin's Frida
    script framework. The cracker's banner always identifies itself, so a
    run is the reliable disambiguator.
    """
    used_by = used_by or []
    from android_re_mcp.clitools import find_cli

    cli = find_cli("medusa")
    if cli is None:
        return ToolStatus(
            name="medusa", kind="binary", available=False, used_by=used_by,
            error="'medusa' not found on PATH",
            install_hint="RE framework: pip install 'git+https://github.com/Ch0pin/medusa' "
            "(do NOT install the SSH cracker of the same name)",
        )
    try:
        probe = subprocess.run([cli, "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
        banner = (probe.stdout or probe.stderr).strip().lower()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        banner = ""
    if "foofus" in banner:
        return ToolStatus(
            name="medusa", kind="binary", available=False, path=cli, used_by=used_by,
            error="the 'medusa' on PATH is the SSH login cracker from foofus.net, "
            "not the Medusa RE framework this suite expects",
            install_hint="Get the framework from https://github.com/Ch0pin/medusa, "
            "or remove/rename the cracker to stop the name collision",
        )
    version = (banner or "installed").splitlines()[0]
    return ToolStatus(
        name="medusa", kind="binary", available=True, version=version, path=cli, used_by=used_by,
    )


def _check_java_jar(
    display_name: str,
    jar_path_str: str,
    used_by: Optional[list[str]] = None,
    hint: str = "",
    java_hint: str = "",
) -> ToolStatus:
    """Check a Java JAR is present and java is available.

    ``hint`` and ``java_hint`` let each jar describe its own download and Java
    requirement; the uber-apk-signer defaults are not correct for every jar
    (dexfile-cli needs Java 17+, not 11+).
    """
    used_by = used_by or []
    java_path = shutil.which("java")
    if java_path is None:
        return ToolStatus(
            name=display_name, kind="java_jar", available=False, used_by=used_by,
            error="java not found on PATH — required to run the jar",
            install_hint=java_hint or "Install JDK 11+ and ensure java is on PATH",
        )
    jar_path = Path(jar_path_str)
    if jar_path.exists():
        return ToolStatus(name=display_name, kind="java_jar", available=True, path=str(jar_path), used_by=used_by)
    return ToolStatus(
        name=display_name, kind="java_jar", available=False, used_by=used_by,
        error=f"JAR not found at '{jar_path_str}'",
        install_hint=hint or (
            "Download from https://github.com/patrickfav/uber-apk-signer/releases "
            "and update [signing].jar_path in config.toml  OR  run setup.sh"
        ),
    )


def _check_file(display_name: str, paths: list[str], kind: str = "binary", hint: str = "",
                used_by: Optional[list[str]] = None) -> ToolStatus:
    """Check that at least one file path from *paths* exists."""
    used_by = used_by or []
    for p in paths:
        if Path(p).exists():
            return ToolStatus(name=display_name, kind=kind, available=True, path=p, used_by=used_by)
    return ToolStatus(
        name=display_name, kind=kind, available=False, used_by=used_by,
        error=f"Not found at: {paths[0]}",
        install_hint=hint,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Config helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _get_config_signing() -> dict:
    from android_re_mcp.config import load_config, signer_jar

    cfg = dict(load_config().get("signing", {}))
    cfg["jar_path"] = str(signer_jar())
    return cfg


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tool registry
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def check_all_tools() -> dict:
    """
    Check all required / optional tools.

    Return shape:
    {
        "status": "ok" | "degraded" | "error",
        "summary": {"total": N, "available": N, "missing": N},
        "tools": { "<name>": { ToolStatus dict } }
    }
    """
    cfg = _get_config_signing()
    jar_path = cfg.get("jar_path", "uber-apk-signer.jar")

    from android_re_mcp.paths import tools_dir as _tools_dir

    tools_dir = _tools_dir()

    # Frida version for device binary paths
    frida_version: str | None = None
    _frida_cli = find_cli("frida")
    if _frida_cli:
        try:
            r = subprocess.run([_frida_cli, "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
            frida_version = r.stdout.strip()
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            pass

    frida_server_paths = [str(tools_dir / "frida-server")]
    frida_gadget_paths = list(tools_dir.glob("gadgets/frida-gadget-*.so")) if tools_dir.exists() else []

    checks: list[ToolStatus] = [
        # ── Core static analysis ───────────────────────────────────────────
        _check_binary("apktool", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install apktool yourself",
                      used_by=["apk_decompile", "inject_gadget", "apk_rebuild_sign"]),
        _check_binary("jadx", "--version", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install jadx yourself",
                      used_by=["apk_decompile_java"]),
        _check_binary("apkid", "--version", kind="python", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install apkid yourself",
                      used_by=["apk_identify", "apk_analyze_full", "rasp_identify", "rasp_bypass"]),
        _check_binary("apkleaks", "--version", kind="python", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install apkleaks yourself",
                      used_by=["apk_scan_secrets", "apk_analyze_full"]),
        _check_python_module("androguard", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install androguard yourself",
                             used_by=["manifest_parse", "analyze_code", "find_crypto_usage",
                                      "find_urls", "apk_analyze_full"]),
        _check_python_module("quark-engine", "quark", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install quark-engine yourself",
                             used_by=["quark_scan", "apk_analyze_full"]),
        _check_binary("rg", "--version", hint="Manual install required (ripgrep)",
                      used_by=["search_strings"]),
        _check_python_module("capstone", hint="pip install capstone (the android-re-mcp[native] extra)",
                             used_by=["so_xrefs", "rop_gadgets"]),

        # ── Dynamic instrumentation ────────────────────────────────────────
        _check_python_module("frida", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install frida yourself",
                             used_by=["frida_spawn", "frida_attach", "frida_inject", "frida_detach",
                                      "frida_status", "frida_memdump", "frida_find_bytes",
                                      "ssl_kill_switch"]),
        _check_binary("frida", "--version", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install frida-tools yourself",
                      used_by=["frida_server_push", "frida_spawn_hluda"]),
        _check_binary("objection", "--version", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install objection yourself",
                      used_by=["objection_run"]),

        # ── Device binaries on device (optional — need to be pushed) ──────
        _check_file(
            "frida-server (host binary)",
            frida_server_paths,
            hint=f"Extract matching frida-server-{frida_version or '<ver>'} into ~/tools/",
            used_by=["frida_server_push", "frida_spawn_hluda"],
        ),
        ToolStatus(
            name="frida-gadget",
            kind="binary",
            available=bool(frida_gadget_paths),
            path=str(frida_gadget_paths[0]) if frida_gadget_paths else None,
            error=None if frida_gadget_paths else f"No frida-gadget .so found in {tools_dir}/gadgets/",
            install_hint="Manual frida-gadget download required",
            used_by=["inject_gadget"],
        ),

        # ── Device control ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
        _check_binary("adb", "version", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install adb yourself",
                      used_by=["adb_devices", "adb_shell", "adb_install", "adb_pull", "adb_push",
                               "adb_logcat_start", "adb_logcat_read", "adb_logcat_stop",
                               "adb_ui_dump", "scrcpy_screenshot", "frida_server_push",
                               "frida_spawn_hluda"]),

        # ── Network ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        _check_binary("mitmdump", "--version", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install mitmproxy yourself",
                      used_by=["mitm_start", "mitm_stop", "mitm_read_flows", "mitm_export_har"]),

        # ── Binary analysis / RE (optional) ───────────────────────────────
        _check_binary("r2", "--version", hint="Manual install required",
                      used_by=["native_disasm"]),

        # ── Signing & JAR tools ────────────────────────────────────────────
        _check_java_jar("uber-apk-signer", jar_path, used_by=["apk_sign", "apk_rebuild_sign", "inject_gadget"]),
        _check_java_jar(
            "dexfile-cli",
            str(tools_dir / "dexfile-cli.jar"),
            used_by=_DEXFILE_CLI_TOOLS,
            hint=(
                "Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install_tool dexfile-cli "
                "(https://github.com/FlyPhantomFly/dexfile-cli/releases); Java 17+ required"
            ),
            java_hint="Install JDK 17+ (dexfile-cli requires Java 17+) and ensure java is on PATH",
        ),
        _check_file(
            "smali.jar", [str(tools_dir / "smali.jar")],
            hint="apktool bundles smali; standalone jars are on Maven Central (com.android.tools.smali)",
            used_by=[],
        ),
        _check_file(
            "baksmali.jar", [str(tools_dir / "baksmali.jar")],
            hint="apktool bundles baksmali; standalone jars are on Maven Central (com.android.tools.smali)",
            used_by=[],
        ),
        _check_binary("Il2CppDumper", hint="Run android-re-mcp --setup, or install il2cppdumper yourself",
                      used_by=["il2cpp_dump"]),

        # ── Test keystore ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
        _check_file(
            "test keystore",
            [str(tools_dir / "signing" / "test.jks"), str(tools_dir / "signing" / "test.keystore")],
            hint="keytool -genkey ...",
            used_by=["apk_sign", "apk_rebuild_sign"],
        ),

        # ── Dynamic frameworks (optional) ─────────────────────────────────
        _check_medusa(),

        # ── MCP SDK ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        _check_python_module("mcp", hint="pip install 'mcp>=1.30,<2'"),

        # ── Runtimes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        _check_binary("java", "-version", hint="Install JDK 21+ from https://adoptium.net/",
                      used_by=["apk_sign", "apk_rebuild_sign", "inject_gadget", "il2cpp_dump", "blutter_extract"]),
        _check_binary("node", "--version", hint="Download from https://nodejs.org/",
                      used_by=["install_tool"]),
        _check_binary("npm", "--version", hint="Bundled with Node.js",
                      used_by=["install_tool"]),
    ]

    tools_dict = {s.name: s.to_dict() for s in checks}
    available = sum(1 for s in checks if s.available)
    missing = len(checks) - available
    overall = "ok" if missing == 0 else ("degraded" if available > 0 else "error")

    return {
        "status": overall,
        "summary": {"total": len(checks), "available": available, "missing": missing},
        "tools": tools_dict,
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Standalone entry point
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if __name__ == "__main__":
    result = check_all_tools()
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))

    summary = result["summary"]
    print(
        f"\n[check_tools] {summary['available']}/{summary['total']} tools available "
        f"({summary['missing']} missing)",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    if result["status"] != "ok":
        missing_tools = [name for name, info in result["tools"].items() if not info["available"]]
        print(f"[check_tools] Missing: {', '.join(missing_tools)}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("[check_tools] Run setup.sh to install all tools in one step.", file=sys.stderr)
```

`python/src/android_re_mcp/setup/install_tool.py`:

```py
"""
setup/install_tool.py — Downloads helper tools into ~/tools (or $ANDROID_RE_MCP_TOOLS_DIR).

Every download is pinned to a release and checked against a SHA-256 before it is used.
The install_tool MCP tool is off unless ANDROID_RE_MCP_ALLOW_INSTALL=1; `android-re-mcp --setup` always works.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from android_re_mcp.paths import tools_dir

_APKTOOL = "2.12.1"

# name -> (url, sha256). Hashes were taken from the upstream release files on 2026-11-02.
_PINNED: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {
    "apktool.jar": (
        f"https://github.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/releases/download/v{_APKTOOL}/apktool_{_APKTOOL}.jar",
        "66cf4524a4a45a7f56567d08b2c9b6ec237bcdd78cee69fd4a59c8a0243aeafa",
    ),
    "apktool.sh": (
        f"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/v{_APKTOOL}/scripts/linux/apktool",
        "493a9c98df968a25c373ca9df871ca77730c82954be4959b74e90adaf91a0e77",
    ),
    "apktool.bat": (
        f"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iBotPeaches/Apktool/v{_APKTOOL}/scripts/windows/apktool.bat",
        "b27150908edde47533463e4a3cc518541b253b2a7bf16f21d0df33646afce8d3",
    ),
    "jadx.zip": (
        "https://github.com/skylot/jadx/releases/download/v1.5.6/jadx-1.5.6.zip",
        "545ea2be9c242511bc145755cf4bda2485ade42966e096f8b4d3da2a230e8974",
    ),
    "uber-apk-signer.jar": (

class DownloadError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def _fetch(url: str):
    if not url.startswith("https://"):
        raise DownloadError(f"refusing non-https URL: {url}")
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "android-re-mcp"})
    return urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120)  # noqa: S310 (https enforced above)


def _download(key: str, dest: Path) -> None:
    """Download a pinned file to *dest*, keeping it only if the SHA-256 matches."""
    url, expected = _PINNED[key]
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=dest.parent, prefix=".download-")
    tmp = Path(tmp_name)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as out, _fetch(url) as resp:
            for chunk in iter(lambda: resp.read(1 << 20), b""):
                digest.update(chunk)
                out.write(chunk)
        if digest.hexdigest() != expected:
            raise DownloadError(
                f"SHA-256 mismatch for {url}: expected {expected}, got {digest.hexdigest()}"
            )
        os.replace(tmp, dest)
    finally:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def _extract_zip(zip_path: Path, dest_dir: Path) -> None:
    dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    root = dest_dir.resolve()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        for member in z.infolist():
            target = (root / member.filename).resolve()
            if root != target and root not in target.parents:
                raise DownloadError(f"unsafe path in archive: {member.filename}")
        z.extractall(root)


def _download_zip(key: str, dest_dir: Path) -> None:
    dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    zip_path = dest_dir / ".archive.zip"
    try:
        _download(key, zip_path)
        _extract_zip(zip_path, dest_dir)
    finally:
        zip_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def _make_executable(path: Path) -> None:
    if os.name != "nt":
        os.chmod(path, 0o755)


def _result(fn) -> dict:
    try:
        return fn()
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"status": "error", "error": str(exc)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Binary downloaders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _install_apktool() -> dict:
    def run() -> dict:
        td = tools_dir()
        _download("apktool.jar", td / "apktool.jar")
        if os.name == "nt":
            _download("apktool.bat", td / "apktool.bat")
        else:
            _download("apktool.sh", td / "apktool")
            _make_executable(td / "apktool")
        return {"status": "ok", "message": f"apktool {_APKTOOL} installed and verified"}

    return _result(run)


def _install_jadx() -> dict:
    def run() -> dict:
        target = tools_dir() / "jadx"
        if target.exists():
            shutil.rmtree(target)
        _download_zip("jadx.zip", target)
        if os.name != "nt":
            _make_executable(target / "bin" / "jadx")
        return {"status": "ok", "message": "jadx 1.5.6 installed and verified"}

    return _result(run)

# pip / npm

def _frida_constraints() -> str | None:
    """Pin whatever Frida is installed now, so installing objection and friends can't move it."""
    pins = []
    for dist in ("frida", "frida-tools"):
        try:
            pins.append(f"{dist}=={importlib.metadata.version(dist)}")
        except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
            continue
    if not pins:
        return None
    fd, name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="frida-constraints-", suffix=".txt")
    with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(pins) + "\n")
    return name


def _pip_install(display_name: str, package: str) -> dict:
    constraints = _frida_constraints()
    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", package]
    if constraints:
        cmd[4:4] = ["-c", constraints]
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
        if proc.returncode == 0:
            return {"status": "ok", "message": f"Installed {package} into {sys.prefix}"}
        return {"status": "error", "error": (proc.stderr or proc.stdout)[-2000:]}
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"status": "error", "error": str(exc)}
    finally:
        if constraints:
            Path(constraints).unlink(missing_ok=True)


def _npm_install(display_name: str, package: str) -> dict:
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(["npm", "install", "-g", package], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
        if proc.returncode == 0:
            return {"status": "ok", "message": f"npm installed {package}"}
        return {"status": "error", "error": (proc.stderr or proc.stdout)[-2000:]}
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"status": "error", "error": str(exc)}


def _install_dexfile_cli() -> dict:
    def run() -> dict:
        td = tools_dir()
        _download("dexfile-cli.jar", td / "dexfile-cli.jar")
        return {"status": "ok", "message": "dexfile-cli 0.1.9 installed and verified "
                "(java 17+ required on PATH; see https://github.com/FlyPhantomFly/dexfile-cli)"}

    return _result(run)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Routing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_BINARY_INSTALLERS = {
    "apktool": _install_apktool,
    "jadx": _install_jadx,
    "uber-apk-signer": _install_uber_apk_signer,
    "il2cppdumper": _install_il2cppdumper,
    "adb": _install_adb,
    "scrcpy": _install_scrcpy,
    "dexfile-cli": _install_dexfile_cli,
}


def install_tool(tool_name: str) -> dict:
    """Install *tool_name* from a pinned download, pip, or npm."""
    if tool_name in _BINARY_INSTALLERS:
        return _BINARY_INSTALLERS[tool_name]()

    if tool_name in ("smali", "baksmali"):
        return {
            "status": "manual_required",
            "message": "apktool already bundles smali/baksmali. Standalone jars are on Maven Central (com.android.tools.smali).",
        }

    manual = _MANUAL_TOOLS.get(tool_name)
    if manual:
        return {"status": "manual_required", "message": manual}

    pip_pkg = _PIP_TOOLS.get(tool_name)
    if pip_pkg:
        return _pip_install(tool_name, pip_pkg)

    npm_pkg = _NPM_TOOLS.get(tool_name)
    if npm_pkg:
        if shutil.which("npm"):
            return _npm_install(tool_name, npm_pkg)
        return {"status": "error", "error": "npm not found. Install Node.js first."}

    return {
        "status": "error",
        "tool": tool_name,
        "error": f"No install recipe for '{tool_name}'.",
    }


def install_all_missing_tools() -> None:
    """Check all tools and install the missing ones."""
    from android_re_mcp.setup.check_tools import check_all_tools

    print("[*] Analyzing current environment...")
    tools = check_all_tools().get("tools", {})

    core_tools = [
        "apktool", "jadx", "uber-apk-signer", "il2cppdumper", "adb", "scrcpy",
        "frida", "frida-tools", "objection",
        "androguard", "apkid", "apkleaks", "quark-engine", "mitmproxy",
    ]

    for t in core_tools:
        if tools.get(t, {}).get("available", False):
            print(f"[+] Found: {t} (ready)")
            continue
        print(f"[-] Missing: {t}, installing...")
        res = install_tool(t)
        if res.get("status") == "ok":
            print(f"  [+] {res.get('message', 'Installed')}")
        else:
            err = res.get("error", res.get("message", "Unknown error"))
            print(f"  [!] {t}: {err}")
            if res.get("instructions"):
                print(f"      {res['instructions']}")
```

`python/tests/fixtures/build_notesdemo.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build tests/fixtures/notesdemo.apk from notesdemo/AndroidManifest.xml.
#
# The built APK is committed so the androguard regression tests run hermetically
# in CI (which has no Android SDK). It is our own 5 KB fixture — hence the
# explicit .gitignore exception for exactly this file; the repo-wide *.apk ban
# on committing third-party sample apps still stands. Rebuild it after editing
# the manifest and re-commit both together:
#
#     bash tests/fixtures/build_notesdemo.sh
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
AAPT2="${AAPT2:-$HOME/Android/Sdk/build-tools/34.0.0/aapt2}"
ANDROID_JAR="${ANDROID_JAR:-$HOME/Android/Sdk/platforms/android-36.1/android.jar}"
D8="${D8:-$HOME/Android/Sdk/build-tools/34.0.0/d8}"

TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Trivial classes.dex — the APK needs at least one dex because the Java tests
# drive AnalyzeAPK on it, not just the manifest.
mkdir -p "$TMP/gen/com/example/notes"
cat > "$TMP/gen/com/example/notes/Notes.java" <<'EOF'
package com.example.notes;
public final class Notes {
    public int id;
    public Notes() {}
}
EOF
mkdir -p "$TMP/classes"  # JDK 8 javac does not create -d itself
if ! javac --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    javac -source 8 -target 8 -d "$TMP/classes" "$TMP/gen/com/example/notes/Notes.java"  # JDK 8
else
    javac --release 8 -d "$TMP/classes" "$TMP/gen/com/example/notes/Notes.java"
fi
(cd "$TMP/classes" && "$D8" --release --min-api 21 --output "$TMP" com/example/notes/Notes.class)

# Binary XML manifest + resources, then attach classes.dex to the archive.
"$AAPT2" link --no-compile-sdk-metadata \
    -o "$TMP/notesdemo-stage.apk" -I "$ANDROID_JAR" \
    --manifest "$HERE/notesdemo/AndroidManifest.xml"
(cd "$TMP" && zip -j -q "$TMP/notesdemo-stage.apk" "$TMP/classes.dex")

cp "$TMP/notesdemo-stage.apk" "$HERE/notesdemo.apk"
echo "built $(ls -l "$HERE/notesdemo.apk" | awk '{print $5}') bytes"

```

```py
"""Regression tests for adb_ui_dump (extension E-PY-8).

Hermetic: a fake `adb` script on PATH answers `exec-out uiautomator
dump /dev/tty` with fixture XML, so no device is needed. The fallback
(two-step dump + cat) and the failure paths are covered the same way.
"""

import os
import stat
import subprocess  # noqa: F401 — re-imported through the fake sh shim
import textwrap

import pytest

from android_re_mcp.handlers import device as device_mod

UI_XML = textwrap.dedent("""\
    <?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8' standalone='yes' ?>
    <hierarchy rotation="0" layout-inst="7">
      <node index="0" text="" resource-id="" class="android.widget.FrameLayout"
            package="com.example.notes" content-desc="" checkable="false"
            clickable="false" scrollable="false" checked="false" enabled="true"
            bounds="[0,0][1080,2400]">
        <node index="0" text="Notes" resource-id="com.example.notes:id/title"
              class="android.widget.TextView" package="com.example.notes"
              content-desc="" clickable="false" bounds="[42,110][300,180]"
              enabled="true"/>
        <node index="1" text="" resource-id="com.example.notes:id/fab"
              class="android.widget.Button" package="com.example.notes"
              content-desc="Add note" clickable="true"
              bounds="[900,2200][1050,2350]" enabled="true"/>
        <node index="2" text="" resource-id="" class="android.widget.ScrollView"
              package="com.example.notes" content-desc="" scrollable="true"
              clickable="false" bounds="[0,200][1080,2100]" enabled="true"/>
      </node>
    </hierarchy>
""")

NOT_XML = "UI hierchary dumped to: /sdcard/window_dump.xml\nERROR: could not get idle state.\n"


@pytest.fixture()
def fake_adb_factory(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """Create a fake adb that answers with a caller-chosen script body."""

    def install(script_body: str) -> str:
        bin_dir = tmp_path / f"bin-{len(list(tmp_path.iterdir()))}"
        bin_dir.mkdir()
        adb = bin_dir / "adb"
        adb.write_text("#!/bin/sh\n" + script_body)
        adb.chmod(adb.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC)
        # Prepend, don't replace: the fake adb's own helpers (cat, echo)
        # still need to resolve.
        monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", f"{bin_dir}:{os.environ['PATH']}")
        return str(adb)

    return install


def test_ui_dump_parses_elements(fake_adb_factory):
    fake_adb_factory(f"cat <<'XMLEOF'\n{UI_XML}XMLEOF\n")
    result = device_mod.DeviceHandler().adb_ui_dump({})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    out = result["output"]
    assert out["package"] == "com.example.notes"
    assert out["element_count"] == 3
    by_label = {el.get("text") or el.get("desc"): el for el in out["elements"]}
    fab = by_label["Add note"]
    assert fab["class"] == "Button"
    assert fab["clickable"] == "true"
    assert fab["bounds"] == "[900,2200][1050,2350]"
    title = by_label["Notes"]
    assert title["class"] == "TextView"
    assert title["id"] == "com.example.notes:id/title"
    report = out["report"]
    assert '"Add note"' in report and "[clickable]" in report
    # Plain containers (no text/click/scroll) are excluded from the list.
    assert "FrameLayout" not in report


def test_ui_dump_falls_back_to_two_step_when_tty_refused(fake_adb_factory):
    """/dev/tty unsupported → dump to file + cat is used automatically."""
    fake_adb_factory(
        "if [ \"$1\" = \"exec-out\" ]; then echo 'ERROR: unsupported'; exit 1; "
        "else cat <<'XMLEOF'\n" + UI_XML + "XMLEOF\nfi\n"
    )
    result = device_mod.DeviceHandler().adb_ui_dump({})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    assert result["output"]["package"] == "com.example.notes"


def test_ui_dump_reports_a_total_failure(fake_adb_factory):
    fake_adb_factory("echo 'ERROR: could not get idle state.' >&2; exit 1\n")
    result = device_mod.DeviceHandler().adb_ui_dump({})
    assert result["status"] == "error"
    assert "no XML" in result["error"]


def test_ui_dump_survives_malformed_xml(fake_adb_factory):
    fake_adb_factory("echo '<?xml version=\"1.0\"?><hierarchy><node>'\n")
    result = device_mod.DeviceHandler().adb_ui_dump({})
    assert result["status"] == "error"
    assert "parse error" in result["error"]


def test_ui_dump_missing_adb(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", str(tmp_path))  # no adb anywhere
    result = device_mod.DeviceHandler().adb_ui_dump({})
    assert result["status"] == "missing_tool"
```

`python/tests/test_androguard_tools.py`:

```py
"""Regression tests for the androguard 4.x handlers (finding F-PY-1).

The integration tests run against tests/fixtures/notesdemo.apk; the xref
shape tests substitute fakes for _analyze_apk so all androguard call-graph
record shapes (3.x objects, 2-tuples, 4.x 3-tuples) are covered without
needing bytecode that exercises each one.
"""

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from android_re_mcp.handlers import static as static_mod

pytest.importorskip("androguard")

FIXTURE = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "notesdemo.apk"


# ── Fake objects covering the call-graph record shapes ────────────────────

class _Named:
    """4.x shape participant: exposes only .name."""

    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name


class _MethodObject:
    """3.x shape: method-analysis object with .class_name and .name."""

    def __init__(self, class_name, name):
        self.class_name = class_name
        self.name = name


class _FakeMethod:
    def __init__(self, name, xref_from=(), xref_to=()):
        self.name = name
        self._from = tuple(xref_from)
        self._to = tuple(xref_to)

    def get_xref_from(self):
        return self._from

    def get_xref_to(self):
        return self._to


class _FakeClass:
    def __init__(self, name, methods):
        self.name = name
        self._methods = methods

    def get_methods(self):
        return list(self._methods)


class _FakeDx:
    def __init__(self, classes):
        self._classes = list(classes)

    def get_classes(self):
        return list(self._classes)


def _stub_analysis(*classes):
    """Return a _analyze_apk replacement serving the given classes."""

    def _analyze(apk_path):
        assert Path(apk_path).exists()  # handlers check existence before analysis
        return (None, None, _FakeDx(classes))

    return _analyze


# ── manifest_parse (integration, real fixture) ────────────────────────────

def test_manifest_parse_fixture_fields():
    out = static_mod.StaticHandler().manifest_parse({"apk_path": str(FIXTURE)})
    assert out["status"] == "ok", out.get("error")
    o = out["output"]
    assert o["package_name"] == "com.example.notes"
    assert o["version_name"] == "2.3.1"
    assert o["version_code"] == "23"
    assert o["min_sdk"] == 21
    assert o["target_sdk"] == 28
    assert o["debuggable"] is True
    assert o["allow_backup"] is True
    assert o["network_security_config"] is None


def test_manifest_parse_dangerous_permissions():

def test_manifest_parse_categorization_with_reasons():
    out = static_mod.StaticHandler().manifest_parse({
        "apk_path": str(FIXTURE), "categorize_permissions": True,
    })
    cat = out["output"]["permission_categorization"]
    assert cat["total"] == len(out["output"]["permissions"])
    assert (cat["dangerous_count"], cat["normal_count"]) == (4, 1)

    reasons = {d["permission"]: d["reason"] for d in cat["dangerous"]}
    assert set(reasons) == {
        "android.permission.CAMERA",
        "android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION",
        "android.permission.READ_CONTACTS",
        "android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE",
    }
    assert reasons["android.permission.CAMERA"] == (
        "microphone/camera access allows covert recording"
    )
    assert reasons["android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION"] == (
        "location access enables user tracking"
    )
    assert cat["normal"] == ["android.permission.INTERNET"]
    # npm risk-summary lines, triggered by the same substrings npm uses
    assert "Location permissions enable user tracking." in cat["risk_summary"]
    assert "Microphone/Camera permissions allow covert recording." in cat["risk_summary"]
    assert not any("SMS" in line for line in cat["risk_summary"])

# ── apk_analyze_full aggregation (no masked failures) ──────────────────────

@pytest.fixture()
def patched_children(monkeypatch):
    def patch(manifest, apkid=None, secrets=None, quark=None):
        monkeypatch.setattr(
            static_mod.StaticHandler, "manifest_parse",
            lambda self, args: manifest,
        )
        monkeypatch.setattr(
            static_mod.StaticHandler, "apk_identify",
            lambda self, args: apkid or {"status": "ok", "output": {}},
        )
        monkeypatch.setattr(
            static_mod.StaticHandler, "apk_scan_secrets",
            lambda self, args: secrets
            or {"status": "ok", "output": {"findings": {"URLs": ["https://x.example"]}}},
        )
        monkeypatch.setattr(
            static_mod.StaticHandler, "quark_scan",
            lambda self, args: quark
            or {"status": "missing_tool", "tool": "quark_scan",
                "error": "quark-engine is not installed in this Python environment.",
                "hint": "install quark-engine"},
        )

    return patch


def test_apk_analyze_full_all_ok(patched_children):
    patched_children(
        manifest={"status": "ok", "output": {"package_name": "p"}},
        quark={"status": "ok", "output": {"matches": [], "report": "=== Quark Behaviour Scan ==="}},
    )
    out = static_mod.StaticHandler().apk_analyze_full({"apk_path": str(FIXTURE)})
    assert out["status"] == "ok"
    o = out["output"]
    assert o["manifest"] == {"package_name": "p"}
    assert o["tool_statuses"] == {"apkid": "ok", "apkleaks": "ok", "manifest": "ok", "quark": "ok"}
    assert "errors" not in out
    assert out["output"]["framework"]
    assert out["output"]["protection_tier"]


def test_apk_analyze_full_reports_partial_failure(patched_children):
    patched_children(
        manifest={"status": "error", "tool": "androguard", "error": "boom"},
    )
    out = static_mod.StaticHandler().apk_analyze_full({"apk_path": str(FIXTURE)})
    assert out["status"] == "degraded"  # not the old masked "ok"
    o = out["output"]
    assert o["manifest"] == {}
    assert o["tool_statuses"]["manifest"] == "error"
    assert o["errors"]["manifest"] == "boom"
    assert "manifest: boom" in out["error"]
    assert "1 hardcoded secret(s)" in o["top_findings"]


def test_apk_analyze_full_error_when_everything_fails(patched_children):
    sentinel = {"status": "error", "error": "down"}
    patched_children(
        manifest=sentinel,
        apkid={"status": "missing_tool", "error": "no apkid"},
        secrets={"status": "missing_tool", "error": "no apkleaks"},
        quark={"status": "missing_tool", "error": "no quark"},
    )
    out = static_mod.StaticHandler().apk_analyze_full({"apk_path": str(FIXTURE)})
    assert out["status"] == "error"
    # Optional (missing_tool) stages stay out of the error map; their
    # absence is recorded in tool_statuses only.
    assert set(out["output"]["errors"]) == {"manifest"}
    assert out["output"]["tool_statuses"] == {
        "apkid": "missing_tool",
        "apkleaks": "missing_tool",
        "manifest": "error",
        "quark": "missing_tool",
    }
    assert out["output"]["protection_tier"] == "none"


def test_apk_analyze_full_reports_missing_file():
    out = static_mod.StaticHandler().apk_analyze_full({"apk_path": "/nowhere/app.apk"})
    assert out["status"] == "error"
    assert "not found" in out["error"]
```

`python/tests/test_api_extractor.py`:

```py
"""Hermetic tests for android_api_extractor (PyPI port of the npm tool, E-PY-11).

The smali fixtures mirror what apktool emits for Retrofit interfaces:
runtime annotation blocks under Lretrofit2/http/ plus OkHttp3 field
declarations. The apktool-decompile path is exercised live (real APK
smoke); these tests point the tool at an existing smali_dir.
"""

from pathlib import Path

from android_re_mcp.handlers.apiextractor import ApiExtractorHandler

RETROFIT_SMALI = """.class public interface Lcom/example/Api;
.super Ljava/lang/Object;
.source "Api.java"

# direct methods
.method public constructor <init>()V
    return-void
.end method

.annotation runtime Lretrofit2/http/GET;
    value = "v1/users/{id}"
.end annotation

.method public abstract getUser(Ljava/lang/String;)Lio/reactivex/Observable;
    .annotation system Lretrofit2/Callback;
    .end annotation
.end method

.annotation runtime Lretrofit2/http/POST;
    value = "v1/users"
.end annotation

.field private static final OKCLIENT:Lokhttp3/OkHttpClient;
.field public client:Lokhttp3/OkHttpClient;
"""


def _smali_tree(tmp_path: Path, content: str = RETROFIT_SMALI) -> str:
    root = tmp_path / "smali"
    (root / "com/example").mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "com/example/Api.smali").write_text(content)
    (root / "smali_dir_marker.txt").write_text("not smali")
    return str(root)


URLS_SMALI = """.class public Lcom/example/Net;
.super Ljava/lang/Object;

.method public constructor <init>()V
    const-string v0, "https://api.example.com/v1/login"
    const-string v1, "https://api.example.com/v1/users"
    const-string v2, "https://api.example.com/v1/login"
    const-string v3, "http://cdn.example.net/assets/app.png"
    const-string v4, "AES/GCM/NoPadding"
    const-string/jumbo v5, "https://ws.example.org/socket"
    const-string v6, "https://escaped.example.com/path\\"tail"
    return-void
.end method
"""


def _write_smali(tmp_path: Path, name: str, content: str) -> str:
    root = tmp_path / "smali"
    (root / "com/example").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (root / f"com/example/{name}").write_text(content)
    return str(root)


def test_const_string_urls_harvested_deduped_and_host_grouped(tmp_path):
    root = _write_smali(tmp_path, "Net.smali", URLS_SMALI)
    # duplicate URL in a second file must not be double-counted
    _write_smali(tmp_path, "Net2.smali", 'const-string v0, "https://api.example.com/v1/login"\n')
    result = ApiExtractorHandler().android_api_extractor({"smali_dir": root})
    out = result["output"]
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    assert out["annotation_count"] == 0
    assert out["okhttp3_field_count"] == 0
    cs = out["const_string_urls"]
    assert cs["total"] == 5  # login/users/cdn/ws/escaped — the dup and AES/GCM are dropped
    assert cs["truncated"] is False
    assert cs["shown"] == cs["total"]
    assert cs["oversized_skipped"] == 0
    hosts = cs["by_host"]
    assert list(hosts) == sorted(hosts)  # host-grouped, sorted
    assert hosts["api.example.com"] == [
        "https://api.example.com/v1/login",
        "https://api.example.com/v1/users",
    ]
    assert hosts["cdn.example.net"] == ["http://cdn.example.net/assets/app.png"]
    assert hosts["ws.example.org"] == ["https://ws.example.org/socket"]  # const-string/jumbo
    assert hosts["escaped.example.com"] == ["https://escaped.example.com/path"]


def test_const_string_urls_cap_truncates_deterministically(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from android_re_mcp.handlers import apiextractor as mod

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "_MAX_CONST_URLS", 3)
    root = _write_smali(tmp_path, "Net.smali", URLS_SMALI)
    out = ApiExtractorHandler().android_api_extractor({"smali_dir": root})["output"]
    cs = out["const_string_urls"]
    assert cs["total"] == 5
    assert cs["shown"] == 3
    assert cs["truncated"] is True
    # sorted hosts first: api.example.com (2) then cdn.example.net (1) fill the cap
    assert list(cs["by_host"]) == ["api.example.com", "cdn.example.net"]
    assert "escaped.example.com" not in cs["by_host"]


def test_const_string_urls_oversized_constants_are_skipped_and_counted(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from android_re_mcp.handlers import apiextractor as mod

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "_MAX_URL_LEN", 64)
    smali = (
        '.class public LX;\n'
        'const-string v0, "https://ok.example.com/a"\n'
        f'const-string v1, "https://blob.example.com/{"a" * 200}"\n'
    )
    root = _write_smali(tmp_path, "Net.smali", smali)
    cs = ApiExtractorHandler().android_api_extractor({"smali_dir": root})["output"]["const_string_urls"]
    assert cs["total"] == 1
    assert cs["oversized_skipped"] == 1
    assert "blob.example.com" not in cs["by_host"]


def test_postman_mode_has_no_harvest_section(tmp_path):
```

`python/tests/test_apk_diff.py`:

```py
"""Hermetic tests for apk_diff (PyPI port of the npm E-NPM-4 tool, E-PY-10).

The two zips here carry a plain-text stub manifest, which androguard
cannot parse — so the manifest section is expected to report
``manifest_read: false``; everything else (native libs, secrets,
inventory) is fully checked. The manifest path itself is exercised with
injected facts and live via the real-APK smoke.
"""

import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from android_re_mcp.handlers import apkdiff as apkdiff_mod

# Built by concatenation at runtime so repo scanners don't flag the test
# file itself (same pattern as the existing secret-fixture tests).
FAKE_AWS_KEY = "AKIA" + "IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE"  # AKIA + 16 chars, matches the pattern
FAKE_GOOGLE_KEY = "AIza" + "SyA1bC2dE3fG4hI5jK6lM7nO8pQ9rStUvWxyz"  # AIza + 35 chars

STUB_MANIFEST = b"not a real AXML manifest"


def _write_apk(tmp_path: Path, name: str, files: dict[str, bytes]) -> str:
    apk_path = tmp_path / name
    with zipfile.ZipFile(apk_path, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for fname, data in files.items():
            zf.writestr(fname, data)
    return str(apk_path)


def _old_build(tmp_path: Path) -> str:
    return _write_apk(tmp_path, "old.apk", {
        "AndroidManifest.xml": STUB_MANIFEST,
        "classes.dex": b"old dex",
        "lib/arm64-v8a/libnative.so": b"version-one-bytes",
        "assets/config.json": f'{{"k": "{FAKE_AWS_KEY}"}}'.encode(),
    })


def _new_build(tmp_path: Path) -> str:
    return _write_apk(tmp_path, "new.apk", {
        "AndroidManifest.xml": STUB_MANIFEST,
        "classes.dex": b"new dex bytes are longer",
        "lib/arm64-v8a/libnative.so": b"version-two-bytes!!",
        "lib/armeabi-v7a/libextra.so": b"brand new lib",
        "assets/config.json": f'{{"k": "{FAKE_GOOGLE_KEY}"}}'.encode(),
    })


def test_deltas_native_libs_secrets_inventory(tmp_path):
    result = apkdiff_mod.ApkDiffHandler().apk_diff({
        "old_path": _old_build(tmp_path),
        "new_path": _new_build(tmp_path),
    })
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    out = result["output"]

    # stub manifest is not AXML → honest degradation, with the reason
    assert out["manifest_read"] is False
    assert "AndroidManifest.xml" in out["manifest_error"]

    nl = out["native_libraries"]
    assert (nl["old_count"], nl["new_count"]) == (1, 2)
    assert "arm64-v8a/libnative.so" in nl["changed"]
    assert "armeabi-v7a/libextra.so" in nl["added"]
    assert nl["all_identical"] is False

    sec = out["secrets"]
    assert sec["mode"] == "scanned"
    assert {e["pattern"] for e in sec["new_only"]} == {"Google API Key"}
    assert {e["pattern"] for e in sec["old_only"]} == {"AWS Access Key ID"}
    assert sec["changed"] == []
    assert sec["new_only"][0]["risk"] == "HIGH"
    assert sec["old_only"][0]["risk"] == "CRITICAL"

    arch = out["archive"]
    assert (arch["old_entries"], arch["new_entries"]) == (4, 5)
    assert (arch["added"], arch["removed"], arch["changed_size"]) == (1, 0, 3)

    assert out["secrets"] == {"mode": "skipped"}

def test_manifest_delta_rendering(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """The identity/flags/permission/exported sections over injected facts."""
    old = _write_apk(tmp_path, "m_old.apk", {"AndroidManifest.xml": STUB_MANIFEST, "classes.dex": b"x"})
    new = _write_apk(tmp_path, "m_new.apk", {"AndroidManifest.xml": STUB_MANIFEST, "classes.dex": b"y"})

    facts_old = {
        "package": "com.example.app", "version_name": "1.0", "version_code": "1",
        "min_sdk": "21", "target_sdk": "30",
        "debuggable": False, "allow_backup": True, "cleartext": False,
        "permissions": ["android.permission.INTERNET"],
        "exported_components": ["com.example.app.MainActivity (activity)"],
    }
    facts_new = {
        "package": "com.example.app", "version_name": "1.1", "version_code": "2",
        "min_sdk": "21", "target_sdk": "31",
        "debuggable": True, "allow_backup": True, "cleartext": True,
        "permissions": ["android.permission.CAMERA", "android.permission.INTERNET"],
        "exported_components": ["com.example.app.Svc (service)"],
    }
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        apkdiff_mod, "_manifest_facts", lambda p: facts_old if p == old else facts_new
    )

    result = apkdiff_mod.ApkDiffHandler().apk_diff({"old_path": old, "new_path": new})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    out = result["output"]
    assert out["manifest_read"] is True

    by_field = {row["field"]: row for row in out["identity"]}
    assert by_field["package"]["changed"] is False
    assert by_field["version_name"]["changed"] is True
    assert (by_field["version_name"]["old"], by_field["version_name"]["new"]) == ("1.0", "1.1")
    assert (by_field["version_code"]["old"], by_field["version_code"]["new"]) == ("1", "2")
    assert by_field["min_sdk"]["changed"] is False
    assert by_field["target_sdk"]["changed"] is True

    flags = {f["flag"]: f for f in out["flags_changed"]}
    assert set(flags) == {"debuggable", "usesCleartextTraffic"}
    assert flags["debuggable"]["new"] is True

    assert out["permissions"]["added"] == ["android.permission.CAMERA"]
    assert out["permissions"]["removed"] == []
    assert out["exported_components"]["removed"] == ["com.example.app.MainActivity (activity)"]
    assert out["exported_components"]["added"] == ["com.example.app.Svc (service)"]

def test_entry_cap_skips_oversized_entries(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """A declared-oversize lib entry is skipped with a note, not a crash."""
    real = apkdiff_mod._env_max_mb
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        apkdiff_mod, "_env_max_mb",
        lambda name, fallback: 1 if name == "ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_ENTRY_MB" else real(name, fallback),
    )  # 1 MB per-entry cap, file cap untouched
    huge = b"x" * (2 * 1024 * 1024)  # 2 MB entry > 1 MB cap
    old = _write_apk(tmp_path, "cap_old.apk", {
        "lib/arm64-v8a/libhuge.so": huge,
        "classes.dex": b"same dex",
    })
    new = _write_apk(tmp_path, "cap_new.apk", {
        "lib/arm64-v8a/libhuge.so": huge,
        "classes.dex": b"same dex",
    })
    result = apkdiff_mod.ApkDiffHandler().apk_diff({
        "old_path": old, "new_path": new, "skip_secrets": True,
    })
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    nl = result["output"]["native_libraries"]
    # both entries unreadable → hash None on both sides → reported unchanged,
    # and the skip is visible in the archive notes
    assert nl["old_count"] == 1 and nl["all_identical"] is True
    notes = result["output"]["archive"]["notes"]
    assert any("above the per-entry cap" in n for n in notes)
```

`python/tests/test_check_tools_honesty.py`:

```py
"""Regression tests for the check_tools honesty pass (finding F-PY-2).

Every entry must be probed exactly the way its consumer invokes it: pip
CLIs as executables (not importable modules), 'medusa' disambiguated from
the foofus.net SSH cracker, and resolution shared with the handlers via
android_re_mcp.clitools.find_cli.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import stat
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from android_re_mcp import clitools
from android_re_mcp.handlers import static as static_mod
from android_re_mcp.setup import check_tools as ct


def _spy_sh(name: str, body: str) -> None:
    """Write an executable *name* shell script into the current directory."""
    script = Path(name)
    script.write_text("#!/bin/sh\n" + body + "\n")
    script.chmod(script.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH)


def test_find_cli_prefers_path_hit(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    fake = tmp_path / "mytool"
    fake.write_text("#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n")
    fake.chmod(0o755)
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", str(tmp_path))
    assert clitools.find_cli("mytool") == str(fake)


def test_find_cli_falls_back_to_interpreter_sibling(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", str(tmp_path / "empty"))  # nothing on PATH
    (tmp_path / "empty").mkdir()
    sibling = tmp_path / "bin" / "mytool"
    bin_dir = tmp_path / "bin"
    bin_dir.mkdir()
    sibling.write_text("#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n")
    sibling.chmod(0o755)
    fake_python = bin_dir / "python3"
    fake_python.write_text("")  # sibling dir is derived from sys.executable
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "executable", str(fake_python))
    assert clitools.find_cli("mytool") == str(sibling)


def test_find_cli_requires_exec_bit(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    sibling = tmp_path / "bin" / "mytool"
    sibling.parent.mkdir()
    sibling.write_text("#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n")  # not executable
    fake_python = tmp_path / "bin" / "python3"
    fake_python.write_text("")
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", str(tmp_path / "nope"))
    (tmp_path / "nope").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "executable", str(fake_python))
    assert clitools.find_cli("mytool") is None


def test_find_cli_survives_symlinked_interpreter(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Venv pythons are symlinks; the parent dir must NOT be the target's.

    Regression: Path(sys.executable).resolve() once pointed find_cli at the
    *base* interpreter's directory, so venv console scripts were invisible.
    """
    venv_bin = tmp_path / "venv" / "bin"
    venv_bin.mkdir(parents=True)
    tool = venv_bin / "mytool"
    tool.write_text("#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n")
    tool.chmod(0o755)
    base_python = tmp_path / "base" / "python3.13"
    base_python.parent.mkdir()
    base_python.write_text("")
    os.symlink(base_python, venv_bin / "python3")
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", str(tmp_path / "empty"))
    (tmp_path / "empty").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "executable", str(venv_bin / "python3"))
    assert clitools.find_cli("mytool") == str(tool)


def test_check_tools_reports_pip_cli_not_module(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """apkleaks is invoked as a CLI: a module-only install must NOT count."""
    _spy_sh(tmp_path / "apkleaks", "echo 'apkleaks 2.6.3'")
    _spy_sh(tmp_path / "apkid", "echo 'apkid 3.2.0'")
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", str(tmp_path))
    tools = ct.check_all_tools()["tools"]
    assert tools["apkleaks"]["available"] is True
    assert tools["apkleaks"]["path"] == str(tmp_path / "apkleaks")
    assert tools["apkid"]["available"] is True
    assert tools["apkleaks"]["used_by"] == ["apk_scan_secrets", "apk_analyze_full"]


def test_check_tools_marks_module_only_pip_tool_missing(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
```

`python/tests/test_concurrency.py`:

```py
"""Concurrency regression tests for the F-PY-4 non-blocking dispatch.

_run_tool must free the event loop while a slow sync handler runs, and
must queue concurrent calls to stateful handler classes instead of
letting them race on shared state.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import time

import pytest

from android_re_mcp.handlers.device import DeviceHandler
from android_re_mcp.handlers.dynamic import DynamicHandler
from android_re_mcp.handlers.network import NetworkHandler
from android_re_mcp.server import _run_tool
from mcp.types import CallToolResult

pytest.importorskip("mcp")


class _StatefulHandler:
    """Stands in for Dynamic/Network/Device: holds nominally shared state."""

    _SERIALIZE = True

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.log: list[tuple[float, float]] = []

    def work(self, args: dict) -> dict:
        start = time.monotonic()
        time.sleep(args["sleep"])
        self.log.append((start, time.monotonic()))
        return {"status": "ok"}


class _SlowHandler:
    """Stateless: two methods — one slow, one instant."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.done: list[tuple[str, float]] = []

    def slow(self, args: dict) -> dict:
        time.sleep(args["sleep"])
        self.done.append(("slow", time.monotonic()))
        return {"status": "ok", "who": "slow"}

    def fast(self, args: dict) -> dict:
        self.done.append(("fast", time.monotonic()))
        return {"status": "ok", "who": "fast"}


def _result(res: CallToolResult) -> dict:
    import json

    return json.loads(res.content[0].text)


def test_stateless_slow_handler_does_not_block_the_loop():
    """A slow sync handler must not stall the loop (F-PY-4).

    'slow' is scheduled FIRST: inline dispatch would block the loop for
    its whole run, so 'fast' could only finish after it. Under to_thread
    the loop stays free and 'fast' completes while 'slow' still sleeps.
    """
    slow = _SlowHandler()
    dispatch = {"slow": slow.slow, "fast": slow.fast}
    pools = {}

    async def go():
        slow_task = asyncio.create_task(_run_tool("slow", {"sleep": 0.3}, dispatch, pools))
        fast_task = asyncio.create_task(_run_tool("fast", {}, dispatch, pools))
        return await asyncio.gather(slow_task, fast_task)

    slow_res, fast_res = asyncio.run(go())
    marks = {who: t for who, t in slow.done}
    assert [who for who, _t in slow.done] == ["fast", "slow"]
    assert marks["fast"] < marks["slow"], marks
    assert _result(slow_res)["who"] == "slow"
    assert _result(fast_res)["who"] == "fast"


def test_stateful_handlers_never_overlap():
    stateful = _StatefulHandler()
    dispatch = {"a": stateful.work, "b": stateful.work}
    pools = {}

    async def go():
        return await asyncio.gather(
            _run_tool("a", {"sleep": 0.25}, dispatch, pools),
            _run_tool("b", {"sleep": 0.25}, dispatch, pools),
        )

    asyncio.run(go())
    intervals = sorted(stateful.log)
    assert len(intervals) == 2
    # queueing, not racing: later start is not before earlier end
    assert intervals[1][0] >= intervals[0][1] - 0.05


def test_stateful_flag_is_set_on_the_stateful_classes_and_lambdas_are_free():
    # Semantics flags (the wiring _run_tool keys on)
    assert DynamicHandler._SERIALIZE is True
    assert NetworkHandler._SERIALIZE is True
    assert DeviceHandler._SERIALIZE is True
    # plain function/lambda dispatches have no bound _SERIALIZE
    assert getattr(lambda _a: {}, "_SERIALIZE", False) is False


def test_unknown_tool_and_guard_paths_look_the_same():
    dispatch = {"echo": lambda args: {"status": "ok"}}
    res = asyncio.run(_run_tool("nope", {}, dispatch, {}))
    assert res.isError is False  # 'Unknown tool' is a normal result, not protocol error
    assert _result(res)["status"] == "error"

    # guard refusal (install_tool is off by default) → isError + structured body
    res = asyncio.run(_run_tool("install_tool", {"tool_name": "jadx"}, {"echo": lambda a: {}}, {}))
    assert res.isError is True
    assert "refused" in _result(res)["error"]


def test_handler_exception_is_reported_not_raised():
    def boom(args: dict) -> dict:
        raise RuntimeError("kaboom")

    res = asyncio.run(_run_tool("boom", {}, {"boom": boom}, {}))
    assert res.isError is False
    assert _result(res) == {"status": "error", "tool": "boom", "error": "kaboom"}

```

`python/tests/test_decompile_fallback.py`:

```py
"""Hermetic tests for the apk_decompile_java apktool fallback (jadx unavailable).

The contract: when jadx is missing the call still succeeds via apktool,
flagged honestly (engine + fallback + note); when both are missing it is
a missing_tool; jadx errors pass through unchanged.
"""

from android_re_mcp.handlers import static as static_mod
from android_re_mcp.handlers.static import StaticHandler


class _Proc:
    def __init__(self, returncode=0, stdout="", stderr=""):
        self.returncode = returncode
        self.stdout = stdout
        self.stderr = stderr


def _check(name: str, jadx: bool, apktool: bool):
    def fake(tool):
        return {"jadx": jadx, "apktool": apktool}.get(tool, False)

    return fake


def test_jadx_available_uses_jadx(monkeypatch):
    seen = {}

    def fake_run(cmd, **_k):
        seen["cmd"] = cmd
        return _Proc(0, stdout="jadx ok")

    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod, "_check_tool", _check(None, jadx=True, apktool=True))
    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod.subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    result = StaticHandler().apk_decompile_java({"apk_path": "/x/notes.apk"})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    assert result["tool"] == "jadx"
    assert result["output"]["engine"] == "jadx"
    assert result["output"]["out_dir"] == "/x/notes_jadx"
    assert seen["cmd"][0] == "jadx"


def test_jadx_missing_falls_back_to_apktool(monkeypatch):
    seen = {}

    def fake_run(cmd, **_k):
        seen["cmd"] = cmd
        return _Proc(0, stdout="apktool ok")

    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod, "_check_tool", _check(None, jadx=False, apktool=True))
    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod.subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    result = StaticHandler().apk_decompile_java({"apk_path": "/x/notes.apk"})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    assert result["tool"] == "apk_decompile_java"
    assert result["output"]["engine"] == "apktool (jadx unavailable)"
    assert result["output"]["fallback"] is True
    assert "smali" in result["output"]["note"]
    assert "--setup" in result["output"]["note"]
    assert result["output"]["out_dir"] == "/x/notes_apktool"
    assert seen["cmd"][0] == "apktool"  # mode defaults to full (smali + resources)


def test_both_missing_is_missing_tool(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod, "_check_tool", _check(None, jadx=False, apktool=False))
    result = StaticHandler().apk_decompile_java({"apk_path": "/x/notes.apk"})
    assert result["status"] == "missing_tool"
    assert "neither jadx nor apktool" in result["error"]
    assert "--setup" in result["hint"]


def test_apktool_failure_passes_through(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod, "_check_tool", _check(None, jadx=False, apktool=True))
    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod.subprocess, "run", lambda *a, **k: _Proc(1, stderr="apktool boom"))
    result = StaticHandler().apk_decompile_java({"apk_path": "/x/notes.apk"})
    assert result["status"] == "error"
    assert "apktool boom" in result["error"]


def test_jadx_failure_does_not_fall_back(monkeypatch):
    # jadx present but broken is a jadx problem — honest error, no silent engine swap
    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod, "_check_tool", _check(None, jadx=True, apktool=True))
    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod.subprocess, "run", lambda *a, **k: _Proc(1, stderr="jadx boom"))
    result = StaticHandler().apk_decompile_java({"apk_path": "/x/notes.apk"})
    assert result["status"] == "error"
    assert result["tool"] == "jadx"
    assert "jadx boom" in result["error"]
```
